sentences.zh: 列傳第七十一文苑

translations.literal: Biography 71: The Literary Grove
translations.idiomatic: Biography 71: Men of Letters

sentences.zh: 溫子升荀濟祖鴻勳李廣樊遜荀士遜王褒庾信顏之推弟之儀虞世基柳許善心李文博明克讓劉臻諸葛潁王貞虞綽王胄庾自直潘徽常德志尹式劉善經祖君彥孔德紹劉斌

translations.literal: Wen Zisheng, Xun Ji, Zu Hongxun, Li Guang, Fan Xun, Xun Shisun, Wang Bao, Yu Xin, Yan Zhitui, younger brother Zhiyi, Yu Shiji, Liu Guyan, Xu Shanxin, Li Wenbo, Ming Kerang, Liu Zhen, Zhuge Ying, Wang Zhen, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, Yu Zizhi, Pan Hui, Chang Dezhi, Yin Shi, Liu Shanqing, Zu Junyan, Kong Deshao, Liu Bin
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zisheng, Xun Ji, Zu Hongxun, Li Guang, Fan Xun, Xun Shisun, Wang Bao, Yu Xin, Yan Zhitui, his younger brother Zhiyi, Yu Shiji, Liu Guyan, Xu Shanxin, Li Wenbo, Ming Kerang, Liu Zhen, Zhuge Ying, Wang Zhen, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, Yu Zizhi, Pan Hui, Chang Dezhi, Yin Shi, Liu Shanqing, Zu Junyan, Kong Deshao, and Liu Bin

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「觀乎天文，以察時變；

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "Look to the patterns of Heaven to discern how the seasons shift;

sentences.zh: 觀乎人文，以化成天下。」

translations.literal: observe the patterns of culture to transform and complete the world."
translations.idiomatic: look to the patterns of human culture to civilize and perfect the world."

sentences.zh: 然則文之為用其大矣哉！

translations.literal: Thus the function of writing—how great it is!
translations.idiomatic: How vast, then, is the office of literature!

sentences.zh: 逖聽三古，彌綸百代，若乃《墳》、《素》所紀，靡得而雲；

translations.literal: Listening distantly across the three antiquities, spanning a hundred generations—as for what the Fen and Su record, none can speak of it;
translations.idiomatic: Listening back through the three antiquities and spanning a hundred generations, what the Fen and Su annals record cannot even be put into words;

sentences.zh: 《典》、《謨》已降，遺風可述。

translations.literal: from the Canon and Counsels downward, surviving styles can be recounted.
translations.idiomatic: but from the Canon and Counsels onward, surviving traditions may still be told.

sentences.zh: 至於制禮作樂，騰實飛聲，善乎。

translations.literal: As for instituting rites and composing music, making substance soar and reputation fly—excellent indeed.
translations.idiomatic: When it comes to establishing rites and composing music, giving substance wings and sending fame aloft—how fine that is.

sentences.zh: 言之不文，行之豈能遠也。

translations.literal: If speech is not refined, how can conduct reach far?
translations.idiomatic: If words lack polish, how can deeds travel far?

sentences.zh: 是以曲阜之多才多藝，監二代以正其源；

translations.literal: Therefore the man of many talents and many arts at Qufu, overseeing the two dynasties to rectify the source;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the master of manifold gifts at Qufu, surveying the two dynasties to set the source aright;

sentences.zh: 闕里之性與天道，修《六經》以維其末。

translations.literal: he whose nature accorded with the Way of Heaven in Que Li, editing the Six Classics to sustain the branch ends.
translations.idiomatic: he whose nature was one with Heaven's Way in Que Li, editing the Six Classics to secure what lay downstream.

sentences.zh: 用能窮神知化，稱首於千古；

translations.literal: By this he could exhaust the spirit and know transformation, standing first through a thousand ages;
translations.idiomatic: By this he plumbed the spirit and grasped transformation, standing foremost through the ages;

sentences.zh: 經邦緯俗，藏用於百代。

translations.literal: ordering the state and weaving custom, storing his use for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: ordering the realm and weaving the customs, his influence stored away for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 至哉，斯固聖人之述作也。

translations.literal: Supreme indeed—this is truly the sage's literary creation.
translations.idiomatic: Supreme indeed—such is the literary work of the sage.

sentences.zh: 逮乎兩周道喪，七十義乖。

translations.literal: When it reached the two Zhou dynasties the Way was lost, and the seventy disciples' meanings diverged.
translations.idiomatic: By the time of the Eastern and Western Zhou the Way had waned, and the meanings of the seventy disciples had fallen out of accord.

sentences.zh: 淹中、稷下，八儒、三墨之異，漆園、黍穀，名、法、兵、農之別，雖雅誥奧義，或未盡善，考其遺跡，亦賢達之流乎。

translations.literal: At Yanzhong and Jixia were the differences of the eight Ru and three Mo; in the Lacquer Garden and Millet Valley were the divisions of the School of Names, Legalists, Militarists, and Agriculturists—though their elegant pronouncements and profound meanings were not always perfect, examining their traces, were they not also streams of worthy and eminent men?
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhong and Jixia the eight Ru schools and three Mo lines contended; in the Lacquer Garden and Millet Valley the schools of Names, Law, War, and Agriculture parted ways. Though their elegant edicts and abstruse doctrines were not always flawless, judged by what they left behind, were they not men of talent and distinction as well?

sentences.zh: 其離讒放逐之臣，塗窮後門之士，道晳感軻而未遇，志鬱抑而不申。

translations.literal: Those ministers slandered and exiled, gentlemen whose path ended at the back gate, men like Dao Xi who was moved by Ke yet went unmet, whose ambitions were pent up and unexpressed—
translations.idiomatic: Ministers driven out by slander, scholars whose road ended at a humble gate, men like Qu Yuan, stirred by Ke's example yet never received, their ambitions choked off and never voiced—

sentences.zh: 憤激委約之中，飛文魏闕之下，奮迅泥滓，自致青雲，振沈溺於一朝，流風聲於千載者往往而有矣。

translations.literal: in the midst of indignant passion and straitened circumstance, beneath the soaring gates of Wei they sent their writings flying; struggling up from the mire they reached the blue clouds themselves, rousing the drowned in a single morning and streaming their fame through a thousand years—such men were often to be found.
translations.idiomatic: in the heat of resentment and the pinch of poverty, they sent their writings up to the imperial court; shaking off the mud they climbed to the clouds on their own, lifting the drowning in a single day and leaving a reputation that flowed through a thousand years—such cases were by no means rare.

sentences.zh: 漢自孝武之後，雅尚斯文，揚葩振藻者如林，而二馬、王、楊為之傑。

translations.literal: From Emperor Wu of Han onward, elegant literature was honored; those who flourished blossoms and shook brilliance were like a forest, yet the two Mas, Wang, and Yang were its champions.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Han, refined letters were held in esteem; writers who unfurled blossoms of style stood thick as a wood, yet the two Mas, Wang, and Yang were its foremost masters.

sentences.zh: 東京之朝，茲道逾扇，咀徵含商者成市，而班、傅、張、蔡為之雄。

translations.literal: In the Eastern Capital court this art was ever more fanned; those who chewed modes and held tones filled the market, while Ban, Fu, Zhang, and Cai were its heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Eastern Han the fashion spread ever wider; masters of tone and measure crowded the age, and Ban, Fu, Zhang, and Cai stood at its head.

sentences.zh: 當塗受命，尤好蟲篆；

translations.literal: When the House on the Road received the Mandate, it especially loved ornate seal script;
translations.idiomatic: When Wei received the Mandate, it especially favored ornate, archaic diction;

sentences.zh: 金行勃興，無替前烈。

translations.literal: the Metal Phase rose vigorously and did not replace the former glory.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Jin dynasty rose in turn, it did not fall short of what had come before.

sentences.zh: 曹、王、陳、阮負宏衍之思，挺棟幹于鄧林；

translations.literal: Cao, Wang, Chen, and Ruan bore vast, expansive thought, raising pillar timbers in the Deng Grove;
translations.idiomatic: Cao, Wang, Chen, and Ruan carried far-reaching minds, standing like great trunks in the Deng Grove;

sentences.zh: 潘、陸、張、左擅侈麗之才，飾羽儀於鳳穴。

translations.literal: Pan, Lu, Zhang, and Zuo excelled in lavish, ornate talent, adorning feather regalia at the phoenix's nest.
translations.idiomatic: while Pan, Lu, Zhang, and Zuo excelled in opulent brilliance, decking out their plumage at the phoenix's roost.

sentences.zh: 斯並高視當世，連衡孔門。

translations.literal: All these looked down on their age and linked arms with the Confucian school.
translations.idiomatic: All looked down upon their contemporaries and measured themselves against the Confucian tradition.

sentences.zh: 雖時運推移，質文屢變，譬猶六代並奏，易俗之用無爽；

translations.literal: Though the times shifted and substance and ornament changed again and again, it was like the six dynasties playing together—the use of changing custom did not err;
translations.idiomatic: Though fortune shifted and substance and ornament changed again and again, it was like the six modes played together—the power to transform custom remained unimpaired;

sentences.zh: 九源競逐，一致之理同歸。

translations.literal: nine sources racing in pursuit, yet the single principle returned to the same end.
translations.idiomatic: nine streams racing side by side, yet all converged on one underlying truth.

sentences.zh: 曆選前英，于斯為盛。

translations.literal: Surveying the eminent of former ages, none was more flourishing than this.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the masters of earlier ages, none surpassed this age in brilliance.

sentences.zh: 既而中州板蕩，戎狄交侵，僭偽相屬，生靈塗炭，故文章黜焉。

translations.literal: Then the central provinces were shaken, Rong and Di invaded in turn, usurpers and pretenders followed one upon another, and the people were scorched—so belles-lettres were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Then the heartland was torn apart, barbarians raided from every side, pretenders rose in succession, and the people were left in ashes—so literature itself was pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 其能潛思於戰爭之間，揮翰於鋒鏑之下，亦有時而間出矣。

translations.literal: Yet those who could ponder in secret amid war and wield the brush beneath spear and blade also appeared from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men who could compose in the midst of war and write under crossing blades still appeared, now and then.

sentences.zh: 若乃魯徵、杜廣、徐光、尹弼之儔，知名于二趙；

translations.literal: Such men as Lu Zheng, Du Guang, Xu Guang, and Yin Bi were famed in the two Zhao states;
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Lu Zheng, Du Guang, Xu Guang, and Yin Bi won renown in the two Zhao realms;

sentences.zh: 宋該、封弈、硃彤、梁讜之屬，見重于燕、秦。

translations.literal: while Song Gai, Feng Yi, Zhu Tong, and Liang Tan and their kind were esteemed in Yan and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: while Song Gai, Feng Yi, Zhu Tong, Liang Tan, and their like were held in honor in Yan and Qin.

sentences.zh: 然皆迫於倉卒，牽于戰陣，章奏符檄，則粲然可觀；

translations.literal: Yet all were pressed by haste and bound to the battlefield; memorials, reports, and military dispatches were splendid to behold;
translations.idiomatic: Yet all were driven by urgency and tied to the battlefield: their memorials, edicts, and dispatches could be brilliant;

sentences.zh: 體物緣情，則寂寥於世。

translations.literal: but in embodying things and following feeling, they were lonely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: yet in descriptive and lyrical verse they were nearly absent from the age.

sentences.zh: 非其才有優劣，時運然也。

translations.literal: This was not because their talent was superior or inferior—it was the turn of the times.
translations.idiomatic: This was not a matter of better or worse talent, but of what the times allowed.

sentences.zh: 至於朔方之地，蕞爾夷俗，胡義周之頌國都，足稱宏麗。

translations.literal: As for the northern frontier, a petty barbarian custom—Hu Yizhou's hymn to the capital could be called grand and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Even on the northern frontier, in what was only a petty barbarian culture, Hu Yizhou's hymn to the capital was truly magnificent.

sentences.zh: 區區河右，而學者埒于中原，劉延明之銘酒泉，可謂清典。

translations.literal: In the narrow lands west of the Yellow River, scholars were the equals of the central plain; Liu Yanming's inscription for Jiuquan may be called pure and canonical.
translations.idiomatic: In the modest lands west of the River, scholars could rival those of the central plain; Liu Yanming's inscription for Jiuquan may be called refined and authoritative.

sentences.zh: 子曰：「十室之邑，必有忠信。」

translations.literal: The Master said: "In a hamlet of ten households there must be loyalty and good faith."
translations.idiomatic: The Master said, "In a hamlet of ten households there are sure to be men of loyalty and integrity."

sentences.zh: 豈徒言哉。

translations.literal: Was this spoken in vain?
translations.idiomatic: Was that an empty saying?

sentences.zh: 洎乎有魏，定鼎沙朔。

translations.literal: When Wei arose, it set the tripod in the sands of the north.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei arose, it established its capital in the northern sands.

sentences.zh: 南包河、淮，西吞關、隴。

translations.literal: To the south it embraced the Yellow and Huai rivers; to the west it swallowed Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: To the south it took in the Yellow and Huai; to the west it absorbed Guan and Long.

sentences.zh: 當時之士，有許謙、崔巨集、巨集子浩、高允、高閭、遊雅等，先後之間，聲實俱茂，詞義典正，有永嘉之遺烈焉。

translations.literal: Among the gentlemen of that time were Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Hong's son Hao, Gao Yun, Gao Lu, You Ya, and others; in succession their fame and substance both flourished, their diction canonical and correct, preserving the lingering glory of the Yongjia era.
translations.idiomatic: Among the scholars of that age were Xu Qian, Cui Hong, Hong's son Hao, Gao Yun, Gao Lu, You Ya, and others. One after another their reputation and achievement flourished together; their language was canonical and correct, carrying forward the legacy of the Yongjia period.

sentences.zh: 及太和在運，銳情文學，固以頡頏漢徹，跨躡曹丕，氣韻高遠，豔藻獨構。

translations.literal: When the Taihe reign came into its destiny, literary passion sharpened; it truly matched Han Wudi and stepped across Cao Pi, its spirit lofty and far-reaching, its gorgeous ornament uniquely fashioned.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taihe era arrived, literary ambition sharpened; it could truly rival Han Wudi and stride past Cao Pi, with a spirit lofty and far-reaching and a gorgeous style all its own.

sentences.zh: 衣冠仰止，咸慕新風，律調頗殊，曲度遂改。

translations.literal: The gentry looked up and all admired the new style; tonal rules were quite different, and melodic patterns were changed.
translations.idiomatic: The educated elite looked up in admiration and all sought the new fashion; tonal rules shifted markedly, and musical patterns were remade.

sentences.zh: 辭罕泉源，言多胸臆，潤古雕今，有所未遇。

translations.literal: Their phrasing rarely drew from the springhead; their words came mostly from the breast—polishing antiquity and carving the present, something was still not met.
translations.idiomatic: Their diction seldom drew from deep springs; their words came mostly from the heart. In refining antiquity and shaping the present, something was still missing.

sentences.zh: 是故雅言麗則之奇，綺合繡聯之美，眇曆歲年，未聞獨得。

translations.literal: Therefore the marvel of elegant speech and beautiful rules, the beauty of brocade joined and embroidery linked—through distant years one never heard of a single master.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the marvel of elegant diction and polished form, the beauty of brocade joined and embroidery linked—for many years no single master was heard of.

sentences.zh: 既而陳郡袁翻、河內常景，晚拔疇類，稍革其風。

translations.literal: Then Yuan Fan of Chen commandery and Chang Jing of Henei, late in rising above their peers, gradually reformed this style.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuan Fan of Chen and Chang Jing of Henei, rising late among their peers, gradually changed this fashion.

sentences.zh: 及明皇禦曆，文雅大盛，學者如牛毛，成者如麟角。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne, elegant letters flourished greatly; learners were like ox-hairs, achievers like unicorn horns.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, letters flourished exceedingly; students were as numerous as ox-hairs, but finished masters as rare as unicorn horns.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「才難。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "Talent is hard to find."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Talent is hard to find."

sentences.zh: 不其然也？

translations.literal: Was it not so?
translations.idiomatic: Was that not exactly the case?

sentences.zh: 于時陳郡袁翻、翻弟躍、河東裴敬憲、弟莊伯、莊伯族弟伯茂、范陽盧觀、弟仲宣、頓丘李諧、勃海高肅、河間邢臧、趙國李騫，雕琢瓊瑤，刻削杞梓，並為龍光，俱稱鴻翼。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Fan of Chen, Fan's younger brother Yue, Pei Jingxian of Hedong, younger brother Zhuangbo, Zhuangbo's clansman younger brother Bomao, Lu Guan of Fanyang, younger brother Zhongxuan, Li Xie of Dunqiu, Gao Su of Bohai, Xing Zang of Hejian, and Li Qian of Zhao—carving jade and cutting catalpa—were all dragon light together, all called great wings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Fan of Chen, his brother Yue, Pei Jingxian of Hedong, his brothers Zhuangbo and Bomao, Lu Guan of Fanyang and his brother Zhongxuan, Li Xie of Dunqiu, Gao Su of Bohai, Xing Zang of Hejian, and Li Qian of Zhao—all carving fine jade and shaping choice timber—shone like dragon light and were hailed as great wings.

sentences.zh: 樂安孫彥舉、濟陰溫子升，並自孤寒，鬱然特起。

translations.literal: Sun Yanju of Le'an and Wen Zisheng of Jiyin both rose from lonely poverty and flourished with sudden distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yanju of Le'an and Wen Zisheng of Jiyin both rose from obscure poverty and flourished with sudden distinction.

sentences.zh: 咸能綜采繁縟，興屬清華。

translations.literal: All could gather and employ ornate complexity and raise themes of pure elegance.
translations.idiomatic: All could weave together rich ornament and lift themes of pure elegance.

sentences.zh: 比于建安之徐、陳、應、劉，元元之潘、張、左、束，各一時也。

translations.literal: Compared with the Xu, Chen, Ying, and Liu of the Jian'an era, or the Pan, Zhang, Zuo, and Shu of the Yuanyuan era, each was master of an age.
translations.idiomatic: They may be compared with the Xu, Chen, Ying, and Liu of the Jian'an period, or the Pan, Zhang, Zuo, and Shu of the Western Jin—each the voice of an age.

sentences.zh: 有齊自霸業雲啟，廣延髦俊，開四門以賓之，頓八紘以掩之。

translations.literal: When Qi arose from its hegemonic enterprise like clouds unfolding, it broadly extended invitation to eminent talents, opening the four gates to receive them as guests and pausing the eight cords to embrace them.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi began its hegemony like clouds unfolding, it widely gathered eminent men, opening the four gates to receive them and drawing in the whole realm.

sentences.zh: 鄴都之下，煙霏霧集。

translations.literal: Beneath the capital at Ye, mist and fog gathered thick.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath the capital at Ye, talents gathered thick as mist.

sentences.zh: 河間邢子才、钜鹿魏伯起、范陽盧元明、钜鹿魏季景、清河崔長儒、河間邢子明、范陽祖孝徵、中山杜輔玄、北平陽子烈並其流也。

translations.literal: Xing Zicai of Hejian, Wei Boqi of Julu, Lu Yuanming of Fanyang, Wei Jijing of Julu, Cui Changru of Qinghe, Xing Ziming of Hejian, Zu Xiaozheng of Fanyang, Du Fuxuan of Zhongshan, and Yang Zilie of Beiping were all of this current.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai of Hejian, Wei Boqi of Julu, Lu Yuanming of Fanyang, Wei Jijing of Julu, Cui Changru of Qinghe, Xing Ziming of Hejian, Zu Xiaozheng of Fanyang, Du Fuxuan of Zhongshan, and Yang Zilie of Beiping were all of this company.

sentences.zh: 復有范陽祖鴻勳，亦參文士之列。

translations.literal: There was also Zu Hongxun of Fanyang, who likewise joined the ranks of literary gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Hongxun of Fanyang also joined the ranks of literary men.

sentences.zh: 及天保中，李愔、陸仰、崔瞻、陸元規並在中書，參掌綸誥。

translations.literal: By the Tianbao era, Li Yin, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and Lu Yuangui were all at the Secretariat, sharing in the drafting of imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianbao era, Li Yin, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and Lu Yuangui all served in the Secretariat, drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 其李廣、樊遜、李德林、盧詢祖、盧思道始以文章著名。

translations.literal: Among them Li Guang, Fan Xun, Li Delin, Lu Xunzu, and Lu Sidao first became famous for their writings.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, Fan Xun, Li Delin, Lu Xunzu, and Lu Sidao first won fame through their writings.

sentences.zh: 皇建之朝，常侍王晞獨擅其美。

translations.literal: In the Huangjian reign, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Xi alone monopolized its excellence.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangjian reign, Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Xi alone held the palm in literary excellence.

sentences.zh: 河清、天統之辰，杜台卿、劉逖、魏騫亦參詔敕。

translations.literal: In the Heqing and Tiantong years, Du Taiqing, Liu Ti, and Wei Qian also took part in drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In the Heqing and Tiantong eras, Du Taiqing, Liu Ti, and Wei Qian also helped draft imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 自李愔已下，在省唯撰述除官詔旨，其關涉軍國文翰，多是魏收作之。

translations.literal: From Li Yin downward, those in the Secretariat only composed appointment and dismissal edicts; documents touching on military and state affairs were mostly written by Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Yin downward, those in the Secretariat chiefly drafted appointment edicts; documents touching military and state affairs were mostly written by Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 及在武平，李若、荀士遜、李德林、薛道衡並為中書侍郎，典司綸綍。

translations.literal: By the Wuping era, Li Ruo, Xun Shisun, Li Delin, and Xue Daheng were all Vice Directors of the Secretariat, presiding over the imperial brush.
translations.idiomatic: By the Wuping era, Li Ruo, Xun Shisun, Li Delin, and Xue Daheng all served as Vice Directors of the Secretariat, overseeing the drafting of edicts.

sentences.zh: 後主雖溺於群小，然頗好詠詩，幼時嘗讀詩賦，語人云：「終有解作此理不？」

translations.literal: Though the Last Ruler was drowned in petty men, he nevertheless quite loved composing poetry; in youth he had read poems and rhapsodies, and said to people: "Will there finally be someone who understands how to do this art?"
translations.idiomatic: Though the Last Ruler was sunk in petty favorites, he still loved composing poetry. In youth he had read poems and rhapsodies and said to others, "Will there ever be someone who truly understands how to do this?"

sentences.zh: 初因畫屏風，敕通直郎蕭放及晉陵王孝式錄古賢烈士及近代輕豔諸詩以充圖畫，帝彌重之。

translations.literal: At first, because of painted screens, he ordered Palace Gentleman Xiao Fang and Prince Xiaoshi of Jinling to record poems of ancient worthies, martyrs, and recent light and alluring verse to fill out the pictures; the emperor valued this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: At first, for painted screens, he ordered Palace Gentleman Xiao Fang and Prince Xiaoshi of Jinling to collect poems of ancient worthies, martyrs, and recent light and alluring verse to accompany the pictures, and the emperor valued this all the more.

sentences.zh: 後復追齊州錄事參軍蕭愨、趙州功曹參軍顏之推同入撰錄，猶依霸朝，謂之館客。

translations.literal: Later he recalled Qizhou Recorder Xiao Que and Zhaozhou Merit Officer Yan Zhitui to join in compiling and recording; still following the hegemonic court, they were called lodge guests.
translations.idiomatic: Later he recalled Qizhou Recorder Xiao Que and Zhaozhou Merit Officer Yan Zhitui to join the compilation, still following the old hegemonic custom and calling them lodge guests.

sentences.zh: 放及之推意欲更廣其事，又因祖珽輔政，愛重之推，又托鄧長顒漸說後主，屬意斯文。

translations.literal: Fang and Zhitui wished to broaden the undertaking further; moreover, because Zu Ting was regent and cherished Zhitui, and also through Deng Changying gradually persuading the Last Ruler, he turned his mind to refined letters.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and Zhitui wished to broaden the project further. Zu Ting, then regent, cherished Zhitui, and through Deng Changying gradually persuaded the Last Ruler to turn his heart to letters.

sentences.zh: 三年，祖珽奏立文林館，於是更召引文學士，謂之待詔文林館焉。

translations.literal: In the third year Zu Ting memorialized to establish the Forest of Letters Lodge, and so literary scholars were again summoned and called attendants-at-court of the Forest of Letters Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Zu Ting memorialized to establish the Forest of Letters Lodge, and literary scholars were again summoned as attendants-at-court of that lodge.

sentences.zh: 珽又奏撰《御覽》，詔珽及特進魏收、太子太師徐之才、中書令崔劼、散騎常侍張凋、中書監陽休之監撰。

translations.literal: Ting also memorialized to compile the Imperial Overview; an edict ordered Ting, Special Advance Wei Shou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Xu Zhicai, Director of the Secretariat Cui Jie, Regular Attendant Zhang Diao, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Yang Xiuzhi to supervise the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Ting also memorialized to compile the Imperial Overview. An edict appointed Ting, Special Advance Wei Shou, Grand Tutor of the Heir Xu Zhicai, Director of the Secretariat Cui Jie, Regular Attendant Zhang Diao, and Supervisor of the Secretariat Yang Xiuzhi to supervise it.

sentences.zh: 珽等奏追通直散騎侍郎韋道遜、陸乂、太子舍人王劭、衛尉丞李孝基、殿中侍御史魏澹、中散大夫劉仲威、袁奭、國子博士硃才、奉車都尉眭道閑、考功郎中崔子樞、左外兵郎薛道衡、並省主客郎中盧思道、司空東閣祭酒崔德立、太傅行參軍崔儦、太學博士諸葛漢、奉朝請鄭公超、殿中侍御史鄭子信等入館撰書，並敕放、愨、之推等同入撰例。

translations.literal: Ting and the others memorialized to recall Palace Attendant Wei Daoxun, Lu Yi, Crown Prince Household Officer Wang Shao, Commandant of the Guard Li Xiaoji, Palace Attendant Censor Wei Dan, Palace Attendant Liu Zhongwei, Yuan Shang, Director of the National University Zhu Cai, Commandant of the Imperial Carriage Sui Daoxian, Director of Evaluations Cui Zishu, Outer Left Military Gentleman Xue Daheng, Concurrent Director of Guests Lu Sidao, Libationer of the Eastern Pavilion of the Ministry of Works Cui Deli, Acting Gentleman of the Grand Tutor Cui Yi, Director of the Imperial University Zhuge Han, Court Gentleman Zheng Gongchao, Palace Attendant Censor Zheng Zixin, and others to enter the lodge and compile books; an edict also ordered Fang, Que, and Zhitui to enter the compilation rules together.
translations.idiomatic: Ting and his colleagues memorialized to recall Wei Daoxun, Lu Yi, Wang Shao, Li Xiaoji, Wei Dan, Liu Zhongwei, Yuan Shang, Zhu Cai, Sui Daoxian, Cui Zishu, Xue Daheng, Lu Sidao, Cui Deli, Cui Yi, Zhuge Han, Zheng Gongchao, Zheng Zixin, and others to enter the lodge and compile books, and also ordered Fang, Que, and Zhitui to join the project on the same terms.

sentences.zh: 復命散騎常侍封孝琰、前樂陵太守鄭元禮、衛尉少卿杜台卿、通直散騎常侍楊訓、前南兗州長史羊肅、通直散騎侍郎馬元熙、並省三公郎中劉瑉、開府行參軍李師上、溫君悠入館，亦令撰書。

translations.literal: They were again ordered to summon Regular Attendant Feng Xiaoyan, former Administrator of Leling Zheng Yuanli, Vice Commandant of the Guard Du Taiqing, Regular Attendant Yang Xun, former Chief Clerk of Southern Yanzhou Yang Su, Palace Attendant Ma Yuanxi, Concurrent Director of the Three Dukes Liu Min, Acting Gentleman of the Opening Office Li Shishang, and Wen Junyou to enter the lodge and likewise compile books.
translations.idiomatic: They were again ordered to summon Feng Xiaoyan, former Administrator of Leling Zheng Yuanli, Vice Commandant Du Taiqing, Yang Xun, former Chief Clerk of Southern Yanzhou Yang Su, Ma Yuanxi, Liu Min, Li Shishang, and Wen Junyou to enter the lodge and compile books as well.

sentences.zh: 後復命特進崔季舒、前仁州刺史劉逖、散騎常侍李孝貞、中書侍郎李德林續入待詔。

translations.literal: Later they were again ordered to summon Special Advance Cui Jishu, former Inspector of Renzhou Liu Ti, Regular Attendant Li Xiaozhen, and Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Delin to continue entering as attendants-at-court.
translations.idiomatic: Later Special Advance Cui Jishu, former Inspector of Renzhou Liu Ti, Regular Attendant Li Xiaozhen, and Vice Director Li Delin were also summoned to continue as attendants-at-court.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔諸人各舉所知。

translations.literal: Soon an edict again ordered each man to recommend those he knew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered each man to recommend those he knew.

sentences.zh: 又有前濟州長史李翥、前廣武太守魏謇、前西兗州司馬蕭溉、前幽州長史陸仁惠、鄭州司馬江旰、前通直散騎侍郎辛德源、陸開明、通直郎封孝騫、太尉掾張德沖、並省右戶郎元行恭、司徒戶曹參軍古道子、前司空功曹參軍劉顗、獲嘉令崔德儒、給事中李元楷、晉州中從事陽師孝、太尉中兵參軍劉儒行、司空祭酒陽辟疆、司公士曹參軍盧公順、司空中兵參軍周子深、開府行參軍王友伯、崔君洽、魏師謇併入館待詔。

translations.literal: There were also former Chief Clerk of Jizhou Li Xu, former Administrator of Guangwu Wei Qian, former Major of Western Yanzhou Xiao Gai, former Chief Clerk of Youzhou Lu Renhui, Major of Zhengzhou Jiang Gan, former Palace Attendant Xin Deyuan, Lu Kaiming, Palace Gentleman Feng Xiaoqian, Secretariat Officer of the Grand Commandant Zhang Dechong, Concurrent Director of the Right Household Yuan Xinggong, Household Officer of the Minister of Education Gu Daozi, former Merit Officer of the Ministry of Works Liu Yi, Magistrate of Huojia Cui Deru, Attendant within the Gates Li Yuanqi, Middle Retainer of Jinzhou Yang Shixiao, Middle Military Officer of the Grand Commandant Liu Ruxing, Libationer of the Ministry of Works Yang Bijiang, Gentleman of the Ministry of Public Works Lu Gongshun, Middle Military Officer of the Ministry of Works Zhou Zishen, Acting Gentleman of the Opening Office Wang Youbo, Cui Junqia, and Wei Shiqian—all entering the lodge as attendants-at-court.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Li Xu, Wei Qian, Xiao Gai, Lu Renhui, Jiang Gan, Xin Deyuan, Lu Kaiming, Feng Xiaoqian, Zhang Dechong, Yuan Xinggong, Gu Daozi, Liu Yi, Cui Deru, Li Yuanqi, Yang Shixiao, Liu Ruxing, Yang Bijiang, Lu Gongshun, Zhou Zishen, Wang Youbo, Cui Junqia, and Wei Shiqian—all brought into the lodge as attendants-at-court.

sentences.zh: 又敕僕射段孝言亦入焉。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered Vice Director Duan Xiaoyan to enter as well.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered Vice Director Duan Xiaoyan to join them.

sentences.zh: 《御覽》成後，所撰錄人亦有不得待詔，付所司處分者。

translations.literal: After the Imperial Overview was completed, some of those who had compiled and recorded were not granted attendant status and were handed over to the relevant offices for disposition.
translations.idiomatic: After the Imperial Overview was completed, some compilers were not granted attendant status and were handed over to the relevant offices for disposition.

sentences.zh: 凡此諸人，亦有文學膚淺，附會親識，妄相推薦者十三四焉。

translations.literal: Of all these men, some three or four in ten also had shallow learning, curried favor with kin and acquaintances, and recklessly recommended one another.
translations.idiomatic: Of all these men, perhaps three or four in ten had shallow learning, curried favor with kin and acquaintances, and recklessly recommended one another.

sentences.zh: 雖然，當時操筆之徒，搜求略盡。

translations.literal: Even so, those who wielded the brush at the time were sought out almost to exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, the writers of the age were sought out almost to the last man.

sentences.zh: 其外如廣平宋孝王、信都劉善經輩三數人，論其才性，入館諸賢亦十三四不逮之。

translations.literal: Beyond them, such men as Song Xiaowang of Guangping and Liu Shanqing of Xindu—a few in number—in talent and nature were also not matched by three or four in ten of the worthies who entered the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond them, a few men such as Song Xiaowang of Guangping and Liu Shanqing of Xindu, judged by talent and character, were unmatched by three or four in ten of those who entered the lodge.

sentences.zh: 周氏創業，運屬陵夷，纂遺文於既喪，聘奇士如弗及。

translations.literal: When the Zhou house founded its enterprise, fortune belonged to decline; it gathered surviving writings after they had perished and recruited extraordinary men as though it could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou house founded its enterprise in an age of decline, it gathered surviving writings after civilization had collapsed and recruited extraordinary men as though racing against time.

sentences.zh: 是以蘇亮、蘇綽、盧柔、唐瑾、元偉、李昶之徒，咸奮鱗翼，自致青紫。

translations.literal: Therefore Su Liang, Su Chuo, Lu Rou, Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Li Chang, and their kind all roused scales and wings and reached the purple and blue ranks on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Su Liang, Su Chuo, Lu Rou, Tang Jin, Yuan Wei, Li Chang, and their like all spread their wings and rose to high office on their own.

sentences.zh: 然綽之建言，務存質樸，遂糠秕魏、晉，憲章虞、夏，雖屬辭有師古之美，矯枉非適時之用，故莫能常行焉。

translations.literal: Yet Chuo's proposals aimed to preserve simplicity and plainness; he therefore rejected Wei and Jin as chaff and took Yu and Xia as his model. Though his phrasing had the beauty of honoring antiquity, correcting excess was not suited to the needs of the time, so it could not be practiced for long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Chuo's proposals aimed at plainness and simplicity; he rejected Wei and Jin as chaff and took Yu and Xia as his model. Though his diction had the beauty of honoring antiquity, such correction was ill suited to the age, and so it could not endure.

sentences.zh: 既而革車電邁，渚宮雲撤，梁、荊之風，扇于關右，狂簡之徒，斐然成俗，流宕忘反，無所取裁。

translations.literal: Then war-chariots flashed like lightning and the palace on the isle vanished like clouds; the styles of Liang and Jing fanned west of the Pass, and reckless, shallow men flourished into custom, drifting without return, with nothing to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Then war-chariots raced like lightning and the palace on the isle vanished like clouds; the styles of Liang and Jing swept west of the Pass, and reckless, shallow writers flourished into custom, drifting without return and beyond restraint.

sentences.zh: 夫人有六情，稟五常之秀；

translations.literal: Man has the six emotions and receives the excellence of the five constants;
translations.idiomatic: Human beings possess the six emotions and partake of the excellence of the five constants;

sentences.zh: 情感六氣，順四時之序。

translations.literal: emotion responds to the six qi and follows the sequence of the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: and emotion responds to the six qi, following the sequence of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 蓋文之所起，情發於中。

translations.literal: Thus writing arises because feeling bursts forth from within.
translations.idiomatic: Writing arises because feeling bursts forth from within.

sentences.zh: 而自漢、魏以來，迄乎晉、宋，其體屢變，前哲論之詳矣。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei down to Jin and Song, its forms changed again and again, as former sages have discussed in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei down to Jin and Song, its forms changed again and again, as earlier critics have discussed at length.

sentences.zh: 暨永明、天監之際，太和、天保之間，洛陽、江左，文雅尤盛，彼此好尚，互有異同。

translations.literal: By the Yongming and Tianjian eras, and between the Taihe and Tianbao reigns, Luoyang and the lands south of the Yangtze saw elegant letters flourish especially; each side's preferences differed in part from the other.
translations.idiomatic: By the Yongming and Tianjian eras, and between the Taihe and Tianbao reigns, Luoyang and the south of the Yangtze saw letters flourish especially, yet their tastes differed in important ways.

sentences.zh: 江左宮商發越，貴於清綺；

translations.literal: South of the Yangtze, modes soared in brilliance and valued pure elegance;
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangtze, tonal patterns soared and pure elegance was prized;

sentences.zh: 河朔詞義貞剛，重乎氣質。

translations.literal: north of the Yellow River, diction and meaning were steadfast and firm, stressing vital substance.
translations.idiomatic: while north of the River, diction and meaning were steadfast and firm, stressing vital substance.

sentences.zh: 氣質則理勝其詞，清綺則文過其意。

translations.literal: Where vital substance prevailed, principle outweighed phrasing; where pure elegance prevailed, ornament exceeded intent.
translations.idiomatic: Where substance prevailed, principle outweighed ornament; where elegance prevailed, ornament exceeded intent.

sentences.zh: 理深者便於時用，文華者宜於詠歌。

translations.literal: Deep principle was suited to timely use; florid writing was fit for song and chant.
translations.idiomatic: Depth of principle served timely use; florid writing suited song and chant.

sentences.zh: 此其南北詞人得失之大較也。

translations.literal: This is the great comparison of the gains and losses of poets north and south.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the broad comparison of the strengths and weaknesses of poets north and south.

sentences.zh: 若能掇彼清音，簡茲累句，各去所短，合其兩長，則文質彬彬，盡美盡善矣。

translations.literal: If one could gather those pure tones and simplify these encumbered lines, each removing its shortcoming and combining the two strengths, then substance and ornament would be balanced, beauty and goodness complete.
translations.idiomatic: If one could gather those pure tones and simplify these encumbered lines, each side discarding its weakness and combining its strengths, then substance and ornament would be balanced and perfection attained.

sentences.zh: 梁自大同之後，雅道淪缺，漸乖典則，爭馳新巧。

translations.literal: From Datong onward in Liang, the elegant Way collapsed and fell short, gradually departing from canonical norms as men raced after new cleverness.
translations.idiomatic: From the Datong era onward in Liang, the elegant Way collapsed, norms were gradually abandoned, and men raced after new cleverness.

sentences.zh: 簡文、湘東啟其淫放，徐陵、庾信分路揚鑣。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen and the Prince of Xiangdong opened its licentious excess; Xu Ling and Yu Xin went their separate ways.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen and the Prince of Xiangdong opened the way to licentious excess; Xu Ling and Yu Xin went their separate ways.

sentences.zh: 其意淺而繁，其文匿而彩，詞尚輕險，情多哀思，格以延陵之聽，蓋亦亡國之音也。

translations.literal: Their ideas were shallow yet elaborate, their writing hidden yet colorful; diction favored lightness and peril, feeling mostly mournful thought—judged by Yanling's ear, this was surely also the music of a perishing state.
translations.idiomatic: Their ideas were shallow yet elaborate, their writing ornate yet insubstantial; diction favored lightness and peril, feeling mostly mournful—judged by the standards of the ancients, this was music fit for a dying state.

sentences.zh: 隋文初統萬機，每念斫凋為樸，發號施令，咸去浮華。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui first took charge of all affairs, he often thought of cutting ornament back to plainness; in issuing orders and commands, he removed all florid display.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui first took the reins of government, he often thought of cutting ornament back to plainness; in issuing orders and commands, he stripped away florid display.

sentences.zh: 然時俗詞藻、猶多淫麗；

translations.literal: Yet the diction of the age still tended toward licentious splendor;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the diction of the age still tended toward licentious splendor;

sentences.zh: 故憲台執法，屢飛霜簡。

translations.literal: Therefore the censorate enforced the law, and frost-indictments flew forth again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the censorate upheld the law, sending down indictments again and again.

sentences.zh: 煬帝初習藝文，有非輕側，暨乎即位，一變其體。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang at first studied arts and letters, and some works were frivolous and unbalanced; when he came to the throne, he changed his style entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years Emperor Yang studied literature, and some of his work was light and unbalanced; once he took the throne, he changed his style entirely.

sentences.zh: 《與越公書》、《建東都詔》、《冬至受朝詩》及《擬飲馬長城窟》，並存雅體，歸於典制，雖意在驕淫，而詞無浮蕩。

translations.literal: His "Letter to the Duke of Yue," "Edict on Building the Eastern Capital," "Poem on Receiving Court at the Winter Solstice," and "After 'Drinking Horses at the Long Wall Cavern'" all preserved an elegant style and conformed to canonical norms; though the intent was arrogant and dissolute, the wording was not florid or unmoored.
translations.idiomatic: His Letter to the Duke of Yue, Edict on Building the Eastern Capital, Poem on Receiving Court at the Winter Solstice, and After "Drinking Horses at the Long Wall Cavern" all kept an elegant style and fit canonical form; though his intent was arrogant and dissolute, his diction was not florid or unmoored.

sentences.zh: 故當時綴文之士，遂得依而取正焉。

translations.literal: Therefore writers of the time were able to take them as standards and set their course by them.
translations.idiomatic: Writers of the time could therefore take them as standards and set their course accordingly.

sentences.zh: 所謂能言者未必能行，蓋亦君子不以人廢言也。

translations.literal: As the saying goes, those who can speak well may not necessarily act well—yet the gentleman does not reject words because of the man.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, those who speak well do not necessarily act well—yet a gentleman does not reject words because of the man who spoke them.

sentences.zh: 爰自東帝歸秦，逮乎青蓋入洛，四隩咸暨，九州攸同。

translations.literal: From when the Eastern Emperor returned to Qin until the green-canopied carriage entered Luoyang, the four corners all arrived, and the nine provinces were united as one.
translations.idiomatic: From the Eastern Emperor's submission to Qin until the Jin emperor's entry into Luoyang, the four corners of the realm were brought in, and the nine provinces were united.

sentences.zh: 江、漢英靈，燕、趙奇俊，並該天綱之中，俱為大國之寶。

translations.literal: Spirits of talent from the Yangtze and Han, extraordinary men of Yan and Zhao—all were caught within the celestial net and were treasures of great states alike.
translations.idiomatic: Talented men from the Yangtze and Han regions and remarkable figures from Yan and Zhao—all fell within the imperial net and were alike treasures of great states.

sentences.zh: 言刈其楚，片善無遺，潤水圓流，不能十數，才之難也，不其然乎。

translations.literal: One might say of harvesting Chu that no scrap of merit was left behind, yet the rounded flow of Renshui cannot fill even ten vessels—is it not that talent is hard to come by?
translations.idiomatic: Though one could gather every scrap of merit as when harvesting Chu, the rounded stream of talent could not fill even ten vessels—is it not that ability is scarce?

sentences.zh: 時之文人，見稱當世者，則齊人范陽盧思道、安平李德林、河東薛道衡、趙郡李元操、钜鹿魏澹，陳人會稽虞世基、河東柳{巧言}、高陽許善心等，或鷹揚河朔，或獨步漢南，俱騁龍光，並驅雲路矣。

translations.literal: Among the men of letters of the time who were acclaimed in their age were, from Qi, Fan-yang's Lu Sidao, Anping's Li Delin, Hedong's Xue Daoheng, Zhao commandery's Li Yuancao, and Julu's Wei Dan; from Chen, Kuaiji's Yu Shiji, Hedong's Liu Guyan, and Gaoyang's Xu Shanxin, and others—some soared like eagles over the Hebei region, some walked alone south of the Han; all alike displayed dragon brilliance and raced along the cloud road.
translations.idiomatic: The writers of the age who won renown in their own time included, from Northern Qi, Lu Sidao of Fanyang, Li Delin of Anping, Xue Daoheng of Hedong, Li Yuancao of Zhao commandery, and Wei Dan of Julu; from Chen, Yu Shiji of Kuaiji, Liu Guyan of Hedong, and Xu Shanxin of Gaoyang, among others—some soared over the Hebei region, some stood alone south of the Han; all alike displayed outstanding brilliance and advanced along the high road of fame.

sentences.zh: 《魏書》序袁躍、裴敬憲、盧觀、封肅、邢臧、裴伯茂、邢昕、溫子升為《文苑傳》，今唯取子升，其餘並各附其家傳。

translations.literal: The Book of Wei arranged Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Zang, Pei Bimao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng in the "Garden of Letters" biography; here only Zisheng is taken, while the rest are each attached to their family biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Wei placed Yuan Yue, Pei Jingxian, Lu Guan, Feng Su, Xing Zang, Pei Bimao, Xing Xin, and Wen Zisheng in the Garden of Letters biography; here only Zisheng is included, while the rest are each placed in their family biographies.

sentences.zh: 《齊書》敘祖鴻勳、李廣、樊遜、劉逖、荀士遜、顏之推為《文苑傳》，今唯取祖、李、樊、荀，其餘亦各附其家傳。

translations.literal: The Book of Qi narrated Zu Hongxun, Li Guang, Fan Xun, Liu Ti, Xun Shisun, and Yan Zhitui in the "Garden of Letters" biography; here only Zu, Li, Fan, and Xun are taken, while the rest are likewise each attached to their family biographies.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Qi included Zu Hongxun, Li Guang, Fan Xun, Liu Ti, Xun Shisun, and Yan Zhitui in the Garden of Letters biography; here only Zu, Li, Fan, and Xun are included, while the rest are likewise placed in their family biographies.

sentences.zh: 《周書》不立此傳，今取王褒、庾信列於此篇。

translations.literal: The Book of Zhou did not establish this biography; here Wang Bao and Yu Xin are placed in this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Zhou did not include such a biography; here Wang Bao and Yu Xin are placed in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 顏之推竟從齊入周，故列在王、庾之下。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui in the end followed Qi into Zhou, and therefore is listed below Wang and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui eventually went from Qi into Zhou, and is therefore listed below Wang and Yu.

sentences.zh: 顏之儀既之推之弟，故列在之推之末。

translations.literal: Yan Zhiyi being Zhitui's younger brother, he is therefore listed at the end after Zhitui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhiyi was Zhitui's younger brother and is therefore listed immediately after him.

sentences.zh: 《隋書》序劉臻、崔儦、王頍、諸葛潁、王貞、孫萬壽、虞綽、王胄、庾自直、潘徽為《文學傳》，今檢崔儦、王頍、孫萬壽各從其家傳，其餘編之此篇，並取虞世基、許善心、柳{巧言}、明克讓冠之於此，以備《文苑傳》云。

translations.literal: The Book of Sui arranged Liu Zhen, Cui Ti, Wang Yi, Zhuge Ying, Wang Zhen, Sun Wanshou, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, Yu Zizhi, and Pan Hui in the "Literary Writings" biography; on examination Cui Ti, Wang Yi, and Sun Wanshou are each placed in their family biographies, while the rest are compiled in this chapter; Yu Shiji, Xu Shanxin, Liu Guyan, and Ming Kerang are also taken and placed at the head here, to complete the "Garden of Letters" biography.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Sui placed Liu Zhen, Cui Ti, Wang Yi, Zhuge Ying, Wang Zhen, Sun Wanshou, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, Yu Zizhi, and Pan Hui in the Literary Writings biography; on review, Cui Ti, Wang Yi, and Sun Wanshou are each given in their family biographies, while the rest are compiled in this chapter; Yu Shiji, Xu Shanxin, Liu Guyan, and Ming Kerang are also placed at the head here to complete the Garden of Letters biography.

sentences.zh: 溫子升，字鵬舉，自雲太原人，晉大將軍嶠之後也。

translations.literal: Wen Zisheng, courtesy name Pengju, claimed for himself to be a man of Taiyuan and a descendant of the Jin Grand General Wen Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zisheng, courtesy name Pengju, claimed descent from Taiyuan and from the Jin Grand General Wen Jiao.

sentences.zh: 世居江左。

translations.literal: His family for generations resided in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His family had lived south of the Yangtze for generations.

sentences.zh: 祖恭之，宋彭城王義康戶曹，避難歸魏，家于濟陰冤句，因為其郡縣人焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gongzhi was registrar in the household of Song's Prince of Pengcheng, Kang; fleeing trouble he returned to Wei and settled in Yuanqu in Jiyin, and thereby became a man of that commandery and county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gongzhi served as registrar in the household of Liu Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng of Song; fleeing turmoil he went over to Wei and settled in Yuanqu in Jiyin, and thus became a native of that commandery and county.

sentences.zh: 父暉，兗州左將軍長史，行濟陰郡事。

translations.literal: His father Hui was chief clerk to the Left General of Yan province and acted as administrator of Jiyin commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hui was chief clerk to the Left General of Yan province and acted as administrator of Jiyin commandery.

sentences.zh: 子升初受學于崔靈恩、劉蘭。

translations.literal: Zisheng at first received instruction from Cui Lin'en and Liu Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng first studied under Cui Lin'en and Liu Lan.

sentences.zh: 精勤，以夜繼晝，晝夜不倦。

translations.literal: He was diligent and refined, continuing through the night into day, never weary day or night.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with tireless diligence, continuing through the night into day without ever tiring.

sentences.zh: 長乃博覽百家，文章清婉。

translations.literal: When grown he broadly read the works of the hundred schools, and his writing was clear and graceful.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he read widely among the hundred schools, and his writing was clear and graceful.

sentences.zh: 為廣陽王深賤客，在馬坊教諸奴子書。

translations.literal: He became a low-ranking retainer to Prince of Guangyang Shen and in the horse stables taught the household slaves to read.
translations.idiomatic: He became a low-ranking retainer to Prince Shen of Guangyang and in the horse stables taught the household slaves to read.

sentences.zh: 作《侯山祠堂碑文》，常景見而善之，故詣深謝之。

translations.literal: He wrote the "Stele Inscription for the Hou Mountain Ancestral Shrine"; Chang Jing saw it and approved of it, and therefore went to Shen to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Stele Inscription for the Hou Mountain Ancestral Shrine; Chang Jing saw it and admired it, and therefore went to Shen to express his thanks.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「頃見溫生。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Recently I saw Master Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "I recently saw Master Wen.

sentences.zh: 深怪問之。

translations.literal: Shen wondered and questioned him about it.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was puzzled and questioned him about it.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「溫生是大才士。」

translations.literal: Jing said: "Master Wen is a great man of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "Master Wen is a man of great talent.

sentences.zh: 深由是稍知之。

translations.literal: Thereby Shen gradually came to know of him.
translations.idiomatic: From this Shen gradually came to know of him.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，中尉、東平王匡博召辭人以充御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xiping era, the Commandant and Prince of Dongping, Kuang, broadly summoned men of letters to fill the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiping era, the Commandant and Prince of Dongping, Kuang, broadly summoned men of letters to fill posts in the censorate.

sentences.zh: 同時射策者八百餘人，子升與盧仲宣、孫搴等二十四人為高第。

translations.literal: At the same time more than eight hundred men took the policy-examination; Zisheng, together with Lu Zhongxuan, Sun Qian, and twenty-four others, received the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: More than eight hundred men took the civil examination at the same time; Zisheng, together with Lu Zhongxuan, Sun Qian, and twenty-four others, received the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 於是預選者爭相引決，匡使子升當之，皆受屈而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon those who had been pre-selected vied to challenge him to decisive contests; Kuang had Zisheng take them on, and all were overborne and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had been pre-selected then vied to challenge him to decisive contests; Kuang had Zisheng face them, and all were defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 搴謂人曰：「朝來靡旗亂轍者，皆子升逐北。」

translations.literal: Qian said to others: "Those who this morning had their banners scattered and wheels overturned were all driven north by Zisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said to others, "Everyone whose banners were scattered and wheels overturned this morning was driven north by Zisheng.

sentences.zh: 遂補御史，時年二十二。

translations.literal: He was then appointed censor, at the age of twenty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed censor at the age of twenty-two.

sentences.zh: 台中彈文皆委焉。

translations.literal: Impeachment documents within the censorate were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Impeachment documents within the censorate were all entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 以憂去任。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，還為朝請。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he returned as Court Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he returned to service as Court Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 後李神俊行荊州事，引兼錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Later, when Li Shenjun acted as administrator of Jing province, he summoned him as acting recorder and staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Li Shenjun administered Jing province, he summoned Zisheng as acting recorder and staff officer.

sentences.zh: 被徽赴省，神俊表留不遣。

translations.literal: He was summoned by imperial order to the capital; Shenjun memorialized to retain him and not send him away.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned by imperial order to the capital; Shenjun memorialized to retain him and not release him.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中李獎退表不許，曰：「昔伯瑜之不應留，王朗所以發歎。

translations.literal: Li Jiang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, returned the memorial without approval, saying: "In former days Bo Yu did not comply with being retained, and for that Wang Lang sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, returned the memorial disapproved, saying, "In former days Bo Yu would not comply with being retained, and Wang Lang sighed over it.

sentences.zh: 宜速遣赴，無踵彥雲前失。」

translations.literal: You should send him quickly and not follow in Yan Yun's earlier mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Send him quickly, and do not repeat Yan Yun's earlier mistake.

sentences.zh: 於是還省。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及廣陽王深為東北道行台，召為郎中。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guangyang Shen became Commissioner of the Northeast Route, he summoned him as Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shen of Guangyang became Commissioner of the Northeast Route, he summoned him as Gentleman of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎徐紇受四方表啟，答之敏速，于深獨沈思，曰：「彼有溫郎中，才藻可畏。」

translations.literal: Huangmen Gentleman Xu He received memorials and reports from the four quarters and answered them with quick facility; toward Shen alone he pondered and said: "Over there is Gentleman Wen—the brilliance of his talent is to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Huangmen Gentleman Xu He received memorials and reports from the four quarters and answered them with quick facility; toward Shen alone he pondered and said, "Over there is Gentleman Wen—the brilliance of his talent is to be feared.

sentences.zh: 高車破走，珍寶盈滿，子升取絹四十疋。

translations.literal: The Gaoche were defeated and fled; precious goods filled the camp, and Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche were defeated and fled; precious goods filled the camp, and Zisheng took forty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 深軍敗，子升為葛榮所得。

translations.literal: When Shen's army was defeated, Zisheng was taken by Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen's army was defeated, Zisheng was captured by Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮下都督和洛興與子升舊識，以數十騎潛送子升，得達冀州。

translations.literal: Ge Rong's subordinate commander He Luoxing was an old acquaintance of Zisheng; with several dozen horsemen he secretly escorted Zisheng, and he was able to reach Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's subordinate commander He Luoxing was an old acquaintance of Zisheng; with several dozen horsemen he secretly escorted Zisheng until he reached Ji province.

sentences.zh: 還京，李楷執其手曰：「卿今得免，足使夷甫慚德。」

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, Li Kai took his hand and said: "You have now escaped—enough to make Yifu ashamed of his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, Li Kai took his hand and said, "You have now escaped—enough to make Wang Yan ashamed of his own conduct.

sentences.zh: 自是無復宦情，閉門讀書，厲精不已。

translations.literal: From this time he had no further desire for office; he shut his doors and read books, refining his purpose without cease.
translations.idiomatic: From this time he had no further desire for office; he shut his doors and read books, refining his purpose without cease.

sentences.zh: 及孝莊即位，以子升為南主客郎中，修起居注。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang came to the throne, he appointed Zisheng Gentleman of the Southern Host and ordered him to compile the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang came to the throne, he appointed Zisheng Gentleman of the Southern Host and ordered him to compile the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 曾一日不直，上党王天穆時錄尚書事，將加捶撻，子升遂逃遁。

translations.literal: Once he failed to attend duty for a single day; Shangdang Prince Tianmu was then acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was about to have him beaten; Zisheng thereupon fled.
translations.idiomatic: Once he failed to attend duty for a single day; Prince Tianmu of Shangdang was then acting Director of the Imperial Secretariat and was about to have him beaten, and Zisheng fled.

sentences.zh: 天穆甚怒，奏人代之。

translations.literal: Tianmu was greatly angry and memorialized that another man replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu was greatly angered and memorialized that another man replace him.

sentences.zh: 莊帝曰：「當世才子不過數人，豈容為此便相放黜？」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang said: "The talented men of the age number no more than a few—how can we dismiss one for this alone?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said, "The talented men of the age number no more than a few—how can we dismiss one for this alone?

sentences.zh: 乃寢其奏。

translations.literal: Thereupon the memorial was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 及天穆將討邢杲，召子升同行，子升未敢應。

translations.literal: When Tianmu was about to campaign against Xing Geng, he summoned Zisheng to go with him; Zisheng did not dare answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianmu was about to campaign against Xing Geng, he summoned Zisheng to accompany him; Zisheng did not dare respond.

sentences.zh: 天穆謂人曰：「吾欲收其才用，豈懷前忿也？

translations.literal: Tianmu said to others: "I wish to employ his talent—do you think I bear an earlier grudge?
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu said to others, "I wish to employ his talent—do you think I still bear an earlier grudge?

sentences.zh: 今復不來，便須南走越，北走胡耳！」

translations.literal: If he does not come now, he will have to flee south to Yue or north to the barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: If he does not come now, he will have to flee south to Yue or north to the barbarians!

sentences.zh: 子升不得已而見之。

translations.literal: Zisheng, having no alternative, went to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng, having no alternative, went to see him.

sentences.zh: 加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Subdues Waves.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title General Who Subdues Waves.

sentences.zh: 為行台郎中。

translations.literal: He served as Gentleman of the Route Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Gentleman of the Route Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天穆深知賞之。

translations.literal: Tianmu deeply knew and appreciated him.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu deeply appreciated him.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，天穆召子升問曰：「即欲向京師？

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianmu summoned Zisheng and asked: "Do you intend to go at once to the capital?
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Tianmu summoned Zisheng and asked, "Do you intend to go at once to the capital?

sentences.zh: 為隨我北度？」

translations.literal: Or will you follow me north across the river?
translations.idiomatic: Or will you follow me north across the river?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「主上以武牢失守，致此狼狽。

translations.literal: He replied: "The sovereign, because Wu Fortress was lost, has come to this distress.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The sovereign, because Wu Fortress was lost, has come to this distress.

sentences.zh: 元顥新入，人情未安，今往討之，必有征無戰。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao has newly entered, and men's hearts are not yet settled; if you go now to attack him, there will surely be a campaign without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao has newly entered, and popular sentiment is not yet settled; if you go now to attack him, you will surely win without fighting.

sentences.zh: 王若克復京師，奉迎大駕，桓、文之舉也。

translations.literal: If my lord recovers the capital and welcomes back the imperial carriage, it will be an achievement like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.
translations.idiomatic: If my lord recovers the capital and welcomes back the imperial carriage, it will be an achievement like those of Duke Huan and Duke Wen.

sentences.zh: 舍此北度，竊為大王惜之。」

translations.literal: To abandon this and go north—I privately lament it for my lord.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this and go north—I must say I lament it for my lord.

sentences.zh: 天穆善之而不能用，遣子升還洛，顥以為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Tianmu approved of this but could not adopt it; he sent Zisheng back to Luoyang, and Hao appointed him Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu approved of this but could not adopt it; he sent Zisheng back to Luoyang, and Hao appointed him Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還宮，為顥任使者多被廢黜，而子升復為舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, many envoys who had served Hao were dismissed, but Zisheng again became Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the palace, many envoys who had served Hao were dismissed, but Zisheng again became Attendant.

sentences.zh: 天穆每謂子升曰：「恨不用卿前計。」

translations.literal: Tianmu often said to Zisheng: "I regret that I did not use your earlier plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tianmu often said to Zisheng, "I regret that I did not use your earlier plan.

sentences.zh: 除正員郎，仍舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Regular Attendant and still served as Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Regular Attendant while continuing as Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及帝殺爾硃榮也，子升預謀，當時赦詔，子升詞也。

translations.literal: When the emperor killed Erzhu Rong, Zisheng took part in the plot; the amnesty edict of the time was in Zisheng's wording.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor killed Erzhu Rong, Zisheng took part in the plot; the amnesty edict of the time was in Zisheng's wording.

sentences.zh: 榮入內，遇子升把詔書，問：「是何文字？」

translations.literal: When Rong entered the inner palace, he encountered Zisheng holding the edict and asked: "What writing is this?
translations.idiomatic: When Rong entered the inner palace, he encountered Zisheng holding the edict and asked, "What writing is this?

sentences.zh: 子升顏色不變，曰：「敕。」

translations.literal: Zisheng's countenance did not change, and he said: "An imperial order."
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng's countenance did not change, and he said, "An imperial order."

sentences.zh: 榮不視之。

translations.literal: Rong did not look at it.
translations.idiomatic: Rong did not look at it.

sentences.zh: 爾硃兆入洛，子升懼禍逃匿。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zisheng, fearing disaster, fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Zisheng, fearing disaster, fled and hid.

sentences.zh: 永熙中為侍讀，兼舍人、鎮南將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he became Lecturer-in-Waiting, and concurrently Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongxi era he became Lecturer-in-Waiting, and concurrently Attendant, General Who Pacifies the South, and Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、中軍大將軍，後領本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand General of the Central Army, and later headed the provincial chief rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Grand General of the Central Army, and later headed the provincial chief rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 梁使張皋寫子升文筆，傳于江外，梁武稱之曰：「曹植、陸機復生於北土，恨我辭人，數窮百六。」

translations.literal: The Liang envoy Zhang Gao copied out Zisheng's writings and transmitted them beyond the Yangtze; Emperor Wu of Liang praised them, saying: "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji have been reborn in the northern lands—I regret that our men of letters are so few in number.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang envoy Zhang Gao copied out Zisheng's writings and transmitted them beyond the Yangtze; Emperor Wu of Liang praised them, saying, "Cao Zhi and Lu Ji have been reborn in the northern lands—I regret that our men of letters are so few in number.

sentences.zh: 陽夏守傅摽使吐谷渾，見其國主床頭有書數卷，乃是子升文也。

translations.literal: Yangxia Prefect Fu Biao was sent on mission to the Tuyuhun; he saw several scrolls of books at the head of their ruler's couch, and they were Zisheng's writings.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxia Prefect Fu Biao was sent on mission to the Tuyuhun; he saw several scrolls of books at the head of their ruler's couch, and they were Zisheng's writings.

sentences.zh: 濟陰王暉業嘗云：「江左文人，宋有顏延之、謝靈運，梁有沈約、任昉，我子升足以陵顏轢謝，含任吐沈。」

translations.literal: Prince of Jiyin Huiye once said: "Among the men of letters south of the Yangtze, Song had Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, and Liang had Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng is enough to overleap Yan and trample Xie, to encompass Ren and surpass Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huiye of Jiyin once said, "Among writers south of the Yangtze, Song had Yan Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun, and Liang had Shen Yue and Ren Fang; our Zisheng is enough to surpass Yan and Xie and to outdo Ren and Shen.

sentences.zh: 楊遵彥作《文德論》，以為古今辭人皆負才遺行，澆薄險忌，唯邢子才、王元景、溫子升彬彬有德素。

translations.literal: Yang Zunyan wrote the "Discourse on Literary Virtue," holding that men of letters ancient and modern all possessed talent yet left behind misconduct, being shallow, thin, and dangerously jealous—only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were cultivated and possessed moral substance.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zunyan wrote the Discourse on Literary Virtue, holding that writers ancient and modern all possessed talent yet left misconduct behind, being shallow, dissolute, and dangerously jealous—only Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, and Wen Zisheng were cultivated and possessed moral substance.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄引子升為大將軍諮議。

translations.literal: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as staff adviser to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi summoned Zisheng as staff adviser to the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 子升前為中書郎，嘗詣梁客館受國書，自以不修容止，謂人曰：「詩章易作，逋峭難為。」

translations.literal: Zisheng had formerly been a Secretariat Gentleman and once went to the Liang guesthouse to receive the state letter; because he did not cultivate his bearing and appearance, he said to others: "Poems and essays are easy to compose; imposing presence is hard to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng had formerly been a Secretariat Gentleman and once went to the Liang guesthouse to receive the state letter; because he did not cultivate his bearing and appearance, he said to others, "Poems and essays are easy to compose; imposing presence is hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 文襄館客元僅曰：「諸人當賀，推子升合陳辭。」

translations.literal: Wenxiang's house guest Yuan Jin said: "Everyone should congratulate you—push Zisheng to deliver the Chen court's address."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang's house guest Yuan Jin said, "Everyone should congratulate you—have Zisheng deliver the Chen court's address."

sentences.zh: 子升久忸怩，乃推陸操焉。

translations.literal: Zisheng was long bashful and uneasy, and in the end pushed Lu Cao forward.
translations.idiomatic: Zisheng was long bashful and uneasy, and in the end pushed Lu Cao forward.

sentences.zh: 及元僅、劉思逸、荀濟等作亂，文襄疑子升知其謀。

translations.literal: When Yuan Jin, Liu Siyi, Xun Ji, and others made rebellion, Wenxiang suspected that Zisheng knew of their plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Jin, Liu Siyi, Xun Ji, and others rebelled, Wenxiang suspected that Zisheng knew of their plot.

sentences.zh: 方使之作《神武碑》。

translations.literal: He was just then having him compose the "Stele for Divine Might."
translations.idiomatic: He was just then having him compose the Stele for Divine Might.

sentences.zh: 文既成，乃餓諸晉陽獄，食弊襦而死。

translations.literal: When the text was finished, he starved him in the Jinyang prison, and he died eating worn-out trousers.
translations.idiomatic: When the text was finished, he starved him in the Jinyang prison, and he died after eating worn-out trousers.

sentences.zh: 棄屍路隅，沒其家口。

translations.literal: His corpse was cast by the roadside, and his household was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His corpse was cast by the roadside, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 太尉長史宋遊道收葬之，又為集其文筆為三十五卷。

translations.literal: Song Youdao, chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, gathered his body for burial and also collected his writings into thirty-five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao, chief clerk to the Grand Marshal, gathered his body for burial and also collected his writings into thirty-five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子升外恬靜，與物無競，言有准的，不妄毀譽。

translations.literal: Outwardly Zisheng was calm and still, not contending with others; in speech he had a standard and did not recklessly praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly Zisheng was calm and still and did not contend with others; in speech he had a standard and did not recklessly praise or blame.

sentences.zh: 而內深險，事故之際，好豫其間，所以終致禍敗。

translations.literal: Inwardly he was deeply treacherous; at times of sudden events he liked to insert himself among them, and for this reason in the end he met with ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly he was deeply treacherous; at times of crisis he liked to insert himself among them, and for this reason he met ruin in the end.

sentences.zh: 又撰《永安記》三卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled the "Record of Yong'an" in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Record of Yong'an in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 弟子盛，州主簿，有文才，年二十餘卒。

translations.literal: His disciple Sheng was a provincial registrar; he had literary talent and died in his twenties.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Sheng was a provincial registrar; he had literary talent and died in his twenties.

sentences.zh: 荀濟，字子通。

translations.literal: Xun Ji, courtesy name Zitong.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Ji, courtesy name Zitong.

sentences.zh: 其先潁川人，世居江左。

translations.literal: His ancestors were men of Yingchuan, and the family for generations resided in the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors were from Yingchuan, and the family had lived south of the Yangtze for generations.

sentences.zh: 濟初與梁武帝布衣交。

translations.literal: Ji at first was a commoner friend of Emperor Wu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ji at first was a commoner friend of Emperor Wu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 知梁武當王，然負氣不服，謂人曰：「會楯上磨墨作檄文。」

translations.literal: Knowing that Liang Wu would become king, yet proud and unwilling to submit, he said to others: "When the time comes I shall grind ink on the meeting shield to write a proclamation against him.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Liang Wu would become king, yet proud and unwilling to submit, he said to others, "When the time comes I shall grind ink on the meeting shield to write a proclamation against him.

sentences.zh: 或稱其才于梁武，梁武曰：「此人好亂者也。」

translations.literal: Someone praised his talent to Liang Wu, and Liang Wu said: "This man is one who loves disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Someone praised his talent to Liang Wu, and Liang Wu said, "This man is one who loves disorder."

sentences.zh: 濟又上書譏佛法，言營費太甚。

translations.literal: Ji again submitted a memorial mocking Buddhist teachings, saying that construction expenses were excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Ji again submitted a memorial mocking Buddhist teachings, saying that construction expenses were excessive.

sentences.zh: 梁武將誅之，遂奔魏，館于崔甗家。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang was about to execute him, he fled to Wei and lodged in the household of Cui Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang was about to execute him, he fled to Northern Wei and was housed in the home of Cui Yan.

sentences.zh: 及是見執。

translations.literal: At this juncture he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture he was seized.

sentences.zh: 楊愔音謂曰：「遲暮何為然？」

translations.literal: Yang Yin said to him with feeling, "In your twilight years, why act thus?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin said to him with feeling, "In your twilight years, why act thus?

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「叱叱，氣耳，何關遲暮！」

translations.literal: Ji said, "Tsk tsk—that is spirit alone; what has that to do with twilight years!
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Tsk tsk—that is spirit alone; what has that to do with twilight years!

sentences.zh: 乃下辯曰：「自傷年幾摧頹，恐功名不立。

translations.literal: Then he lowered his defense and said, "I grieve that my years are failing and fear that achievement and fame may never be established.
translations.idiomatic: Then he lowered his defense and said, "I grieve that my years are failing and fear that achievement and fame may never be established.

sentences.zh: 舍兒女之情，起風雲之事，故挾天子，誅權臣。」

translations.literal: Setting aside the bonds of wife and children, I raised great affairs amid wind and cloud; therefore I took the Son of Heaven in hand to execute powerful ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Setting aside the bonds of wife and children, I raised great affairs of state; therefore I took the Son of Heaven in hand to execute powerful ministers.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄惜其才，將不殺，親謂曰：「荀公何意反？」

translations.literal: Wenxiang of Qi prized his talent and was about to spare him. He asked him in person, "Lord Xun, what did you mean by rebelling?
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang of Qi prized his talent and was about to spare him. He asked him in person, "Lord Xun, what did you mean by rebelling?

sentences.zh: 濟曰：「奉詔誅將軍高澄，何為反！」

translations.literal: Ji said, "I received the edict to execute General Gao Cheng—how is that rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "I received the edict to execute General Gao Cheng—how is that rebellion!

sentences.zh: 於是燔殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was burned to death.

sentences.zh: 鄴下士大夫多傳濟音韻。

translations.literal: Many gentlemen and officials in Ye spread accounts of Ji's final words and tone.
translations.idiomatic: Many gentlemen and officials in Ye spread accounts of Ji's final words and tone.

sentences.zh: 祖鴻勳，涿郡范陽人也。

translations.literal: Zu Hongxun was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Hongxun was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 父慎，仕魏，曆雁門、咸陽二郡太守，政有能名。

translations.literal: His father Shen served Wei, successively as Administrator of Yanmen and Administrator of Xianyang; his governance won a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen served Wei, successively as Administrator of Yanmen and of Xianyang; his governance won a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 卒于金紫光祿大夫、贈中書監、幽州刺史，諡惠侯。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel, posthumously enfeoffed as Supervisor of the Secretariat and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Grand Master with Golden Seal and Purple Tassel, posthumously enfeoffed as Supervisor of the Secretariat and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Hui.

sentences.zh: 鴻勳弱冠，與同郡盧文符並為州主簿。

translations.literal: In his coming-of-age years Hongxun and Lu Wenfu of the same commandery together served as clerks of the province.
translations.idiomatic: In his coming-of-age years Hongxun and Lu Wenfu of the same commandery together served as clerks of the province.

sentences.zh: 僕射、臨淮王彧表薦其文學，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: The Minister Over the Masses and Prince of Huai'an, Yuan Shao, memorialized recommending him for literary attainment, and he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Over the Masses and Prince of Huai'an, Yuan Shao, memorialized recommending him for literary attainment, and he was appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「臨淮舉卿，竟不相謝，恐非其宜。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "The Prince of Huai'an recommended you, yet you never went to thank him—perhaps that is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "The Prince of Huai'an recommended you, yet you never went to thank him—perhaps that is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 鴻勳曰：「為國舉才，臨淮之務，祖鴻勳何事從而識之。」

translations.literal: Hongxun said, "Recommending talent for the state is the Prince of Huai'an's duty. What business has Zu Hongxun in going to acknowledge it.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun said, "Recommending talent for the state is the Prince of Huai'an's duty. What business has Zu Hongxun in going to acknowledge it.

sentences.zh: 彧聞而喜曰：「吾得其人矣。」

translations.literal: When Shao heard this he said with pleasure, "I have found my man.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao heard this he said with pleasure, "I have found my man.

sentences.zh: 後咸陽王徽奏鴻勳為司徒法曹參軍事。

translations.literal: Later Prince Xianyang, Yuan Hui, memorialized appointing Hongxun as Legal Affairs Attendant of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Xianyang, Yuan Hui, memorialized appointing Hongxun as Legal Affairs Attendant of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 及赴洛，徽謂曰：「臨淮相舉，竟不到門，今來何也？」

translations.literal: When he went to Luoyang, Hui said to him, "The Prince of Huai'an recommended you, yet you never came to my door—why have you come now?
translations.idiomatic: When he went to Luoyang, Hui said to him, "The Prince of Huai'an recommended you, yet you never came to my door—why have you come now?

sentences.zh: 鴻勳曰：「今來赴職，非為謝恩。」

translations.literal: Hongxun said, "I have come now to take up my post, not to offer thanks for favor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun said, "I have come now to take up my post, not to offer thanks for favor.

sentences.zh: 轉廷尉正，去官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Punishments in the Court of Justice, then left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of Punishments in the Court of Justice, then left office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 齊神武嘗徽至并州，作《晉祠記》，好事者玩其文。

translations.literal: When Northern Qi's Shenwu (Gao Huan) once had Hui come to Bingzhou, Hui composed "Record of the Jin Shrine"; connoisseurs admired his writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi's Shenwu (Gao Huan) once had Hui come to Bingzhou, Hui composed "Record of the Jin Shrine"; connoisseurs admired his writing.

sentences.zh: 位至高陽太守。

translations.literal: He rose to the post of Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 在官清素，妻子不免寒餒。

translations.literal: While in office he was pure and austere; his wife and children could not escape cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he was pure and austere; his wife and children could not escape cold and hunger.

sentences.zh: 時議高之。

translations.literal: Public opinion held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 李廣，字弘基，范陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Guang, courtesy name Hongji, was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guang, courtesy name Hongji, was a man of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 其先自遼東徙焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors had moved there from Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had moved there from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 廣博涉群書，有才思。

translations.literal: Guang widely studied many books and possessed literary talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Guang widely studied many books and possessed literary talent and thought.

sentences.zh: 少與趙郡李謇齊名，為邢、魏之亞，而訥於言，敏於行。

translations.literal: In youth he was as famous as Li Qian of Zhao commandery; he ranked just below Xing Lü and Wei Shou, yet was slow of speech and quick in action.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was as famous as Li Qian of Zhao commandery; he ranked just below Xing Lü and Wei Shou, yet was slow of speech and quick in action.

sentences.zh: 中尉崔暹精選御史，皆是世胃，廣獨以才學兼侍御史，修國史。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Cui Xian rigorously selected censors—all were sons of eminent houses; Guang alone, for talent and learning, was concurrently appointed Attending Censor and helped compile the national history.
