translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Cui Xian rigorously selected censors—all were sons of eminent houses; Guang alone, for talent and learning, was concurrently appointed Attending Censor and helped compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 南台文奏，多其辭也。

translations.literal: Documents of the Southern Administration were largely in his phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Documents of the Southern Administration were largely in his phrasing.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣初嗣霸業，命掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Qi Wenxuan succeeded the hegemonic enterprise, Guang was ordered to take charge of records.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning when Qi Wenxuan succeeded the hegemonic enterprise, Guang was ordered to take charge of records.

sentences.zh: 天保初，欲以為中書郎，遇其病篤而止。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao they wished to make him Secretariat Gentleman, but stopped when he fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao they wished to make him Secretariat Gentleman, but stopped when he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 廣嘗欲早朝，假寐，忽驚覺，謂其妻曰：「吾向似睡非睡，忽見一人出吾身中，語云：'君用心過苦，非精神所堪，今辭君去。

translations.literal: Guang once wished to attend court early and, feigning sleep, suddenly started awake. He told his wife, "Just now I seemed neither asleep nor awake, when suddenly I saw a man emerge from my body who said, 'Your mind works too bitterly; it is more than the spirit can bear. I now take my leave of you.
translations.idiomatic: Guang once wished to attend court early and, feigning sleep, suddenly started awake. He told his wife, "Just now I seemed neither asleep nor awake, when suddenly I saw a man emerge from my body who said, 'Your mind works too bitterly; it is more than the spirit can bear. I now take my leave of you.

sentences.zh: '」因而恍忽不樂，數日便遇疾，積年不起。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he grew dazed and unhappy; within days he fell ill and for years could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: ' Thereupon he grew dazed and unhappy; within days he fell ill and for years could not rise.

sentences.zh: 廣雅有鑒識，度量弘遠，坦率無私，為士流所愛，時共贍遺之，賴以自給。

translations.literal: Guang was by nature discerning and far-sighted in judgment, open and without selfishness, beloved among the gentry; they often sent him gifts, on which he relied to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was by nature discerning and far-sighted in judgment, open and without selfishness, beloved among the gentry; they often sent him gifts, on which he relied to support himself.

sentences.zh: 竟以疾終。

translations.literal: In the end he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 嘗薦畢義雲于崔暹。

translations.literal: He once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended Bi Yiyun to Cui Xian.

sentences.zh: 廣卒後，義雲集其文筆七卷，托魏收為之序。

translations.literal: After Guang died, Yiyun collected his writings in seven scrolls and entrusted Wei Shou to write the preface.
translations.idiomatic: After Guang died, Yiyun collected his writings in seven scrolls and entrusted Wei Shou to write the preface.

sentences.zh: 樊遜，字孝謙，河東北猗氏人也。

translations.literal: Fan Xun, courtesy name Xiaqian, was a man of Beiyi in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xun, courtesy name Xiaqian, was a man of Beiyi in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 祖琰、父衡，並無官宦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no official posts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yan and his father Heng both held no official posts.

sentences.zh: 而衡性至孝，喪父，負土成墳，植柏方數十畝，朝夕號慕。

translations.literal: Heng was deeply filial; when his father died he carried earth himself to make the tomb mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, mourning and calling out day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was deeply filial; when his father died he carried earth himself to make the tomb mound and planted cypresses over several tens of mu, mourning and calling out day and night.

sentences.zh: 遜少好學。

translations.literal: Xun loved learning from youth.
translations.idiomatic: Xun loved learning from youth.

sentences.zh: 其兄仲以造氈為業，亦常優饒之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Zhong made felt for a living and also often provided for him generously.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Zhong made felt for a living and also often provided for him generously.

sentences.zh: 遜自責曰：「為人弟，獨愛安逸，可不愧於心乎！

translations.literal: Xun blamed himself, saying, "As a younger brother I alone love ease and comfort—can I not feel shame before my own heart!
translations.idiomatic: Xun blamed himself, saying, "As a younger brother I alone love ease and comfort—can I not feel shame before my own heart!

sentences.zh: '欲同勤事業。

translations.literal: I wish to share in diligent work for the family enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to share in diligent work for the family enterprise.

sentences.zh: 母馮氏謂曰：「汝欲謹小行邪？」

translations.literal: His mother, Lady Feng, said, "Do you wish to be careful in small conduct?
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Feng, said, "Do you wish to be careful in small conduct?

sentences.zh: 遜感母言，遂專心典籍，恆書壁作「見賢思齊」四字以自勸。

translations.literal: Moved by his mother's words, Xun thereupon devoted himself to the classics, constantly writing on the wall the four characters "When you see the worthy, think to equal them" to urge himself on.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his mother's words, Xun thereupon devoted himself to the classics, constantly writing on the wall the four characters "When you see the worthy, think to equal them" to urge himself on.

sentences.zh: 遜貌醜陋，有才氣。

translations.literal: Xun was ugly in appearance yet possessed literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was ugly in appearance yet possessed literary talent.

sentences.zh: 屬本州淪陷，寓居鄴中，為臨漳小吏。

translations.literal: When his home province fell, he lodged in Ye and served as a petty clerk in Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When his home province fell, he lodged in Ye and served as a petty clerk in Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 縣令裴鑒蒞官清苦，致白雀等瑞。

translations.literal: The magistrate Pei Jian took office in pure austerity and brought forth auspicious signs such as white sparrows.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate Pei Jian took office in pure austerity and brought forth auspicious signs such as white sparrows.

sentences.zh: 遜上《清德頌》十首，鑒大加賞重，擢為主簿。

translations.literal: Xun submitted ten pieces of "Odes to Pure Virtue"; Jian greatly prized him and promoted him to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xun submitted ten pieces of "Odes to Pure Virtue"; Jian greatly prized him and promoted him to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 仍薦之於右僕射崔暹，與遼東李廣、勃海封孝琰等為暹賓客。

translations.literal: He also recommended him to the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Cui Xian; together with Li Guang of Liaodong, Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai, and others, Xun became a guest of Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended him to the Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Cui Xian; together with Li Guang of Liaodong, Feng Xiaoyan of Bohai, and others, Xun became a guest of Xian.

sentences.zh: 人有譏其靜默不能趨時者。

translations.literal: Some ridiculed him for his silence and inability to keep pace with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Some ridiculed him for his silence and inability to keep pace with the times.

sentences.zh: 遜常服東方朔之言：「陸沈世俗，避世金馬」，遂借陸沈公子為主人，擬《客難》制《客誨》以自廣。

translations.literal: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's words, "Sunk in the world yet above the world, avoiding the world in the Golden Horse Gate," and so borrowed the Sunken-in-the-World Gentleman as his host, modeling himself on "Guest's Difficulty" to compose "Guest's Admonition" to broaden himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun often took to heart Dongfang Shuo's words, "Sunk in the world yet above the world, avoiding the world in the Golden Horse Gate," and so borrowed the Sunken-in-the-World Gentleman as his host, modeling himself on "Guest's Difficulty" to compose "Guest's Admonition" to broaden himself.

sentences.zh: 後崔暹大會客，大司馬、襄城王旭時亦在坐，欲命府僚。

translations.literal: Later, when Cui Xian gave a great banquet for his guests, the Grand Marshal and Prince of Xiangcheng, Gao Xu, was also present and wished to appoint a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cui Xian gave a great banquet for his guests, the Grand Marshal and Prince of Xiangcheng, Gao Xu, was also present and wished to appoint a staff member.

sentences.zh: 暹指遜曰：「此人學富才高，兼之佳行，可為王參軍也。」

translations.literal: Xian pointed to Xun and said, "This man's learning is rich and his talent high; together with his fine conduct, he may serve as the prince's staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xian pointed to Xun and said, "This man's learning is rich and his talent high; together with his fine conduct, he may serve as the prince's staff officer.

sentences.zh: 旭目之曰：「豈能就耶？」

translations.literal: Xu looked at him and said, "How could one employ him?
translations.idiomatic: Xu looked at him and said, "How could one employ him?

sentences.zh: 遜曰：「家無廕第，不敢當此。」

translations.literal: Xun said, "My family has no hereditary privilege; I dare not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "My family has no hereditary privilege; I dare not accept this.

sentences.zh: 武定七年，齊文襄崩，暹為文宣徙于邊，賓客咸散，遜遂徙居陳留。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding, Wenxiang of Qi died; Xian was moved to the frontier by Wenxuan, and all his guests dispersed; Xun then moved to Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding, Wenxiang of Qi died; Xian was moved to the frontier by Wenxuan, and all his guests dispersed; Xun then moved to Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史劉殺鬼以遜兼錄事參軍事。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou, Liu Shagui, had Xun serve concurrently as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Liangzhou, Liu Shagui, had Xun serve concurrently as Recording Secretary.

sentences.zh: 遜仍舉秀才。

translations.literal: Xun then was nominated as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Xun then was nominated as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 尚書案舊令，下州三載一舉秀才，為三年已貢開封人鄭祖獻，計至此年未合。

translations.literal: According to old regulations of the Ministry of Works, each province presents one xiucai every three years; the previous cycle had already presented Zheng Zuxian of Kaifeng, so by the tally this year would not yet qualify.
translations.idiomatic: According to old regulations of the Ministry of Works, each province presents one xiucai every three years; the previous cycle had already presented Zheng Zuxian of Kaifeng, so by the tally this year would not yet qualify.

sentences.zh: 兼別駕王聰抗辭爭議，右丞陽斐不能卻。

translations.literal: The Acting Administrator Wang Cong argued in protest; the Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: The Acting Administrator Wang Cong argued in protest; the Right Assistant Director Yang Fei could not refute him.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高隆之曰：「雖遜才學優異，待明年非遠。」

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Longzhi said, "Though Xun's talent and learning are outstanding, waiting until next year is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Gao Longzhi said, "Though Xun's talent and learning are outstanding, waiting until next year is not far off.

sentences.zh: 遜竟還本州。

translations.literal: Xun in the end returned to his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Xun in the end returned to his home province.

sentences.zh: 天保元年，本州復召舉秀才。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianbao his home province again summoned him as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 三年春，會朝堂對策。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year they assembled at court for policy responses.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year they assembled at court for policy responses.

sentences.zh: 策罷，中書郎張子融奏入。

translations.literal: When the policy essays were finished, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized to submit them.
translations.idiomatic: When the policy essays were finished, Secretariat Gentleman Zhang Zirong memorialized to submit them.

sentences.zh: 至四年五月，遜與定州秀才李子宣等對策三年不調，被付外。

translations.literal: By the fifth month of the fourth year, Xun and the xiucai Li Zixuan of Dingzhou and others, who had presented policy essays yet received no appointment for three years, were assigned outside.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth month of the fourth year, Xun and the xiucai Li Zixuan of Dingzhou and others, who had presented policy essays yet received no appointment for three years, were assigned outside.

sentences.zh: 上書請從罷，詔不報。

translations.literal: They submitted memorials requesting release from service; the edict received no response.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted memorials requesting release from service; the edict received no response.

sentences.zh: 梁州重舉遜為秀才。

translations.literal: Liangzhou again nominated Xun as xiucai.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou again nominated Xun as xiucai.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，制詔問焉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year an imperial edict was issued to question them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year an imperial edict was issued to question them.

sentences.zh: 尚書擢第，以遜為當時第一。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Works ranked the candidates and placed Xun first for that year.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works ranked the candidates and placed Xun first for that year.

sentences.zh: 十二月，清河王嶽為大行台，率眾南討，以遜從軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue served as Grand Commissioner with Full Powers, leading troops south in campaign, and had Xun follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue served as Grand Commissioner with Full Powers, leading troops south in campaign, and had Xun follow the army.

sentences.zh: 明年，文宣納梁貞陽侯蕭明為梁主，嶽假遜大行台郎中，使于江南，與蕭脩、侯瑱和解。

translations.literal: The next year Wenxuan installed Marquis Zhenyang of Liang, Xiao Ming, as ruler of Liang; Yue provisionally appointed Xun as Gentleman of the Grand Commissioner and sent him to the lands south of the Yangtze to make peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Tian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wenxuan installed Marquis Zhenyang of Liang, Xiao Ming, as ruler of Liang; Yue provisionally appointed Xun as Gentleman of the Grand Commissioner and sent him to the lands south of the Yangtze to make peace with Xiao Xiu and Hou Tian.

sentences.zh: 遜往還五日，得脩等報書，嶽因與脩盟于江上。

translations.literal: Xun went and returned in five days with reply letters from Xiu and the others; Yue thereupon allied with Xiu on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xun went and returned in five days with reply letters from Xiu and the others; Yue thereupon allied with Xiu on the river.

sentences.zh: 大軍還鄴，遜仍被都官尚書崔昂舉薦。

translations.literal: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Minister of Justice Cui Ang.
translations.idiomatic: When the great army returned to Ye, Xun was again recommended by Minister of Justice Cui Ang.

sentences.zh: 詔付尚書，考為清平勤幹，送吏部。

translations.literal: An edict entrusted him to the Ministry of Works; he was assessed as pure, fair, diligent, and capable, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict entrusted him to the Ministry of Works; he was assessed as pure, fair, diligent, and capable, and sent to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔令校定群書，供皇太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year an edict ordered collation of the mass of books for the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict ordered collation of the mass of books for the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 遜與冀州秀才高乾和，瀛州秀才馬敬德、許散愁、韓同寶，洛州秀才傅懷德，懷州秀才古道子，廣平郡孝廉李漢子，勃海郡孝廉鮑長暄，陽平郡孝廉景孫，前梁州府主簿王九元、前開府水曹參軍周子深等十一人同被尚書召共刊定。

translations.literal: Xun, together with the xiucai Gao Qianhe of Jizhou; the xiucai Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, and Han Tongbao of Yingzhou; the xiucai Fu Huaide of Luozhou; the xiucai Gudao Zi of Huaizhou; the filial and incorrupt Li Hanzi of Guangping commandery; the filial and incorrupt Bao Changxuan of Bohai commandery; the filial and incorrupt Jing Sun of Yangping commandery; the former chief clerk of Liangzhou Wang Jiuyuan; and the former water bureau attendant of the Opening Office Zhou Zishen—eleven men in all—were together summoned by the Ministry of Works for joint collation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun, together with the xiucai Gao Qianhe of Jizhou; the xiucai Ma Jingde, Xu San'chou, and Han Tongbao of Yingzhou; the xiucai Fu Huaide of Luozhou; the xiucai Gudao Zi of Huaizhou; the filial and incorrupt Li Hanzi of Guangping commandery; the filial and incorrupt Bao Changxuan of Bohai commandery; the filial and incorrupt Jing Sun of Yangping commandery; the former chief clerk of Liangzhou Wang Jiuyuan; and the former water bureau attendant of the Opening Office Zhou Zishen—eleven men in all—were together summoned by the Ministry of Works for joint collation.

sentences.zh: 時秘府書籍紕繆者多，遜乃議曰：「案漢中壘校尉劉向受詔校書，每一書竟，表上，輒言臣向書、長水校尉臣參書、太常博士書、中外書合若干本，以相比校，然後殺青。

translations.literal: At the time many books in the secret repository were erroneous; Xun then proposed, saying, "According to the case of Han Central Fortress Commandant Liu Xiang, who received the edict to collate books: when each book was finished he memorialized upward, always stating the books of your subject Xiang, of Commandant of the Long Water Liu Can, of the Grand Master of Ceremonies's doctoral students, and of inner and outer copies—so many volumes in all—and compared them before making the final fair copy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many books in the secret repository were erroneous; Xun then proposed, saying, "According to the case of Han Central Fortress Commandant Liu Xiang, who received the edict to collate books: when each book was finished he memorialized upward, always stating the books of your subject Xiang, of Commandant of the Long Water Liu Can, of the Grand Master of Ceremonies's doctoral students, and of inner and outer copies—so many volumes in all—and compared them before making the final fair copy.

sentences.zh: 今所仇校，供擬極重，出自蘭台，禦諸甲館。

translations.literal: The collation now undertaken is prepared for the weightiest use, issued from the Orchid Terrace and for imperial viewing in the various armored halls.
translations.idiomatic: The collation now undertaken is prepared for the weightiest use, issued from the Orchid Terrace and for imperial viewing in the various armored halls.

sentences.zh: 向之故事，見存府閣。

translations.literal: Xiang's precedent is still preserved in the repository.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's precedent is still preserved in the repository.

sentences.zh: 即欲刊定，必藉眾本。

translations.literal: If we wish to collate and fix the text, we must rely on many copies.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish to collate and fix the text, we must rely on many copies.

sentences.zh: 太常卿邢子才、太子少傅魏收、吏部尚書辛術、司農少卿穆子容、前黃門郎司馬子瑞、故國子祭酒李業興並是多書之家，請牒借本參校。」

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Finance Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the National University Li Yexing are all households with many books; please issue documents to borrow copies for comparative collation.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Grand Master of Ceremonies Xing Zicai, Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince Wei Shou, Minister of Personnel Xin Shu, Vice Minister of Finance Mu Zirong, former Yellow Gate Gentleman Sima Zirui, and the late Director of the National University Li Yexing are all households with many books; please issue documents to borrow copies for comparative collation.

sentences.zh: 秘書監尉瑾移尚書都坐，凡所得別本三千餘卷。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Yu Jin forwarded the matter to the chief seat of the Ministry of Works; in all they obtained more than three thousand scrolls of separate copies.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Yu Jin forwarded the matter to the chief seat of the Ministry of Works; in all they obtained more than three thousand scrolls of separate copies.

sentences.zh: 《五經》諸史殆無遺闕。

translations.literal: The Five Classics and the various histories were nearly without omission or lack.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Classics and the various histories were nearly without omission or lack.

sentences.zh: 于時魏收作《庫狄幹碑序》，令孝謙為之銘，陸仰不知，以為收合作也。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Shou composed the preface to the "Stele of Kudigan Gan" and had Xiaqian write the inscription; Lu Yang did not know this and thought it was a joint work of Shou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Shou composed the preface to the "Stele of Kudigan Gan" and had Xiaqian write the inscription; Lu Yang did not know this and thought it was a joint work of Shou.

sentences.zh: 陸操、伏渾卒，楊愔使孝謙代己作書以告晉陽朝士，令魏潤色之，收不能改一字。

translations.literal: When Lu Cao and Fu Hun died, Yang Yin had Xiaqian draft letters in his stead to inform the court gentlemen at Jinyang and had Wei polish them; Shou could not change a single character.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Cao and Fu Hun died, Yang Yin had Xiaqian draft letters in his stead to inform the court gentlemen at Jinyang and had Wei polish them; Shou could not change a single character.

sentences.zh: 八年，減東西二省官，更定選，員不過三百，參者二三千人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the offices of the Eastern and Western Provinces were reduced and selections were redefined; posts did not exceed three hundred, while those competing numbered two or three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the offices of the Eastern and Western Provinces were reduced and selections were redefined; posts did not exceed three hundred, while those competing numbered two or three thousand.

sentences.zh: 楊愔言於眾曰：「後生清俊，莫過盧思道；

translations.literal: Yang Yin said to the assembly, "Among the clear and talented of the younger generation, none surpasses Lu Sidao;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin said to the assembly, "Among the clear and talented of the younger generation, none surpasses Lu Sidao;

sentences.zh: 文章成就，莫過樊孝謙；

translations.literal: for literary achievement completed, none surpasses Fan Xiaqian;
translations.idiomatic: for literary achievement completed, none surpasses Fan Xiaqian;

sentences.zh: 几案斷割，莫過崔成之。」

translations.literal: for decisive handling at the desk, none surpasses Cui Chengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: for decisive handling at the desk, none surpasses Cui Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 遂以思道長兼員外郎，三人並員外將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sidao was appointed acting Secretariat Gentleman with extended tenure, and all three were appointed Acting General of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Sidao was appointed acting Secretariat Gentleman with extended tenure, and all three were appointed Acting General of the Household.

sentences.zh: 孝謙辭曰：「門族寒陋，訪第必不成，乞補員外司馬督。」

translations.literal: Xiaqian declined, saying, "My clan is poor and lowly; seeking a grade will surely fail—I beg to be appointed Acting Supervisor of the Household Cavalry instead.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaqian declined, saying, "My clan is poor and lowly; seeking a grade will surely fail—I beg to be appointed Acting Supervisor of the Household Cavalry instead.

sentences.zh: 愔曰：「才高不依常例。」

translations.literal: Yin said, "When talent is high, one need not follow ordinary precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "When talent is high, one need not follow ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 特奏用之。

translations.literal: He specially memorialized and had him appointed.
translations.idiomatic: He specially memorialized and had him appointed.

sentences.zh: 清河初，為主書，參典詔策。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qinghe reign he served as Master of Documents and assisted in drafting edicts and policies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qinghe reign he served as Master of Documents and assisted in drafting edicts and policies.

sentences.zh: 天統元年，加員外郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong he was additionally appointed Acting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiantong he was additionally appointed Acting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 居七八日，行過轜車，嚬眉下淚，指方相曰：「何日更相煩君一到？」

translations.literal: After seven or eight days, as he was walking he passed a hearse; he knit his brows and shed tears, pointed at the exorcist and said, "On what day will I trouble you to come again?
translations.idiomatic: After seven or eight days, as he was walking he passed a hearse; he knit his brows and shed tears, pointed at the exorcist and said, "On what day will I trouble you to come again?

sentences.zh: 數日而卒，雇方相送葬，仍前所逢者。

translations.literal: Within several days he died; he hired the exorcist to conduct the funeral—it was the same man he had met before.
translations.idiomatic: Within several days he died; he hired the exorcist to conduct the funeral—it was the same man he had met before.

sentences.zh: 孝謙死後，定州秀才荀士遜繼為主書，才名相亞。

translations.literal: After Xiaqian's death, the xiucai Xun Shixun of Dingzhou succeeded him as Master of Documents; their talent and fame were nearly equal.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaqian's death, the xiucai Xun Shixun of Dingzhou succeeded him as Master of Documents; their talent and fame were nearly equal.

sentences.zh: 茹瞻字孝博，東安人。

translations.literal: Ru Zhan, courtesy name Xiaobo, was a man of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Zhan, courtesy name Xiaobo, was a man of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 南州舉秀才。

translations.literal: He was recommended as xiucai in Nanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as xiucai in Nanzhou.

sentences.zh: 清朗剛直。

translations.literal: He was clear, bright, and uprightly firm.
translations.idiomatic: He was clear-minded, upright, and firm in character.

sentences.zh: 楊愔將用之，曰：「今日之選，不可無茹生。」

translations.literal: Yang Yin was about to employ him and said, "In today's selection, we cannot do without Master Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin was about to employ him and said, "In today's selection, we cannot do without Master Ru.

sentences.zh: 卒于侍御史。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 荀士遜，廣平人也。

translations.literal: Xun Shixun was a man of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Shixun was a man of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 好學，有思理，為文清典，見賞知音。

translations.literal: He loved learning, possessed reflective judgment, and wrote in a pure and canonical style; he was appreciated by those who understood him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning, possessed reflective judgment, and wrote in a pure and canonical style; he was appreciated by connoisseurs.

sentences.zh: 武定末，舉司州秀才，迄齊天保，十年不調。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was recommended as xiucai of Sizhou; through Northern Qi's Tianbao reign he received no appointment for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was recommended as xiucai of Sizhou; through Northern Qi's Tianbao reign he received no appointment for ten years.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，馬敬德薦為主書，轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: During Huangjian, Ma Jingde recommended him as Master of Documents; he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangjian, Ma Jingde recommended him as Master of Documents; he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 狀貌甚醜，以文辭見重。

translations.literal: His appearance was very ugly, but he was esteemed for his literary skill.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was very ugly, but he was esteemed for his literary skill.

sentences.zh: 嘗有事須奏，遇武成在後庭，因左右傳通，傳通者不得士遜姓名，乃云「醜舍人」。

translations.literal: Once when he had business requiring memorial, he encountered Wucheng in the rear court; he had an attendant relay the message, but the relay could not obtain Shixun's name and so said "the ugly drafter."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he had business requiring a memorial, he encountered Emperor Wucheng in the rear court; he had an attendant relay the message, but the relay did not know Shixun's name and so said "the ugly drafter."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「必士遜也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It must be Shixun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "It must be Shixun.

sentences.zh: 看封題果是，內人莫不歡笑。

translations.literal: When he looked at the cover and title it was indeed so, and everyone inside laughed.
translations.idiomatic: When he looked at the cover and title it was indeed so, and everyone present laughed.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎，號為稱職。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Secretariat Vice Director and was known as competent in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Secretariat Vice Director and was known as competent in office.

sentences.zh: 與李若等撰《典言》，行於世。

translations.literal: Together with Li Ruo and others he compiled the 《Dianyan》; it circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Li Ruo and others he compiled the 《Dianyan》, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 齊亡年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the year Qi perished.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the year Northern Qi fell.

sentences.zh: 王褒，字子深，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, courtesy name Zishen, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, courtesy name Zishen, was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 曾祖儉、祖騫、父規，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jian, grandfather Qian, and father Gui all have biographies in the 《History of the Southern Dynasties》.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jian, grandfather Qian, and father Gui all have biographies in the 《History of the Southern Dynasties》.

sentences.zh: 褒識量淹通，志懷沈靜，美威儀，善談笑，博覽史傳，七歲能屬文。

translations.literal: Bao's knowledge was broad and penetrating, his aims serene and quiet; he had fine bearing and presence, was skilled in conversation and wit, read widely in histories and traditions, and at seven could compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's knowledge was broad and penetrating, his temperament serene and quiet; he had fine bearing and presence, was skilled in conversation and wit, read widely in histories and traditions, and at seven could compose prose.

sentences.zh: 外祖梁司空袁昂愛之，謂賓客曰：「此兒當成吾宅相。」

translations.literal: His maternal grandfather, Liang's Minister of Works Yuan Ang, loved him and said to guests, "This boy will become the glory of our house.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandfather, Liang's Minister of Works Yuan Ang, loved him and said to guests, "This boy will become the glory of our house.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，除秘書郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: At twenty he was recommended as xiucai and appointed Secretariat Gentleman and Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was recommended as xiucai and appointed Secretariat Gentleman and Crown Prince Attendant.

sentences.zh: 梁國子祭酒蕭子雲，褒之姑夫也，特善草隸。

translations.literal: Xiao Ziyun, Libationer of the National University of Liang, was Bao's uncle by marriage and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Ziyun, Libationer of the National University of Liang, was Bao's uncle by marriage and was especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 褒少以姻戚，去來其家，遂相模範，而名亞子雲，並見重于時。

translations.literal: Bao in youth, through kinship, went back and forth to his house and thus took him as a model; his fame was second to Ziyun's, and both were highly regarded in their time.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Bao, through this kinship, frequented his household and took him as a model; his fame was second only to Ziyun's, and both were highly regarded in their time.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉其才藝，遂以弟鄱陽王恢女妻之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu admired his talent and art and thereupon gave him in marriage the daughter of his younger brother, Prince Hui of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his talent and art and thereupon gave him in marriage the daughter of his younger brother, Prince Hui of Poyang.

sentences.zh: 襲爵南昌縣侯，歷位秘書丞、宣城王文學、安城內史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Marquis of Nanchang county and successively held the posts of Secretariat Assistant, Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, and Administrator of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Marquis of Nanchang county and successively held the posts of Secretariat Assistant, Literary Scholar to the Prince of Xuancheng, and Administrator of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 及侯景陷建鄴，褒輯寧所部，見稱于時。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took Jiankang, Bao gathered and pacified his district and was praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Jiankang, Bao gathered and pacified his district and was praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 轉南平內史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝嗣位，褒有舊，召拜吏部尚書、右僕射，仍遷左丞，兼參掌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang succeeded to the throne, Bao had old ties with him and was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel and Vice Director of the Left, then transferred to Left Assistant and concurrently given a share in administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang succeeded to the throne, Bao had old ties with him and was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel and Vice Director of the Left, then transferred to Left Assistant with a concurrent share in administration.

sentences.zh: 褒既名家，文學優贍，當時咸共推挹，故位望隆重，寵遇日甚。

translations.literal: Bao being of an eminent house and richly endowed in letters, all in his time jointly honored and esteemed him; thus his position and repute were weighty and imperial favor grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Bao being of an eminent house and richly endowed in letters, all in his time honored and esteemed him; thus his position and repute were weighty and imperial favor grew daily.

sentences.zh: 而愈自謙損，不以位地矜物，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Yet he became all the more self-restrained and humble, not treating others with arrogance because of rank and status; contemporary opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he became all the more self-restrained and humble, not treating others with arrogance because of rank and status; contemporary opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 初，元帝平侯景及禽武陵王紀後，以建鄴凋殘，時江陵殷盛，便欲安之。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing and captured Prince Ji of Wuling, because Jiankang was devastated while Jiangling at the time was flourishing, he wished to settle the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Emperor Yuan pacified Hou Jing and captured Prince Ji of Wuling, because Jiankang was devastated while Jiangling at the time was flourishing, he wished to move the capital there.

sentences.zh: 又其政府臣僚皆楚人也，並願即都鄢郢。

translations.literal: Moreover the officials of his government were all men of Chu and together wished to establish the capital immediately at Yan and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the officials of his government were all men of Chu and together wished to establish the capital immediately at Yan and Ying.

sentences.zh: 嘗召群臣議之。

translations.literal: He once summoned the ministers to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: He once summoned the ministers to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍胡僧祐、吏部尚書宗懍、太府卿黃羅漢、御史中丞劉玨等曰：「建鄴王氣已盡，又荊南地又有天子氣，遷徙非宜。」

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the Army Hu Sengyou, Minister of Personnel Zong Lin, Grand Steward Huang Luohan, Imperial Censor Liu Jue, and others said, "The royal aura of Jiankang is already exhausted, and moreover in the land south of Jing there is again the aura of an emperor; relocation is not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Pacifies the Army Hu Sengyou, Minister of Personnel Zong Lin, Grand Steward Huang Luohan, Imperial Censor Liu Jue, and others said, "The royal aura of Jiankang is already exhausted, and moreover the land south of Jing again bears the aura of an emperor; relocation is not fitting.

sentences.zh: 元帝深以為然。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 褒性謹慎，知元帝多猜忌，弗敢公言其非。

translations.literal: Bao by nature was cautious; knowing that Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion, he did not dare openly speak against it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao by nature was cautious; knowing that Emperor Yuan was much given to suspicion, he did not dare openly speak against it.

sentences.zh: 後因清閒，密諫，言辭甚切。

translations.literal: Later, taking advantage of a quiet moment, he remonstrated in secret; his words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Later, taking advantage of a quiet moment, he remonstrated in secret; his words were very earnest.

sentences.zh: 元帝意好荊楚，已從僧祐等策，竟不用。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan's inclination favored Jing and Chu; he had already followed the plan of Sengyou and the others and in the end did not adopt Bao's advice.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan's inclination favored Jing and Chu; he had already followed the plan of Sengyou and the others and in the end did not adopt Bao's advice.

sentences.zh: 及魏征江陵，元帝授褒都督城西諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Jiangling, Emperor Yuan entrusted Bao with overall command of military affairs west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei attacked Jiangling, Emperor Yuan entrusted Bao with overall command of military affairs west of the city.

sentences.zh: 柵破，從元帝入金城。

translations.literal: When the palisade was breached, he followed Emperor Yuan into the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: When the palisade was breached, he followed Emperor Yuan into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 俄而元帝出降，褒遂與眾俱出，見柱國於謹，甚禮之。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Yuan came out to surrender; Bao then went out together with the multitude and met the Pillar of State Yu Jin, who treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Yuan came out to surrender; Bao then went out together with the multitude and met the Pillar of State Yu Jin, who treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 褒曾作《燕歌》，妙盡塞北寒苦之狀，元帝及諸文士並和之，而競為淒切之辭，至此方驗焉。

translations.literal: Bao had once composed the 《Yan Song》, wonderfully exhausting the image of the cold and hardship north of the passes; Emperor Yuan and the various men of letters all harmonized with it, competing in plaintive language—only now was it verified.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had once composed the 《Yan Song》, wonderfully capturing the cold and hardship north of the passes; Emperor Yuan and the various men of letters all harmonized with it, competing in plaintive language—only now was it verified.

sentences.zh: 褒與王克、劉玨、宗懍、殷不害等數十人俱至長安，周文喜曰：「昔平吳之利，二陸而已；

translations.literal: Bao, together with Wang Ke, Liu Jue, Zong Lin, Yin Buhai, and several tens of others, all arrived at Chang'an; Zhou Wen said with delight, "In old times the profit of pacifying Wu was only the two Lus;
translations.idiomatic: Bao, together with Wang Ke, Liu Jue, Zong Lin, Yin Buhai, and several tens of others, all arrived at Chang'an; Zhou Wen said with delight, "In old times the profit of pacifying Wu was only the two Lus;

sentences.zh: 今定楚之功，群賢畢至，可謂過之矣。」

translations.literal: now in settling the achievement over Chu, all the worthy have arrived—it may be said to surpass that.
translations.idiomatic: now in settling the achievement over Chu, all the worthy have arrived—it may be said to surpass that.

sentences.zh: 又謂褒及王克曰：「吾即王氏甥也，卿等並吾之舅氏，當以親戚為情，勿以去鄉介意。」

translations.literal: He also said to Bao and Wang Ke, "I am myself a nephew of the Wang clan; you are all my uncles by marriage—you should treat kinship as feeling and not take leaving your homeland to heart.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Bao and Wang Ke, "I am myself a nephew of the Wang clan; you are all my uncles by marriage—you should treat kinship as feeling and not take leaving your homeland to heart.

sentences.zh: 於是授褒及殷不害等車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed Bao and Yin Buhai and others General of Chariots and Cavalry and Senior Grand Master of the Palace with Honored Standing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he appointed Bao and Yin Buhai and others General of Chariots and Cavalry and Senior Grand Master of the Palace with Honored Standing.

sentences.zh: 常從容上席，資餼甚厚。

translations.literal: He was often at ease in the upper seat; provisions and gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was often given the seat of honor at ease; provisions and gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 褒等亦並荷恩眄，忘羈旅焉。

translations.literal: Bao and the others likewise all received gracious favor and forgot they were travelers far from home.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and the others likewise all received gracious favor and forgot they were travelers far from home.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，封石泉縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Bao was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Bao was enfeoffed as Viscount of Shiquan county.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，篤好文學，時褒與庾信才名最高，特加親待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming succeeded, he was ardently fond of letters; at the time Bao and Yu Xin had the highest fame for talent and received special intimate treatment.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming succeeded, he was ardently fond of letters; at the time Bao and Yu Xin had the highest fame for talent and received special intimate treatment.

sentences.zh: 帝每遊宴，命褒賦詩談論，恆在左右。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on excursions or banquets, he ordered Bao to compose poetry and discuss matters; he was constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on excursions or banquets, he ordered Bao to compose poetry and discuss matters; he was constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally given the title Opening Office with Honored Standing of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally given the title Opening Office with Honored Standing of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 保定中，除內史中大夫。

translations.literal: During Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During Baoding he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝作《象經》，令褒注之，引據該洽，甚見稱賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu composed the 《Xiangjing》 and had Bao annotate it; his citations were comprehensive and apt, and he was greatly praised and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu composed the 《Xiangjing》 and had Bao annotate it; his citations were comprehensive and apt, and he was greatly praised and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 褒有器局，雅識政體，既累世在江東為宰輔，帝亦以此重之。

translations.literal: Bao had capacity and breadth of vision and finely understood the substance of government; since for generations his family had been chief ministers in the Jiangdong region, the emperor also valued him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao had capacity and breadth of vision and finely understood the substance of government; since for generations his family had been chief ministers in the Jiangdong region, the emperor also valued him for this.

sentences.zh: 建德以後，頗參朝議，凡大詔冊，皆令褒具草。

translations.literal: After Jiande he participated considerably in court deliberations; for all great edicts and patent letters, Bao was ordered to draft them.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiande he participated considerably in court deliberations; for all great edicts and patent letters, Bao was ordered to draft them.

sentences.zh: 東宮既建，授太子少保，遷少司空，仍掌綸誥。

translations.literal: Once the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, promoted to Junior Minister of Works, and still directed imperial rescripts.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince, promoted to Junior Minister of Works, and still directed imperial rescripts.

sentences.zh: 乘輿行幸，褒常侍從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went on progress, Bao constantly attended and followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went on progress, Bao constantly attended and followed.

sentences.zh: 初，褒與梁處士汝南周弘讓相善，及讓兄弘正自陳來聘，帝許褒等通親知音問，褒贈弘讓詩並書焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Bao was on good terms with the reclusive gentleman of Liang, Zhou Hongrang of Runan; when Hongrang's elder brother Hongzheng came on an embassy from Chen, the emperor permitted Bao and others to communicate with kin and friends and exchange greetings; Bao presented Hongrang with a poem and a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bao was on good terms with the reclusive gentleman of Liang, Zhou Hongrang of Runan; when Hongrang's elder brother Hongzheng came on an embassy from Chen, the emperor permitted Bao and others to communicate with kin and friends and exchange greetings; Bao presented Hongrang with a poem and a letter.

sentences.zh: 尋出為宜州刺史，卒于位。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Yizhou and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as Governor of Yizhou and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子鼒。

translations.literal: His son was Zi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Zi.

sentences.zh: 庾信，字子山，南陽新野人。

translations.literal: Yu Xin, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Xinye in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xin, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Xinye in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖易、父肩吾，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi and father Jianwu both have biographies in the 《History of the Southern Dynasties》.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi and father Jianwu both have biographies in the 《History of the Southern Dynasties》.

sentences.zh: 信幼而俊邁，聰敏絕倫，博覽群書，尤善《春秋左氏傳》。

translations.literal: Xin in youth was outstanding and surpassing, intelligent and keen beyond comparison; he read widely among all books and was especially skilled in the 《Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals》.
translations.idiomatic: Xin in youth was outstanding and surpassing, intelligent and keen beyond comparison; he read widely among all books and was especially skilled in the 《Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals》.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，腰帶十圍，容止頹然，有過人者。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi in height, his waist belt ten wei in girth; his bearing and deportment were lofty, with qualities surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi in height, with a waist belt ten wei in girth; his bearing and deportment were lofty, with qualities surpassing others.

sentences.zh: 父肩吾，為梁太子中庶子，掌管記。

translations.literal: His father Jianwu served as Crown Prince Senior Attendant of Liang and directed the secretariat records.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianwu served as Crown Prince Senior Attendant of Liang and directed the secretariat records.

sentences.zh: 東海徐摛為右衛率。

translations.literal: Xu Chi of Donghai served as Commander of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chi of Donghai served as Commander of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 摛子陵及信並為抄撰學士。

translations.literal: Chi's son Ling and Xin both served as drafting scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's son Ling and Xin both served as drafting scholars.

sentences.zh: 父子東宮，出入禁闥，恩禮莫與比靈斯。

translations.literal: Father and sons in the Eastern Palace, entering and leaving the forbidden gates, in favor shown none could compare.
translations.idiomatic: Father and sons served in the Eastern Palace, entering and leaving the forbidden gates; in favor shown none could compare.

sentences.zh: 既文並綺豔，故世號為徐、庾體焉。

translations.literal: Since their writing was alike in ornate brilliance, the age therefore styled it the Xu and Yu manner.
translations.idiomatic: Since their writing was alike in ornate brilliance, the age therefore styled it the Xu and Yu manner.

sentences.zh: 當時後進，競相模範，每有一文，都下莫不傳誦。

translations.literal: The younger generation of the time competed to take them as models; whenever there was a new piece, none in the capital failed to pass it around and recite it.
translations.idiomatic: The younger generation of the time competed to take them as models; whenever there was a new piece, none in the capital failed to pass it around and recite it.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直散騎常侍，聘於東魏。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and was sent on embassy to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and was sent on embassy to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 文章辭令，盛為鄴下所稱。

translations.literal: His essays and diplomatic letters were greatly praised in Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His essays and diplomatic letters were greatly praised in Ye.

sentences.zh: 還為東宮學士，領建康令。

translations.literal: On his return he became an Eastern Palace scholar and concurrently served as Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became an Eastern Palace scholar and concurrently served as Magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 侯景作亂，梁簡文帝命信率宮中文武千餘人營於硃雀航。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing raised rebellion, Emperor Jianwen of Liang ordered Xin to lead more than a thousand civil and military officials of the palace to encamp at the Vermilion Bird ford.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing raised rebellion, Emperor Jianwen of Liang ordered Xin to lead more than a thousand civil and military officials of the palace to encamp at the Vermilion Bird ford.

sentences.zh: 及景至，信以眾先退。

translations.literal: When Jing arrived, Xin with his troops withdrew first.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing arrived, Xin with his troops withdrew first.

sentences.zh: 台城陷後，信奔於江陵。

translations.literal: After the capital fell, Xin fled to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital fell, Xin fled to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝承制，除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency and appointed him Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang assumed the regency and appointed him Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 及即位，轉右衛將軍，封武康縣侯，加散騎侍郎，聘于西魏。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Xin was transferred to General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang county, given the additional post of Cavalier Attendant, and sent on embassy to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Xin was transferred to General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Marquis of Wukang county, given the additional post of Cavalier Attendant, and sent on embassy to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 屬大軍南討，遂留長安。

translations.literal: As the great army marched south on campaign, he was detained in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: As the great army marched south on campaign, he was detained in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，累遷儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, he was promoted in succession to Honored Standing of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, he was promoted in succession to Honored Standing of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，封臨清縣子，除司水下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linqing county and appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Water Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linqing county and appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Water Affairs.

sentences.zh: 出為弘農郡守。

translations.literal: He went out as Administrator of Hongnong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Administrator of Hongnong commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、司憲中大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Opening Office with Honored Standing of the Third Rank, and Grand Master of the Palace for Law.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Opening Office with Honored Standing of the Third Rank, and Grand Master of the Palace for Law.

sentences.zh: 進爵義城縣侯。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to Marquis of Yicheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in rank to Marquis of Yicheng county.

sentences.zh: 俄拜洛州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 信為政簡靜，吏人安之。

translations.literal: Xin's administration was simple and quiet; officials and people were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's administration was simple and quiet; officials and people were at ease under him.

sentences.zh: 時陳氏與周通好，南北流寓之士，各許還其舊國。

translations.literal: At the time Chen and Zhou were on friendly terms; scholars sojourning north and south were each permitted to return to their former states.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chen and Zhou were on friendly terms; scholars sojourning north and south were each permitted to return to their former states.

sentences.zh: 陳氏乃請王褒及信等十數人。

translations.literal: Chen thereupon requested Wang Bao and Xin and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: Chen thereupon requested Wang Bao and Xin and more than ten others.

sentences.zh: 武帝唯放王克、殷不害等，信及褒並惜而不遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu only released Wang Ke, Yin Buhai, and others; as for Xin and Bao, he cherished them and would not send them away.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu only released Wang Ke, Yin Buhai, and others; as for Xin and Bao, he cherished them and would not send them away.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為司宗中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace for the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Grand Master of the Palace for the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 明帝、武帝並雅好文學，信特蒙恩禮。

translations.literal: Emperors Ming and Wu were both elegantly fond of letters; Xin especially received gracious favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperors Ming and Wu were both elegantly fond of letters; Xin especially received gracious favor.

sentences.zh: 至於趙、滕諸王，周旋款至，有若布衣之交。

translations.literal: As for the princes of Zhao, Teng, and the rest, he moved among them with warm sincerity, as if the friendship of common cloth.
translations.idiomatic: As for the princes of Zhao, Teng, and the rest, he moved among them with warm sincerity, as if the friendship of commoners.

sentences.zh: 群公碑誌，多相托焉。

translations.literal: The steles and epitaphs of the great lords mostly entrusted these to him.
translations.idiomatic: The steles and epitaphs of the great lords mostly entrusted these to him.

sentences.zh: 唯王褒頗與信埒，自余文人，莫有逮者。

translations.literal: Only Wang Bao was nearly equal to Xin; among the other men of letters, none could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Bao was nearly equal to Xin; among the other men of letters, none could match him.

sentences.zh: 信雖位望通顯，常作鄉關之思，乃作《哀江南賦》以致其意。

translations.literal: Though Xin's position and repute were eminent, he often thought of his homeland and therefore composed the "Lament for Jiangnan" to express his feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xin's position and repute were eminent, he often thought of his homeland and therefore composed the "Lament for Jiangnan" to express his feeling.

sentences.zh: 大象初，以疾去職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang he resigned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daxiang he resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Sui's Kaihuang reign.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Sui's Kaihuang reign.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 文帝悼之，贈本官，加荊、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen mourned him, granted his former office posthumously, and added the posts of Governor of Jing and of Yong provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen mourned him, granted his former office posthumously, and added the posts of Governor of Jing and of Yong provinces.

sentences.zh: 子立嗣。

translations.literal: His son Li succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li succeeded.

sentences.zh: 顏之推，字介，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Zhitui, courtesy name Jie, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhitui, courtesy name Jie, was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖見遠、父協，並以義烈稱。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jianyuan and father Xie were both famed for righteous valor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jianyuan and father Xie were both famed for righteous valor.

sentences.zh: 世善《周官》、《左氏》學，俱《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: For generations the family excelled in the learning of the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo tradition; all have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family excelled in the learning of the Offices of Zhou and the Zuo tradition; all have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 之推年十二，遇梁湘東王自講《莊》、《老》，之推便預門徒。

translations.literal: When Zhitui was twelve, he encountered the Prince of Xiangdong of Liang lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi himself; Zhitui at once joined the disciples.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhitui was twelve, he encountered the Prince of Xiangdong of Liang lecturing on the Zhuangzi and Laozi himself; Zhitui at once joined the disciples.

sentences.zh: 虛談非其所好，還習《禮》、《傳》。

translations.literal: Empty talk was not to his liking; he returned to study the Rites and the Traditions.
translations.idiomatic: Empty talk was not to his liking; he returned to study the Rites and the Traditions.

sentences.zh: 博覽書史，無不該洽，辭情典麗，甚為西府所稱。

translations.literal: He read widely in books and histories, mastering all without exception; his literary style was canonical and beautiful, and he was greatly praised by the Western Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in books and histories, mastering all without exception; his literary style was canonical and beautiful, and he was greatly praised by the Western Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 湘東王以為其國右常侍，加鎮西墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Xiangdong appointed him Regular Attendant of the Right in his princedom and additionally made him Ink Bureau Attendant of the Army Pacifying the West.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xiangdong appointed him Regular Attendant of the Right in his princedom and additionally made him Ink Bureau Attendant of the Army Pacifying the West.

sentences.zh: 好飲酒，多任縱，不修邊幅，時論以此少之。

translations.literal: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep up appearances; contemporary opinion therefore thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, was much given to license, and did not keep up appearances; contemporary opinion therefore thought less of him.

sentences.zh: 湘東遣世子方諸鎮郢州，以之推為中撫軍府外兵參軍，掌管記。

translations.literal: Xiangdong sent his heir Fangzhu to garrison Yingzhou and appointed Zhitui External Military Attendant of the Central Pacifying Army Headquarters, in charge of secretariat records.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangdong sent his heir Fangzhu to garrison Yingzhou and appointed Zhitui External Military Attendant of the Central Pacifying Army Headquarters, in charge of secretariat records.

sentences.zh: 遇侯景陷郢州，頻欲殺之，賴其行台郎中王則以免。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou, he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, Attendant of the Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing took Yingzhou, he repeatedly wished to kill him; he was spared thanks to Wang Ze, Attendant of the Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 景平，還江陵。

translations.literal: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing was pacified, he returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 時湘東即位，以之推為散騎侍郎，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: When Xiangdong took the throne, he appointed Zhitui Cavalier Attendant and gave him the duties of a Memorial Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangdong took the throne, he appointed Zhitui Cavalier Attendant and gave him the duties of a Memorial Drafter.

sentences.zh: 後為周軍所破，大將軍李穆重之，送往弘農，令掌其兄陽平公遠書翰。

translations.literal: Later, when they were defeated by the Zhou army, the Great General Li Mu valued him and sent him to Hongnong, ordering him to manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when they were defeated by the Zhou army, the Great General Li Mu valued him and sent him to Hongnong, ordering him to manage the correspondence of his elder brother, the Duke of Yangping, Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遇河水暴長，具船將妻子奔齊，經砥柱之險，時人稱其勇決。

translations.literal: When the river waters rose violently, he prepared a boat and fled to Qi with his wife and children, passing the peril of Jizhu; people of the time praised his courage and resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When the river waters rose violently, he prepared a boat and fled to Qi with his wife and children, passing the peril of Jizhu; people of the time praised his courage and resolve.

sentences.zh: 文宣見，悅之，即除奉朝請，引於內館中，侍從左右，頗被顧眄。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan saw him, he was pleased and at once appointed him Court Gentleman for Attendance, bringing him into the inner lodge to attend at his side; he received considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenxuan saw him, he was pleased and at once appointed him Court Gentleman for Attendance, bringing him into the inner lodge to attend at his side; he received considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 後從至天泉池，以為中書舍人，令中書郎段孝信將敕示之推。

translations.literal: Later, when he followed the emperor to the Heavenly Spring Pool, Zhitui was made Secretariat Drafter; the Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin was ordered to show Zhitui the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he followed the emperor to the Heavenly Spring Pool, Zhitui was made Secretariat Drafter; the Secretariat Gentleman Duan Xiaoxin was ordered to show Zhitui the edict.

sentences.zh: 之推營外飲酒，孝信還以狀言，文宣乃曰：「且停。」

translations.literal: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; Xiaoxin returned and reported the situation, and Wenxuan then said, "Let it wait for now.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui was drinking outside the camp; Xiaoxin returned and reported the situation, and Wenxuan then said, "Let it wait for now.

sentences.zh: 由是遂寢。

translations.literal: Because of this the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 後待詔文林館，除司徒錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Later he awaited edicts at the Forest of Letters Hall and was appointed Recorder of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Later he awaited edicts at the Forest of Letters Hall and was appointed Recorder of the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 之推聰穎機悟，博識有才辯，工尺牘，應對閑明，大為祖珽所重，令掌知館事，判署文書。

translations.literal: Zhitui was intelligent and quick-witted, broadly learned and talented in debate, skilled in letters, and clear and ready in reply; Zu Ting greatly valued him and had him manage the hall affairs and endorse documents.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui was intelligent and quick-witted, broadly learned and talented in debate, skilled in letters, and clear and ready in reply; Zu Ting greatly valued him and had him manage the hall affairs and endorse documents.

sentences.zh: 遷通直散騎常侍，俄領中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and soon concurrently served as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and soon concurrently served as Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 帝時有取索，恆令中使傳旨，之推稟承宣告，館中皆受進止。

translations.literal: When the emperor had demands, he always had palace envoys convey his orders; Zhitui received and announced them, and everyone in the hall took their instructions from him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had demands, he always had palace envoys convey his orders; Zhitui received and announced them, and everyone in the hall took their instructions from him.

sentences.zh: 所進文書，皆是其封署，於進賢門奏之，待報方出。

translations.literal: All documents submitted were sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement of Worthies and released them only after receiving a reply.
translations.idiomatic: All documents submitted were sealed by him; he presented them at the Gate of Advancement of Worthies and released them only after receiving a reply.

sentences.zh: 兼善於文字，監校繕寫，處事勤敏，號為稱職，帝甚加恩接。

translations.literal: He was also skilled in writing, supervised collation and copying, and handled affairs with diligence and alertness; he was known as competent in office, and the emperor greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He was also skilled in writing, supervised collation and copying, and handled affairs with diligence and alertness; he was known as competent in office, and the emperor greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 為勳要者所嫉，常欲害之。

translations.literal: He was envied by powerful meritocrats, who often wished to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: He was envied by powerful meritocrats, who often wished to harm him.

sentences.zh: 崔季舒等將諫也，之推取急還宅，故不連署。

translations.literal: When Cui Jishu and others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in signing.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Jishu and others were about to remonstrate, Zhitui took urgent leave and returned home, and therefore did not join in signing.

sentences.zh: 及召集諫人，之推亦被喚入，勘無名，得免。

translations.literal: When those who had remonstrated were summoned, Zhitui was also called in; on investigation his name was not listed, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When those who had remonstrated were summoned, Zhitui was also called in; on investigation his name was not listed, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 尋除黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 及周兵陷晉陽，帝輕騎還鄴，窘急，計無所從。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor returned to Ye with a light escort; in distress and urgency, he had no plan to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou army took Jinyang, the emperor returned to Ye with a light escort; in distress and urgency, he had no plan to follow.

sentences.zh: 之推因宦者侍中鄧長顒進奔陳策，仍勸募吳士千餘人以為左右，取青、徐路共投陳國。

translations.literal: Zhitui, through the eunuch Attendant-in-Chief Deng Changying, advanced a plan to flee to Chen; he also urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard and taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui, through the eunuch Attendant-in-Chief Deng Changying, advanced a plan to flee to Chen; he also urged recruiting more than a thousand Wu men as a personal guard and taking the Qing and Xu route together to throw themselves on Chen.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，以告丞相高阿那肱等。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it and told the Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted it and told the Chief Minister Gao Anagong and the others.

sentences.zh: 阿那肱不願入陳。

translations.literal: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Anagong did not wish to enter Chen.

sentences.zh: 乃雲吳士難信，勸帝送珍寶累重向青州，且守三齊地。

translations.literal: He then said that Wu men were hard to trust and urged the emperor to send his heavy store of treasures to Qingzhou and for the time being hold the Three Qi region.
translations.idiomatic: He then said that Wu men were hard to trust and urged the emperor to send his heavy store of treasures to Qingzhou and for the time being hold the Three Qi region.

sentences.zh: 若不可保，徐浮海南度。

translations.literal: If it could not be held, they could slowly cross the sea southward.
translations.idiomatic: If it could not be held, they could slowly cross the sea southward.

sentences.zh: 雖不從之推策，然猶以為平原太守，令守河津。

translations.literal: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him Administrator of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Though they did not follow Zhitui's plan, they still made him Administrator of Pingyuan and ordered him to guard the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he entered Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi perished he entered Zhou.

sentences.zh: 大象末，為御史上士。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang he served as Senior Attendant of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daxiang he served as Senior Attendant of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，太子召為文學，深見禮重，尋以疾終。

translations.literal: During Sui's Kaihuang reign the Crown Prince summoned him as Literary Scholar; he was deeply honored, and soon died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: During Sui's Kaihuang reign the Crown Prince summoned him as Literary Scholar; he was deeply honored, and soon died of illness.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十卷，撰《家訓》二十篇，並行於世。

translations.literal: He left collected works in thirty juan and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions; both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in thirty juan and compiled twenty chapters of Family Instructions; both circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 之推在齊有二子，長曰思魯，次曰敏楚，蓋不忘本也。

translations.literal: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder was named Silu, the younger Mintu—showing that he did not forget his origins.
translations.idiomatic: Zhitui had two sons in Qi: the elder was named Silu, the younger Mintu—showing that he did not forget his origins.

sentences.zh: 《之推集》，思魯自為序。

translations.literal: The Collected Works of Zhitui had a preface written by Silu himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Works of Zhitui had a preface written by Silu himself.

sentences.zh: 弟之儀，字升。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhiyi, courtesy name Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhiyi, courtesy name Sheng.

sentences.zh: 幼穎悟，三歲能讀《孝經》。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and perceptive; at three he could read the Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was keen and perceptive; at three he could read the Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉群書，好為詞賦。

translations.literal: When grown, he read widely among all books and loved composing rhapsodies and fu.
translations.idiomatic: When grown, he read widely among all books and loved composing rhapsodies and fu.

sentences.zh: 嘗獻梁元帝《荊州頌》，辭致雅贍。

translations.literal: He once presented to Emperor Yuan of Liang the "Hymn to Jingzhou"; its language was elegant and ample.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented to Emperor Yuan of Liang the "Hymn to Jingzhou"; its language was elegant and ample.

sentences.zh: 帝手敕曰：「枚乘二葉，俱得游梁；

translations.literal: The emperor wrote in his own hand: "Mei Sheng for two generations both gained to roam in Liang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in his own hand: "Mei Sheng for two generations both gained to roam in Liang;

sentences.zh: 應貞兩世，並稱文學。

translations.literal: Ying Zhen for two ages were both styled men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Zhen for two ages were both styled men of letters.

sentences.zh: 我求才子，鯁慰良深。」

translations.literal: I seek a talented man—how deeply this straight answer comforts me."
translations.idiomatic: I seek a talented man—how deeply this straight answer comforts me."

sentences.zh: 江陵平，之儀隨例遷長安，周明帝以為麟趾學士。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified, Zhiyi was moved to Chang'an according to precedent; Emperor Ming of Zhou made him a Unicorn Toe Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling was pacified, Zhiyi was moved to Chang'an according to precedent; Emperor Ming of Zhou made him a Unicorn Toe Scholar.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司書上士。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Senior Attendant of the Directorate of Documents.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Senior Attendant of the Directorate of Documents.

sentences.zh: 武帝初建東宮，盛選師傅，以之儀為侍讀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first established the Eastern Palace, he lavishly selected tutors and made Zhiyi Reader-in-Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first established the Eastern Palace, he lavishly selected tutors and made Zhiyi Reader-in-Attendance.

sentences.zh: 太子後征吐谷渾，在軍有過行，鄭譯等並以不能匡弼坐譴，唯之儀以累諫獲賞。

translations.literal: Later the Crown Prince campaigned against Tuyuhun; in the army he committed misconduct, and Zheng Yi and others were all punished for failing to correct him—only Zhiyi was rewarded for repeated remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Crown Prince campaigned against Tuyuhun; in the army he committed misconduct, and Zheng Yi and others were all punished for failing to correct him—only Zhiyi was rewarded for repeated remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 即拜小宮尹，封平陽縣男。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Junior Palace Steward and enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed Junior Palace Steward and enfeoffed as Baron of Pingyang county.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，遷上儀同大將軍、禦正中大夫，進爵為公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Zhiyi was transferred to General of the Upper Honored Standing and Grand Master of the Palace for the Imperial Household, and advanced in rank to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Zhiyi was transferred to General of the Upper Honored Standing and Grand Master of the Palace for the Imperial Household, and advanced in rank to Duke.

sentences.zh: 帝后刑政乖僻，昏縱日甚。

translations.literal: The emperor afterward was perverse in punishments and government, growing daily more muddled and dissolute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor afterward was perverse in punishments and government, growing daily more muddled and dissolute.

sentences.zh: 之儀犯顏驟諫，雖不見納，終亦不止，深為帝所忌。

translations.literal: Zhiyi offended his countenance and remonstrated repeatedly; though not accepted, he never ceased, and the emperor deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi offended his countenance and remonstrated repeatedly; though not accepted, he never ceased, and the emperor deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 然以恩舊，每優容之。

translations.literal: Yet because of old favor, the emperor always treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of old favor, the emperor always treated him with forbearance.

sentences.zh: 及帝殺王軌，之儀固諫。

translations.literal: When the emperor killed Wang Gui, Zhiyi firmly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor killed Wang Gui, Zhiyi firmly remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，欲並致之於法。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and wished to subject him to the law as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and wished to subject him to the law as well.

sentences.zh: 後以其諒直無私，乃舍之。

translations.literal: Later, because he was honest, upright, and without private motive, the emperor spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he was honest, upright, and without private motive, the emperor spared him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，劉昉、鄭譯等矯遺詔，以隋文帝為丞相輔少主。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others forged the testamentary edict, making Emperor Wen of Sui Chief Minister to assist the young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan died, Liu Fang, Zheng Yi, and others forged the testamentary edict, making Emperor Wen of Sui Chief Minister to assist the young ruler.

sentences.zh: 之儀知非帝旨，拒而弗從。

translations.literal: Zhiyi knew this was not the late emperor's intent and refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi knew this was not the late emperor's intent and refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 昉等草詔，署訖，逼之儀署。

translations.literal: Fang and the others drafted the edict; when it was signed, they forced Zhiyi to sign.
translations.idiomatic: Fang and the others drafted the edict; when it was signed, they forced Zhiyi to sign.

sentences.zh: 之儀厲聲謂昉等曰：「主上升遐，嗣子幼沖，阿衡之任，宜在宗英。

translations.literal: Zhiyi said sharply to Fang and the others, "The lord has ascended on high; the heir is young and tender; the task of the regent should fall on a worthy of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi said sharply to Fang and the others, "The lord has ascended on high; the heir is young and tender; the task of the regent should fall on a worthy of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 方今賢戚之內，趙王最長，以親以德，合膺重寄。

translations.literal: Among the worthy kin today, the Prince of Zhao is eldest; in kinship and in virtue he should bear this heavy charge.
translations.idiomatic: Among the worthy kin today, the Prince of Zhao is eldest; in kinship and in virtue he should bear this heavy charge.

sentences.zh: 公等備受朝恩，當盡忠報國，柰何一旦欲以神器假人！

translations.literal: You have all received the court's grace and ought to serve the state with full loyalty—how can you in a single day wish to lend the sacred vessel to another!
translations.idiomatic: You have all received the court's grace and ought to serve the state with full loyalty—how can you in a single day wish to lend the sacred vessel to another!

sentences.zh: 之儀有死而已，不能誣罔先帝。」

translations.literal: Zhiyi has death and nothing more; he cannot deceive and wrong the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi has death and nothing more; he cannot deceive and wrong the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 於是昉等知不可屈，乃代之儀署而行之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fang and the others knew he could not be bent and signed in Zhiyi's place before carrying it out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Fang and the others knew he could not be bent and signed in Zhiyi's place before carrying it out.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝后索符璽，之儀又正色曰：「此天子之物，自有主者，宰相何故索之？」

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Wen of Sui demanded the seals and credentials; Zhiyi again said sternly, "These are the Son of Heaven's objects; they have their own master—why should the Chief Minister demand them?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Wen of Sui demanded the seals and credentials; Zhiyi again said sternly, "These are the Son of Heaven's objects; they have their own master—why should the Chief Minister demand them?

sentences.zh: 於是文帝大怒，命引出，將戮之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wen was greatly angered, ordered him led out, and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Wen was greatly angered, ordered him led out, and was about to execute him.

sentences.zh: 然以其人望，乃止。

translations.literal: Yet because of his public standing, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because of his public standing, he stopped.

sentences.zh: 出為西疆郡守。

translations.literal: Zhiyi went out as Administrator of Xijiang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi went out as Administrator of Xijiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 及踐極，詔征還京師，進爵新野郡公。

translations.literal: When Wen took the throne, an edict summoned him back to the capital and advanced his rank to Duke of Xinye commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen took the throne, an edict summoned him back to the capital and advanced his rank to Duke of Xinye commandery.

sentences.zh: 開皇五年，拜集州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaihuang he was appointed Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 在州清靜，夷夏悅之。

translations.literal: In the province his rule was pure and quiet; barbarians and Chinese alike were pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the province his rule was pure and quiet; barbarians and Chinese alike were pleased with him.

sentences.zh: 明年代還，遂優遊不仕。

translations.literal: The next year his term ended and he returned; thereafter he lived at ease and took no office.
