translations.idiomatic: The next year his term ended and he returned; thereafter he lived at ease and took no office.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，之儀例入朝。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, Zhiyi entered court according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, Zhiyi entered court according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 文帝望而識之，命引至御坐，謂之曰：「見危授命，臨大節而不可奪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen saw him from afar and recognized him, ordered him brought to the imperial seat, and said to him, "To give one's life in peril, to face great principle and not be turned from it—
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen saw him from afar and recognized him, ordered him brought to the imperial seat, and said to him, "To give one's life in peril, to face great principle and not be turned from it—

sentences.zh: 古人所難，何以加卿。」

translations.literal: what the ancients found difficult—how could one add to you?
translations.idiomatic: what the ancients found difficult—how could one add to you?

sentences.zh: 乃賜錢十萬、米一百石。

translations.literal: He then granted him a hundred thousand cash and a hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted him a hundred thousand cash and a hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the eleventh year.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 有《文集》十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He left a Collected Works in ten juan, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left a Collected Works in ten juan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 虞世基，字懋世，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Shiji, courtesy name Maoshi, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji, courtesy name Maoshi, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父荔，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Li has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 世基幼恬靜，喜慍不形于色，博學有高才，兼善草隸。

translations.literal: Shiji in youth was tranquil; joy and anger did not show on his face; he was broadly learned with high talent and was also skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji in youth was tranquil; joy and anger did not show on his face; he was broadly learned with high talent and was also skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 陳中書令孔奐見而歎曰：「南金之貴，屬在斯人。」

translations.literal: Kong Huan, Secretariat Director of Chen, saw him and sighed, saying, "The worth of southern gold belongs to this man.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan, Secretariat Director of Chen, saw him and sighed, saying, "The worth of southern gold belongs to this man.

sentences.zh: 少傅徐陵聞其名，召之，世基不往。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor Xu Ling heard his name and summoned him; Shiji did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor Xu Ling heard his name and summoned him; Shiji did not go.

sentences.zh: 後因公會，陵一見而奇之，顧朝士曰：「當今潘、陸也。」

translations.literal: Later, at a public gathering, Ling saw him once and marveled at him; turning to the court gentlemen he said, "The Pan and Lu of our day.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a public gathering, Ling saw him once and marveled at him; turning to the court gentlemen he said, "The Pan and Lu of our day.

sentences.zh: 因以弟女妻焉。

translations.literal: He thereupon gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon gave him his younger brother's daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，累遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He served Chen and was promoted in succession to Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chen and was promoted in succession to Left Assistant of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 陳主嘗于莫府山校獵，令世基為《講武賦》，於坐奏之。

translations.literal: The ruler of Chen once hunted at Mofu Mountain and had Shiji compose the "Fu on Military Instruction"; he presented it at the gathering.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Chen once hunted at Mofu Mountain and had Shiji compose the "Fu on Military Instruction"; he presented it at the gathering.

sentences.zh: 陳主嘉之，賜馬一匹。

translations.literal: The ruler of Chen praised it and granted him one horse.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Chen praised it and granted him one horse.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，入隋為通直郎，直內史省。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed, he entered Sui as Direct Attendant and served in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was destroyed, he entered Sui as Direct Attendant and served in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 貧無產業，每傭書養親，怏怏不平。

translations.literal: He was poor without property, copied books to support his parents, and was resentful and discontent.
translations.idiomatic: Poor and without property, he copied books to support his parents and nursed a constant resentment.

sentences.zh: 嘗為五言詩以見情，文理忄妻切，世以為工，作者無不吟詠。

translations.literal: He once composed pentasyllabic verse to express his feelings; the writing was poignant and moving, and the age thought it skillful—every author recited it.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote pentasyllabic poems to vent his feelings; the lines were moving and poignant, and contemporaries hailed them as masterly—every writer recited them.

sentences.zh: 未幾拜內史舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，顧遇彌隆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, his favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, imperial favor toward him grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 秘書監河東柳顧言，博學有才，罕所推謝，至是與世基相見，歎曰：「海內當共推此一人，非吾儕所及也。」

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Liu Guyan of Hedong, broadly learned and talented, rarely praised others; on meeting Shiji he sighed and said, "Within the seas this one man should be jointly acclaimed—it is not something our sort can match.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guyan of Hedong, the Secretariat Director, was learned and talented and rarely praised anyone; meeting Shiji, he sighed and said, "Within the four seas this one man alone should be acclaimed—we of our sort cannot match him.

sentences.zh: 俄遷內史侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以母憂去職，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his mother's death and was emaciated with grief to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother and wasted away with grief until he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 有詔起令視事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him recalled to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to duty.

sentences.zh: 拜見之日，殆不能起，令左右扶之。

translations.literal: On the day he paid homage he could scarcely rise and had attendants support him.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he paid homage he could barely stand and had to be supported by attendants.

sentences.zh: 哀其羸瘠，詔令進肉。

translations.literal: Pitying his frailty, the emperor ordered meat brought to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying how frail he was, the emperor ordered that meat be brought to him.

sentences.zh: 世基食，輒悲哽不能下筋。

translations.literal: When Shiji ate, he would choke with grief and could not swallow.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiji tried to eat, grief would choke him and he could not swallow.

sentences.zh: 帝使謂曰：「方相委任，宜為國惜身。」

translations.literal: The emperor had someone say to him, "Now that I entrust you with responsibility, you should spare your person for the state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent word: "Now that I entrust affairs to you, you ought to spare your health for the sake of the state.

sentences.zh: 前後敦勸者數矣。

translations.literal: Such earnest urging came several times before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Such earnest admonitions were repeated several times.

sentences.zh: 帝重其才，親禮逾厚，專典機密，與納言蘇威、左翊衛大將軍宇文述、黃門侍郎裴矩、御史大夫裴蘊等參掌朝政。

translations.literal: The emperor valued his talent, treated him with ever closer personal courtesy, put him in sole charge of secrets, and with Censor-in-Chief Su Wei, General of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu, Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju, Imperial Censor Pei Yun, and others jointly managed court government.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor prized his talent, drew him ever closer, put him in sole charge of confidential matters, and with Su Wei, Yuwen Shu, Pei Ju, Pei Yun, and others shared in governing the court.

sentences.zh: 時天下多事，四方表奏，日有百數。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had many troubles; memorials from the four quarters numbered in the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was troubled on every side; memorials from the four quarters ran to hundreds a day.

sentences.zh: 帝方凝重，事不廷決。

translations.literal: The emperor was grave and slow; affairs were not decided in open court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was grave and deliberate and would not decide matters in open court.

sentences.zh: 入閣之後，始召世基口授節度。

translations.literal: After entering the inner chambers he would summon Shiji and dictate orders orally.
translations.idiomatic: Only after retiring to the inner quarters would he summon Shiji and dictate his orders.

sentences.zh: 世基至省，方為敕書，日旦百紙，無所遺繆。

translations.literal: Shiji would reach the ministry and then draft edicts—by dawn a hundred sheets, without omission or error.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji would go to the ministry and draft edicts—by dawn a hundred documents, without slip or omission.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 後從幸雁門，為突厥所圍。

translations.literal: Later he followed the emperor to Yanmen and was besieged by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor to Yanmen, where they were besieged by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 戰士多敗。

translations.literal: Many soldiers were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the troops were defeated.

sentences.zh: 世基勸帝為賞格，親自撫循，乃下詔停遼東事。

translations.literal: Shiji urged the emperor to set reward standards and personally comfort the troops; thereupon an edict halted the Liaodong campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji urged the emperor to proclaim rewards and go among the men in person; an edict then halted the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝從之，師乃復振。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; the army then rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the army's spirit revived.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，勳格不行，又下伐遼之詔，由是言其詐眾，朝野離心。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted the merit rewards were not carried out, and an edict to attack Liao was issued again; therefore people said he deceived the masses, and court and country lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege was lifted the promised rewards were not granted, and a new edict ordered another attack on Liao; people said he had deceived the army, and court and country turned away from him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸江都，次鞏縣，世基以盜賊日盛，請發兵屯洛口倉，以備不虞。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Jiangdu and stopped at Gong county; Shiji, because bandits grew daily, asked to send troops to garrison the Luokou granary against emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor traveled to Jiangdu and halted at Gong; as banditry grew daily, Shiji asked to station troops at the Luokou granary against surprise.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，但答云：「卿是書生，定猶恇怯。」

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree but only replied, "You are a man of letters and surely still timid and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused, answering only, "You are a scholar—you must still be timid and fearful.

sentences.zh: 于時天下大亂，世基知帝不可諫正，又以高熲、張衡等相繼誅戮，懼禍及己，雖居近侍，唯諂取容，不敢忤意。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was in great disorder; Shiji knew the emperor could not be corrected by remonstrance, and because Gao Jiong, Zhang Heng, and others were executed in succession, he feared harm would reach himself; though he served close at hand, he only flattered to please and did not dare oppose the emperor's will.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was falling apart; Shiji knew the emperor could not be remonstrated with, and as Gao Jiong, Zhang Heng, and others were executed one after another, he feared for his own life; though he stayed at the emperor's side, he only flattered and never contradicted him.

sentences.zh: 盜賊日甚，郡縣多沒，世基知帝惡數聞之，後有告敗者，乃抑損表狀，不以實聞。

translations.literal: Bandits grew daily worse and many commanderies and counties fell; Shiji knew the emperor hated to hear such news repeatedly, so when later reports of defeat came he suppressed and reduced the memorials and did not inform him of the truth.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits grew worse and commanderies and counties fell, Shiji knew the emperor hated repeated bad news; when defeat was reported later, he toned down the memorials and did not tell him the truth.

sentences.zh: 是後外間有變，帝弗之知也。

translations.literal: After this, when changes occurred outside, the emperor did not know of them.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the emperor knew nothing of what was happening outside.

sentences.zh: 嘗遣太僕卿楊義臣捕盜河北，降賊數十萬，列狀上聞。

translations.literal: He once sent Minister of Imperial Studs Yang Yichen to capture bandits in Hebei; tens of thousands of surrendered bandits were listed and reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent Yang Yichen, Minister of Imperial Studs, to suppress bandits in Hebei; tens of thousands surrendered and were listed in a memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「我初不聞賊頓如此，義臣列降賊何多也？」

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "At first I did not hear that bandits were suddenly so numerous—why does Yichen list so many surrendered bandits?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed: "I never heard that bandits had suddenly become so numerous—why does Yichen list so many surrenders?

sentences.zh: 世基曰：「鼠竊雖多，未足為慮。

translations.literal: Shiji said, "Though rats and thieves are many, they are not worth concern.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji said, "Rats and thieves may be many, but they are no great concern.

sentences.zh: 義臣克之，擁兵不少，久在閫外，此最非宜。」

translations.literal: Yichen has defeated them but holds no small army; long outside the passes—this is most unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen has beaten them but now commands no small force and has long been outside the passes—that is most dangerous.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 遽追義臣，放其兵散。

translations.literal: He hastily recalled Yichen and dispersed his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He hastily recalled Yichen and dispersed his troops.

sentences.zh: 又越王侗遣太常丞元善達間行賊中，詣江都奏事，稱：「李密有眾數萬，圍逼京都。

translations.literal: Also Prince of Yue Tong sent the Director of Ceremonies Yuan Shanda by a secret route through the bandits to Jiangdu to report, saying, "Li Mi has tens of thousands of men and presses upon the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yue also sent Yuan Shanda, Director of Ceremonies, through the bandits by a secret route to Jiangdu to report that Li Mi had tens of thousands of men and was pressing the capital.

sentences.zh: 賊據洛口倉，城內無食。

translations.literal: The bandits hold the Luokou granary; within the city there is no food.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits held the Luokou granary and the city had no grain.

sentences.zh: 若陛下速還，烏合必散。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty returns quickly, the rabble will surely scatter.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty returns at once, the mob will surely scatter.

sentences.zh: 不然者，東都決沒。」

translations.literal: Otherwise the eastern capital will certainly fall.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the eastern capital will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 因歔欷嗚咽，帝為改容。

translations.literal: He then sobbed and wept; the emperor's expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shanda sobbed and wept; the emperor's face changed.

sentences.zh: 世基見帝色憂，進曰：「越王年小，此輩誑之。

translations.literal: Shiji, seeing the emperor's worried look, advanced and said, "The Prince of Yue is young; these people deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor troubled, Shiji stepped forward: "The Prince of Yue is young; these men deceive him.

sentences.zh: 若如所言，善達何緣得至？」

translations.literal: If it were as they say, how could Shanda have reached here?
translations.idiomatic: If things were as they say, how could Shanda have arrived here?

sentences.zh: 帝勃然怒曰：「善達小人，敢廷辱我！」

translations.literal: The emperor said angrily, "Shanda is a petty man who dares insult me in open court!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flared up: "Shanda is a petty fellow who dares insult me in court!

sentences.zh: 因使經賊中，向東陽催運。

translations.literal: He therefore had him pass through the bandits and go east to Dongyang to urge transport.
translations.idiomatic: He sent him back through the bandit country to Dongyang to urge grain transport.

sentences.zh: 善達遂為群盜所殺。

translations.literal: Shanda was thereupon killed by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shanda was killed by the bandits.

sentences.zh: 此後外人杜口，莫敢以賊聞奏。

translations.literal: After this outsiders kept silent and dared not report bandits in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After that no outsider dared report bandits in memorials.

sentences.zh: 世基氣貌沈審，言多合意，是以特見親愛，朝臣無與為比。

translations.literal: Shiji's bearing was deep and careful; his words mostly pleased the emperor, and therefore he was especially beloved; no court minister could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was deep and careful in manner; his words usually pleased the emperor, and none at court was so beloved.

sentences.zh: 其繼室孫氏，性驕淫，世基惑之，恣意奢靡，雕飾器服，無復素士之風。

translations.literal: His second wife, the Sun clan, was proud and dissolute; Shiji was bewitched by her and indulged in extravagance, carving and adorning vessels and dress, with no trace left of a plain scholar's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His second wife, of the Sun clan, was arrogant and dissolute; bewitched by her, he indulged in luxury, carving and adorning vessels and dress until nothing remained of a scholar's plain ways.

sentences.zh: 孫復攜前夫子夏侯儼入世基舍，而頑鄙無賴，為其聚斂，鬻官賣獄，賄賂公行，其門如市，金寶盈積。

translations.literal: Sun again brought in her former husband's son Xia Houyan into Shiji's house; he was coarse and worthless, gathering wealth for them, selling offices and judgments, bribes flowing openly—their gate like a market, gold and gems heaped up.
translations.idiomatic: Sun also brought her former husband's son Xia Houyan into the household; coarse and worthless, he amassed wealth for them, sold offices and judgments, and bribes flowed at their gate like a market, gold and gems piled high.

sentences.zh: 其弟世南素國士，而清貧不立，未曾有所贍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shinan was always a man of the state's scholar class yet poor and without support; Shiji never provided for him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shinan, though a man of the state's scholar class, was poor and unsupported; Shiji never helped him.

sentences.zh: 由是為論者所譏。

translations.literal: Therefore critics ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics therefore mocked him.

sentences.zh: 朝野咸共疾怨。

translations.literal: Court and country alike hated and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike hated him.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，世基乃見害。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, Shiji was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Shiji was killed too.

sentences.zh: 長子肅，好學才藝，時人稱有家風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Su loved learning and the arts; people of the time praised the family's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Su loved learning and the arts; contemporaries praised the family's tradition.

sentences.zh: 弱冠早沒。

translations.literal: He died young in his twenties.
translations.idiomatic: He died young, not yet thirty.

sentences.zh: 肅弟熙，大業末為符璽郎。

translations.literal: Su's younger brother Xi, at the end of Daye, served as Credential Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Su's younger brother Xi, at the end of Daye, was Credential Attendant.

sentences.zh: 次子柔、晦，並宣義郎。

translations.literal: The second sons Rou and Hui both served as Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The second sons Rou and Hui both held the post of Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 化及將亂之夕，宗人虞伋知而告熙曰：「事勢已然，吾將濟卿南度，且得免禍，同死何益。」

translations.literal: On the eve of Huaji's rebellion, their clansman Yu Ji knew of it and told Xi, "The situation is already decided; I will help you cross south and at least escape harm—what use is dying together?
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of Huaji's revolt their clansman Yu Ji learned of it and told Xi, "The die is cast; I will help you flee south and escape harm—what good is dying together?

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「棄父背君，求生何地，感尊之懷，自此訣矣。」

translations.literal: Xi said, "To abandon one's father and turn one's back on one's lord—where is life to be sought? I am grateful for your kindness; from this we part.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "To abandon one's father and betray one's lord—where could one live? I thank you for your kindness; we part here.

sentences.zh: 及難作，兄弟競請先死，行刑人先世基殺之。

translations.literal: When disaster struck, the brothers competed to die first; the executioners killed Shiji first.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster came, the brothers vied to die first; the executioners killed Shiji first.

sentences.zh: 柳{巧言}，字顧言，河東人也。

translations.literal: Liu Guyan, courtesy name Guyan, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guyan, courtesy name Guyan, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世仕江南，居襄陽。

translations.literal: For generations the family served in Jiangnan and dwelt in Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had served in the south and lived at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 祖惔，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan is given a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: {巧言}少聰敏，解屬文，好讀書，所覽將萬卷。

translations.literal: Guyan in youth was intelligent and quick, could compose prose, loved reading, and perused nearly ten thousand juan.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Guyan was clever and quick, could write prose, loved books, and had read nearly ten thousand juan.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，為著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang he served as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition.

sentences.zh: 後蕭察據荊州，以為侍中，領國子祭酒、吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Cha held Jingzhou and made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Libationer of the National University and Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Cha held Jingzhou he made him Attendant-in-Ordinary, Libationer of the National University, and Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及梁國廢，拜開府，為內史侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Liang state was abolished he was appointed Opening Office and made Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang state was abolished he received the Opening Office and became Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以無吏幹，轉晉王諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Because he lacked administrative skill, he was transferred to Advisory Attendant of the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Lacking administrative talent, he was transferred to be Advisory Attendant to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 王好文雅，招引才學之士諸葛潁、虞世南、王胄、硃瑒等百餘人以充學士，而{巧言}為之冠。

translations.literal: The prince loved letters and gathered more than a hundred talented scholars such as Zhuge Ying, Yu Shiji, Wang Zhou, Zhu Yang, and others to fill the academy, with Guyan at their head.
translations.idiomatic: The prince loved letters and gathered more than a hundred scholars—Zhuge Ying, Yu Shiji, Wang Zhou, Zhu Yang, and others—with Guyan at their head.

sentences.zh: 王以師友處之，每有文什，必令其潤色，然後示人。

translations.literal: The prince treated him as teacher and friend; whenever he had a literary piece he always had Guyan polish it before showing others.
translations.idiomatic: The prince treated him as teacher and friend; every literary piece was polished by Guyan before it was shown to others.

sentences.zh: 嘗朝京還，作《歸籓賦》，命{巧言}為序，詞甚典麗。

translations.literal: Once returning from court to the capital he composed the "Fu on Returning to the Fief" and had Guyan write the preface; the language was very canonical and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from the capital he wrote the "Fu on Returning to the Fief" and had Guyan compose the preface in splendidly canonical language.

sentences.zh: 初王屬文，效庾信體，及見{巧言}後，文體遂變。

translations.literal: At first when the prince wrote he imitated Yu Xin's manner; after meeting Guyan his style changed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prince wrote in imitation of Yu Xin; after meeting Guyan his style changed.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，引為東宮學士，加通直散騎常侍，檢校洗馬，甚見親重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was brought in as Eastern Palace scholar, given additional title Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry, and made Inspector of the Crown Prince's Chariot; he was greatly honored.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Renshou he entered the Eastern Palace as scholar, was given Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry, and made Inspector of the Crown Prince's Chariot, with great honor.

sentences.zh: 每召入臥內，與之宴謔。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned into the inner quarters he feasted and jested with the prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was often summoned into the inner quarters to feast and jest with the prince.

sentences.zh: {巧言}尤俊辯，多在侍從，有所顧問，應答如響。

translations.literal: Guyan was especially quick in debate; often in attendance, when questioned he answered like an echo.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan was especially quick-tongued; in attendance he answered questions like an echo.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，言雜誹諧。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine; his speech mixed in jest and banter.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and his speech mixed jest and banter.

sentences.zh: 由是彌為太子所親狎。

translations.literal: Therefore the prince drew even closer to him in intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince therefore drew even closer to him.

sentences.zh: 以其好內典，令撰《法華玄宗》，為二十卷上之。

translations.literal: Because he loved Buddhist sutras, he was ordered to compile the Xuanzong of the Lotus Sutra in twenty juan and present it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Because he loved Buddhist sutras, he was ordered to compile the Xuanzong of the Lotus Sutra in twenty juan and present it.

sentences.zh: 太子大悅，賞賜優洽，儕輩莫比。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince was greatly pleased and rewarded him generously; none of his peers could compare.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince was delighted and rewarded him generously beyond any peer.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜秘書監，封漢南縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was appointed Secretariat Director and enfeoffed as Duke of Hannan county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was made Secretariat Director and enfeoffed Duke of Hannan county.

sentences.zh: 帝退朝後，便命入問，言宴諷讀，終日而罷。

translations.literal: After the emperor left court he would order Guyan in to question him; they talked, feasted, read, and jested all day before parting.
translations.idiomatic: After court the emperor would have him brought in; they talked, feasted, read, and jested all day.

sentences.zh: 常每與嬪後對酒，時逢興會，輒遣命之至，與同榻共席，恩比友朋。

translations.literal: Often when drinking with consorts and concubines, if the mood struck he would send for Guyan to share the couch and mat, treating him like a friend.
translations.idiomatic: Often when drinking with consorts he would send for Guyan to share couch and mat, treating him as a friend.

sentences.zh: 帝猶恨不能夜召，乃命匠刻木為偶人，施機關，能坐起拜伏，以像{巧言}。

translations.literal: The emperor still regretted he could not summon him at night, and ordered craftsmen to carve a wooden automaton with mechanisms to sit, rise, bow, and prostrate, in Guyan's likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Still regretting he could not summon him at night, the emperor had craftsmen carve a wooden automaton with mechanisms to sit, rise, bow, and prostrate in Guyan's likeness.

sentences.zh: 帝每月下對飲酒，輒令宮人置於座，與相酬酢，而為歡笑。

translations.literal: Each month under the moon the emperor drank wine and had palace women place it at his seat to toast and exchange cups, laughing in delight.
translations.idiomatic: Each month under the moon he would drink and have palace women set the figure at his seat to exchange toasts and laugh.

sentences.zh: 從幸揚州，卒，帝傷惜者久之。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Yangzhou, he died; the emperor mourned him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Following the emperor to Yangzhou he died; the emperor mourned him long.

sentences.zh: 贈大將軍，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted the title Great General and given the posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Great General with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: {巧言}撰《晉王北伐記》十五卷，有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: Guyan compiled fifteen juan of the Record of the Prince of Jin's Northern Campaign and left a collected works in ten juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Guyan compiled fifteen juan of the Record of the Prince of Jin's Northern Campaign and left collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 許善心，字務本，高陽北新城人也。

translations.literal: Xu Shanxin, courtesy name Wuben, was a man of Beixin in Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shanxin, courtesy name Wuben, was from Beixin in Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 祖茂、父亨，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mao and father Heng both have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mao and father Heng both appear in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 善心九歲而孤，為母范氏所鞠養。

translations.literal: Shanxin was orphaned at nine and was raised by his mother, Lady Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at nine, he was raised by his mother Lady Fan.

sentences.zh: 幼聰明，有思理，所聞輒能記，多聞默識，為當世所稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was intelligent, with reflective judgment; what he heard he could remember, and he knew much in silent study—he was acclaimed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, he remembered whatever he heard and was famed for silent breadth of learning.

sentences.zh: 家有舊書萬餘卷，皆遍通涉。

translations.literal: The family had more than ten thousand juan of old books, all of which he read through.
translations.idiomatic: The family had more than ten thousand juan of old books, all of which he mastered.

sentences.zh: 十五解屬文，為箋上父友徐陵，陵大奇之，謂人曰：「此神童也。」

translations.literal: At fifteen he could compose prose; he sent a letter to his father's friend Xu Ling, who greatly marveled and said to others, "This is a divine child.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he could write prose and sent a letter to Xu Ling, who marveled and said, "This is a divine child.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事江總舉秀才，對策高第，授度支郎中，補撰史學士。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor Jiang Zong recommended him as xiucai; in the palace examination he ranked high and was appointed Director of Revenue, supplementary Drafting Historian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong recommended him as xiucai; he ranked high in the examination and was made Director of Revenue and supplementary Drafting Historian.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，加通直散騎常侍聘隋。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming he was given additional title Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry on embassy to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenming he was sent as envoy to Sui with the title Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 遇文帝伐陳，禮成而不獲反命。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen attacked Chen, the rites were completed but he could not return with his mission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen attacked Chen, the rites were done but he could not return.

sentences.zh: 累表請辭，上不許。

translations.literal: He memorialized repeatedly asking to be dismissed; the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked leave; the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 留縶賓館。

translations.literal: He was detained in the guest lodge.
translations.idiomatic: He was held in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，上遣使告之。

translations.literal: When Chen perished, the emperor sent an envoy to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell the emperor sent an envoy to tell him.

sentences.zh: 善心素服號哭於西階下，藉草東向，經三日，敕書唁焉。

translations.literal: Shanxin in plain dress wailed below the western steps, spread grass, and faced east for three days; an edict letter condoled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin wailed in plain dress on the western steps, spread grass, and faced east for three days until an edict condoled with him.

sentences.zh: 明日，有詔就館拜通直散騎常侍，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: The next day an edict came to the lodge appointing him Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and granting one suit of clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Next day an edict at the lodge made him Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry and gave him a suit of clothes.

sentences.zh: 善心哭盡哀，入房改服，復出北面立，垂涕再拜受詔。

translations.literal: Shanxin wept out his grief, went inside to change garments, came out again and stood facing north, and with tears bowed twice to receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He wept out his grief, changed clothes, came out facing north, and with tears received the edict bowing twice.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃朝服泣于殿下，悲不能興。

translations.literal: The next day, in court dress, he wept below the hall and was too overcome with grief to rise.
translations.idiomatic: The next day in court dress he wept below the hall, too stricken to rise.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「我平陳國，唯獲此人。

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those at his side and said, "In pacifying Chen I gained only this man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told those beside him, "In pacifying Chen I gained only this man.

sentences.zh: 既能懷其舊君，即我誠臣也。」

translations.literal: Since he can cherish his former ruler, he is my loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: One who cherishes his former ruler will be loyal to me.

sentences.zh: 敕以本官直門下省，賜物千段、草馬二十匹。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in his former office at the Department of the Imperial Secretariat, and granted a thousand lengths of goods and twenty rough horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to his former post at the Secretariat and given a thousand lengths of goods and twenty rough horses.

sentences.zh: 從幸太山，還，授虞部侍郎。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Mount Tai, on return he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Parks.
translations.idiomatic: After accompanying the emperor to Mount Tai he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Parks.

sentences.zh: 十六年，有神雀降于含章闥，上召百官賜宴，告以此瑞。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year a divine sparrow descended at the Hanzhang Gate; the emperor summoned the hundred officials to a banquet and announced this auspice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year a divine sparrow alighted at Hanzhang Gate; the emperor feasted the officials and announced the omen.

sentences.zh: 善心於坐請紙筆，制《神雀頌》奏之。

translations.literal: At the gathering Shanxin asked for paper and brush, composed the "Hymn to the Divine Sparrow," and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin asked for brush and paper, wrote the Hymn to the Divine Sparrow, and presented it.

sentences.zh: 上甚悅曰：「我見神雀，共皇后觀之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said, "I saw the divine sparrow and viewed it together with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with delight, "I saw the sparrow with the empress.

sentences.zh: 今且召公等入，適述此事。

translations.literal: Now I have just summoned you gentlemen in to tell you of this very matter.
translations.idiomatic: I have just called you in to tell you of it.

sentences.zh: 善心於坐始知，即能成頌。

translations.literal: Shanxin only learned of it at the gathering yet could at once complete the hymn.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin learned of it only at table yet finished the hymn at once.

sentences.zh: 文不加點，筆不停毫，常聞此言，今見其事。」

translations.literal: The text needed no dotting, the brush did not pause—one often hears this saying; today I have seen it in deed.
translations.idiomatic: No revision needed, brush never pausing—I have heard the saying; today I saw it.

sentences.zh: 因賜物二百段。

translations.literal: He thereupon granted two hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He granted two hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 十七年，除秘書丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Secretariat Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became Secretariat Assistant.

sentences.zh: 時秘藏圖籍，尚多淆亂。

translations.literal: At the time the secret repository of books and maps was still much confused.
translations.idiomatic: Books in the secret repository were still in great disorder.

sentences.zh: 善心效阮孝緒《七錄》，更制《七林》，各總敘冠於篇首。

translations.literal: Shanxin modeled himself on Ruan Xiaoxu's Seven Records and compiled the Seven Forests, placing a general preface at the head of each section.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin took Ruan Xiaoxu's Seven Records as his model and compiled the Seven Forests, with a general preface at the head of each section.

sentences.zh: 又于部錄之下明作者之意，區分類例焉。

translations.literal: Beneath each departmental catalogue he clarified the author's intent and distinguished categories and examples.
translations.idiomatic: Under each departmental catalogue he explained the author's intent and sorted categories and examples.

sentences.zh: 又奏追李文博、陸從典等學者十許人，正定經史錯謬。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to recall more than ten scholars such as Li Wenbo and Lu Congdian to correct errors in the Classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to recall more than ten scholars including Li Wenbo and Lu Congdian to correct errors in the Classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，攝黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou he acted as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Renshou he served as acting Gentleman of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 二年，加攝太常少卿，與牛弘等議定禮樂，秘書丞、黃門並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he was additionally made Acting Junior Minister of Ceremonies; with Niu Hong and others he deliberated on rites and music, while retaining his posts as Secretariat Assistant and Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was additionally Acting Junior Minister of Ceremonies; with Niu Hong and others he settled rites and music while keeping his former posts.

sentences.zh: 四年，留守京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was left to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝崩于仁壽宮，煬帝秘不發喪，先易留宮人，出除岩州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor died at Renshou Palace; Emperor Yang kept the death secret, first replaced the palace women, and sent Shanxin out as Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Renshou Palace, Yang kept the death secret, replaced the palace women, and sent Shanxin out as Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 逢漢王諒反，不之任。

translations.literal: When Prince Han of Liang rebelled he did not take up the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Han of Liang rebelled he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，轉禮部侍郎，奏薦儒者徐文遠為國子博士，包愷、陸德明、褚徽、魯世達之輩，並加品秩，授為學官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites; he memorialized recommending the Confucian Xu Wenyuan as National University Doctor, and men such as Bao Kai, Lu Deming, Chu Hui, and Lu Shida were all given ranks and appointed as instructors.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye's first year he became Vice Minister of Rites and recommended Xu Wenyuan and others as instructors in the National University.

sentences.zh: 其年，副納言楊達為冀州道大使，以稱旨，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: That year, as deputy to Censor-in-Chief Yang Da, envoy on the Jizhou circuit, he pleased the emperor and was granted five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: That year, as Yang Da's deputy on the Jizhou mission, he pleased the throne and received five hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 左衛大將軍宇文述每日借本部兵數十人以供私役，常半日而罷。

translations.literal: General of the Left Guard Yuwen Shu daily borrowed several tens of men from his command for private service, often dismissing them by midday.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu daily impressed dozens of his own troops for private errands, often for only half a day.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫梁毗奏劾之。

translations.literal: Imperial Censor Liang Pi memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Censor Liang Pi impeached him.

sentences.zh: 上方以腹心委述，初付法官推，千餘人皆稱被役。

translations.literal: The emperor above entrusted Shu as a confidant; at first he handed the case to the judges for investigation, and more than a thousand men all said they had been impressed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor trusted Shu; the case went to the judges and over a thousand men said they had been impressed.

sentences.zh: 經二十餘日，法官候伺上旨，乃言役不滿日，其數雖多，不合通計，縱令有實，亦無罪。

translations.literal: After more than twenty days the judges watched the emperor's intent and then said the service did not amount to a full day; though the number was large, it should not be totaled together—even if true, there was no crime.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days the judges read the emperor's mind and ruled that service did not amount to a full day—no crime even if true.

sentences.zh: 諸兵士聞之，更雲初不被役。

translations.literal: When the soldiers heard this they again said they had not been impressed at all.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the soldiers then denied they had been impressed at all.

sentences.zh: 上欲釋之，付議虛實，百僚咸議為虛。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to release him and submitted the matter for debate on truth or falsehood; the hundred officials all argued it was false.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to absolve Shu; the officials all called the charges false.

sentences.zh: 善心以為述于仗衛之所，抽兵私役，雖不滿日，闕于宿衛，與常役所部，情狀乃殊。

translations.literal: Shanxin held that Shu, in the place of armed guard, drew troops for private service; though not a full day, it fell short of night watch—and the circumstances differed from ordinary impressed labor.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin argued that drawing guards for private labor, even under a day, still breached night watch—and differed from ordinary corvée.

sentences.zh: 又兵多下番，散還本府，分道追至，不謀同辭。

translations.literal: Moreover many soldiers were off rotation and had scattered back to their original offices; pursued separately along different routes, they had not agreed on one story.
translations.idiomatic: Many men were off duty and scattered home; pursued separately they had not agreed in advance.

sentences.zh: 今殆一月，方始翻覆，奸狀分明，此何可舍？

translations.literal: Now after nearly a month they have only just reversed their testimony—the fraudulent conduct is clear; how can this be pardoned?
translations.idiomatic: Only after a month did they reverse their story—the fraud was obvious and must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 蘇威、楊汪等二十餘人同善心議，其餘皆議免罪。

translations.literal: Su Wei, Yang Wang, and more than twenty others agreed with Shanxin; the rest all argued for exemption from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Yang Wang, and twenty others sided with Shanxin; the rest favored acquittal.

sentences.zh: 煬帝可免者之奏。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang approved the memorial for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang approved acquittal.

sentences.zh: 後數月，述譖善心曰：「陳叔寶卒，善心共周羅碶、虞世基、袁充、蔡徵等同往送葬。

translations.literal: Several months later Shu slandered Shanxin, saying, "When Chen Shubao died, Shanxin went with Zhou Luochen, Yu Shiji, Yuan Chong, Cai Zheng, and others to escort the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Shu accused Shanxin of attending Chen Shubao's funeral with Zhou Luochen and others.

sentences.zh: 善心為祭文，謂為'陛下 '。

translations.literal: Shanxin composed a sacrificial text and used the term 'Your Majesty.'
translations.idiomatic: In the sacrificial text Shanxin used 'Your Majesty.'

sentences.zh: 敢於今日加叔寶尊號。」

translations.literal: He dared on this day to add the exalted title to Shubao.
translations.idiomatic: He had dared to give Shubao an imperial title that day.

sentences.zh: 召問有實，自援古例，事得釋，而甚惡之。

translations.literal: Summoned and questioned, the facts were established; he cited ancient precedents himself and the matter was released, but the emperor deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Questioned, he admitted it, cited precedent, and was released—but the emperor hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 又太史奏帝即位年與堯時符合，善心議以國哀甫爾，不宜稱賀。

translations.literal: Also the Grand Astrologer reported that the year of the emperor's accession matched the era of Yao; Shanxin argued that national mourning had only just ended and congratulations were inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: When the astrologer said the accession year matched Yao's era, Shanxin said national mourning forbade congratulations.

sentences.zh: 述諷御史劾之，左遷給事郎，降品二等。

translations.literal: Shu prompted the censor to impeach him; he was demoted to Drafting Attendant and reduced two grades in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had him impeached; he was demoted to Drafting Attendant and dropped two grades.

sentences.zh: 四年，撰《方物志》，奏之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he compiled the Record of Regional Products and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he presented his Record of Regional Products.

sentences.zh: 七年，從至涿郡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed the emperor to Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he followed the emperor to Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 帝方自禦戎以東討，善心上封事，忤旨免官。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to lead the army east in person; Shanxin submitted a sealed memorial, offended the intent, and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor prepared to campaign east in person, Shanxin's sealed memorial offended him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其年復征守給事郎。

translations.literal: That year he was again summoned to serve as Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was summoned back as Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言及文帝受命之符，因問鬼神之事，敕善心與崔祖浚撰《靈異記》十卷。

translations.literal: The emperor once spoke of Emperor Wen's tokens of mandate and then asked about ghosts and spirits; he ordered Shanxin and Cui Zujun to compile the Record of Strange Events in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about ghosts and spirits, the emperor ordered Shanxin and Cui Zujun to compile the Record of Strange Events in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 初，善心父撰著《梁史》，未就而歿。

translations.literal: Earlier Shanxin's father had compiled the History of Liang but died before finishing.
translations.idiomatic: His father had begun a History of Liang but died before finishing.

sentences.zh: 善心述成父志，修續家書。

translations.literal: Shanxin carried out his father's intent and continued the family book.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin fulfilled his father's aim and continued the family history.

sentences.zh: 其《序傳》末述製作之意，曰：

translations.literal: At the end of the Autobiographical Account he stated the intent of his compilation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Autobiographical Account he explained why he wrote, saying:

sentences.zh: 謹按太素將萌，洪荒初判。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering: when the Grand Simplicity was about to stir, the primordial chaos was first divided.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry shows: as Grand Simplicity stirred, primordial chaos was first divided.

sentences.zh: 乾儀資始，辰象所以正時；

translations.literal: Heaven's pattern provides the beginning; the stars and constellations thereby correct the seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's pattern begins all things; stars and seasons set the calendar right;

sentences.zh: 坤載厚生，品物於焉播氣。

translations.literal: Earth's bearing thickly generates life; the myriad things therein receive their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Earth bears and nourishes; the myriad creatures breathe there.

sentences.zh: 參三才而育德，肖二統而降靈。

translations.literal: Aligning the three powers to nurture virtue, modeling the two systems to bring down the numinous—
translations.idiomatic: Harmonizing the three powers to cultivate virtue, shaping the two models to bring down the sacred—

sentences.zh: 有黎人焉，為之君長；

translations.literal: there were the black-haired people, for whom rulers were made;
translations.idiomatic: the common people received rulers;

sentences.zh: 有貴賤矣，為其宗極。

translations.literal: there were noble and base, for whom the apex of the clan was set.
translations.idiomatic: noble and base found their clan's summit.

sentences.zh: 保上天之眷命，膺下土之樂推，莫不執太方，振長策，感召風雲，驅馳英俊。

translations.literal: Receiving heaven's favoring mandate, accepting the people's joyful elevation below, none failed to grasp the great square, shake the long whip, summon wind and cloud, and drive the outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's mandate and the people's acclaim: each grasped the great compass, shook the long whip, called up wind and cloud, and drove the worthy.

sentences.zh: 干戈揖讓，取之也殊功；

translations.literal: By arms or by yielding, the means of taking differed in merit;
translations.idiomatic: By arms or by yielding—the taking differed;

sentences.zh: 鼎玉龜符，成之也一致。

translations.literal: by tripods, jade, and tortoise credentials, the completion was one in principle.
translations.idiomatic: by tripod, jade, and tortoise sign—the completion was one.

sentences.zh: 革命創制，竹素之道稍彰；

translations.literal: Revolution and new institutions—the way of bamboo and silk gradually appeared;
translations.idiomatic: Revolution made institutions; writing on bamboo and silk slowly emerged;

sentences.zh: 紀事記言，筆墨之官漸著。

translations.literal: recording events and words—the office of brush and ink gradually stood forth.
translations.idiomatic: recording deeds and words—the scribe's office slowly rose.

sentences.zh: 炎、農以往，存其名而漏其跡；

translations.literal: From the Flame and Agricultural emperors onward, names were preserved while traces were lost;
translations.idiomatic: From the Flame and Agricultural age, names survived but traces were lost;

sentences.zh: 黃、軒以來，晦其文而顯其質。

translations.literal: from the Yellow and August emperors onward, texts were hidden while substance was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: from the Yellow and August Sovereigns, text was veiled but substance shown.

sentences.zh: 登丘納麓，具訓誥及典謨；

translations.literal: Ascending the hill and receiving the foot of the mountain—there were the Instructions and the Canon;
translations.idiomatic: On the hill, at the mountain's foot—instructions and canons were complete;

sentences.zh: 貫昴入房，傳夏正與殷祀。

translations.literal: piercing the Pleiades and entering the Chamber—there were transmitted the Xia calendar and Yin sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: through the stars, into the chamber—Xia's calendar and Yin's rites passed down.

sentences.zh: 洎辨方正位，論時計功。

translations.literal: When it came to distinguishing directions and fixing positions, discussing seasons and reckoning merit—
translations.idiomatic: Fixing directions and seasons, weighing time and merit—

sentences.zh: 南北左右，兼四名之別；

translations.literal: north, south, east, and west, together with the four names' distinctions;
translations.idiomatic: the four quarters each had their name;

sentences.zh: 《檮杌》、《乘》車，擅一家之稱。

translations.literal: the Tuwu and the Sheng chariot, each monopolizing one school's title.
translations.idiomatic: Tuwu and Sheng each claimed a school.

sentences.zh: 國惡雖諱，君舉必書。

translations.literal: Though a state's ugliness was tabooed, a ruler's actions must be written.
translations.idiomatic: A state's shame might be hidden, but a ruler's acts must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 故賊子亂臣，天下大懼，元龜明鏡，昭然可察。

translations.literal: Therefore rebellious sons and disorderly ministers made the world greatly fear; the great tortoise and bright mirror made it clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious sons and treacherous ministers terrified the world; the mirror and tortoise made guilt plain.

sentences.zh: 及三郊遞襲，五勝相沿，俱稱百谷之王，並以四海自任。

translations.literal: When the three suburban sacrifices succeeded one another and the five victories followed in turn, all called themselves kings of the hundred grains and took the four seas as their charge.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice followed sacrifice, victory followed victory—each called himself king of grain and lord of the seas.

sentences.zh: 重光累德，何世無哉。

translations.literal: Repeated brilliance and accumulated virtue—what age lacks them?
translations.idiomatic: Glory heaped on glory—what age has lacked it?

sentences.zh: 逮有梁之興，君臨天下，江左建國，莫斯為盛。

translations.literal: When Liang arose it ruled the world; establishing the state in the Jiangzuo region, none was more flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rose over the realm, its founding in Jiangzuo was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 受命在於一君，繼統傳乎四主。

translations.literal: The mandate was received by one ruler; the succession passed through four sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: One ruler received the mandate; four sovereigns passed the succession.

sentences.zh: 克昌四十八載，餘祚五十六年。

translations.literal: Prosperity lasted forty-eight years; remaining fortune fifty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-eight years of splendor; fifty-six of lingering fortune.

sentences.zh: 武皇帝出自諸生，爰升寶曆。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu came forth from the student class and thereupon ascended the imperial calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu rose from the schools to the throne.

sentences.zh: 拯百王之弊，救萬姓之危。

translations.literal: He rescued the abuses of a hundred kings and saved the myriad people from peril.
translations.idiomatic: He ended the abuses of ages and rescued the people from ruin.

sentences.zh: 反澆季之末流，登上皇之獨道。

translations.literal: He reversed the last current of a decadent age and ascended the unique Way of the Supreme Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back decadence and mounted the Supreme Way.

sentences.zh: 朝多君子，野無遺賢，禮樂必備，憲章咸舉，弘深慈於不殺，濟大忍于無刑。

translations.literal: The court had many gentlemen; the wilds had no overlooked worthies; rites and music were complete and statutes all enacted; he extended deep kindness in not killing and aided great forbearance in having no punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside brimmed with worthies; rites and laws were complete; mercy deep, punishment rare.

sentences.zh: 蕩蕩巍巍，可為稱首。

translations.literal: Vast and lofty—he could be called foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Grand and towering—he could stand first.

sentences.zh: 屬陰戎入潁，羯胡侵洛。

translations.literal: Then the northern barbarians entered Ying and the Jie barbarians invaded Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then northern tribes entered Ying and Jie raiders took Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 沸騰墋黷，三季之所未聞；

translations.literal: Boiling turmoil and defiled slaughter—what the three degenerate ages had not heard;
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil and slaughter unheard since the three degenerate ages;

sentences.zh: 掃地滔天，一元之所巨厄。

translations.literal: sweeping the ground and flooding heaven—the great calamity of a unified age.
translations.idiomatic: heaven and earth overturned—the unified realm's great disaster.

sentences.zh: 廊廟有序，翦成狐兔之場；

translations.literal: Though the court had order, it was cut into a field of foxes and hares;
translations.idiomatic: The court in order became a warren for fox and hare;

sentences.zh: 圭帛有儀，碎夫犬羊之手。

translations.literal: though ritual jade and silks had their forms, they were shattered in the hands of dogs and goats.
translations.idiomatic: jade and silk were smashed by dog and goat.

sentences.zh: 福善積而身禍，仁義存而國亡，豈天道歟？

translations.literal: Good fortune accumulated yet the person suffered calamity; benevolence and righteousness remained yet the state perished—is this the Way of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Virtue amassed yet the man suffered; benevolence lived yet the state fell—was this Heaven?

sentences.zh: 豈人事歟？

translations.literal: Is it human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Or was it man?

sentences.zh: 嘗別論之，在於《序論》之卷。

translations.literal: I once discussed this separately in the chapter of the Prefatory Discourse.
translations.idiomatic: I have treated this at length in the Prefatory Discourse.

sentences.zh: 先君昔在前代，早懷述作，凡撰《齊書》為五十卷；

translations.literal: My late father in former times early cherished composition; in all he compiled the History of Qi in fifty juan;
translations.idiomatic: My father early took up writing; his History of Qi ran fifty juan;

sentences.zh: 《梁書》紀傳，隨事勒成及闕而未就者，目錄注為一百八卷。

translations.literal: the annals and biographies of the History of Liang, completed as events allowed and what remained unfinished, were catalogued and noted as one hundred eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: his Liang annals and biographies, finished or not, were catalogued at one hundred eight juan.

sentences.zh: 梁室交喪，墳籍銷盡。

translations.literal: When the Liang house was lost together, tomb records were utterly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell, the archives were burned away.

sentences.zh: 塚壁皆殘，不准無所盜；

translations.literal: Tomb walls were all ruined—Buzhun had nothing left to steal;
translations.idiomatic: Tomb walls collapsed—nothing left to steal;

sentences.zh: 帷囊同毀，陳農何以求！

translations.literal: curtain bags likewise destroyed—how could Chen Nong seek them!
translations.idiomatic: bags destroyed—nothing left to gather.

sentences.zh: 秦儒既坑，先王之道將墜；

translations.literal: When Qin scholars were buried in pits, the way of the former kings was about to fall;
translations.idiomatic: Qin's burying of scholars nearly ended the ancient Way;

sentences.zh: 漢臣徒請，口授之文亦絕。

translations.literal: when Han ministers vainly requested, orally transmitted texts also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Han's vain pleas could not restore orally transmitted texts.

sentences.zh: 所撰之書，一時亡散。

translations.literal: The books he compiled were scattered at once.
translations.idiomatic: His books were lost at once.

sentences.zh: 有陳初建，詔為史官，補闕拾遺，心識口誦，依舊目錄，更加修撰，且成百卷，已有六帙五十八卷上秘閣訖。

translations.literal: When Chen was first established an edict made him Historian, to repair omissions and gather what was lost, keeping the old catalogue in mind and further revising—altogether one hundred juan, with six fascicles of fifty-eight juan already submitted to the secret repository.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen began, he was ordered to repair the history; from memory and the old catalogue he brought it to one hundred juan, fifty-eight already in the secret vault.

sentences.zh: 善心早嬰荼蓼，弗克荷薪，太建之末，頻抗表聞，至德之初，蒙授史任。

translations.literal: Shanxin early suffered hardship and could not bear the firewood burden; at the end of Taijian he repeatedly submitted memorials; at the beginning of Zhide he received the historiographer's charge.
translations.idiomatic: I was early orphaned and could not carry the load; only at Zhide did I receive the historian's post.

sentences.zh: 方願緗素採訪，門庭記錄，俯勵弱才，仰成先志。

translations.literal: I had hoped to gather silk and plain, record at gate and courtyard, bend my weak talent downward, and look up to fulfill my father's intent.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to collect and record, to bend my small talent and fulfill my father's will.

sentences.zh: 而單宗少強近，虛室類原、顏，退屏無所交遊，棲遲不求進益。

translations.literal: Yet being of a solitary clan with few powerful kin, an empty house like Yuan and Yan, he withdrew and had no companions, lingering without seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Yet of a solitary clan with few powerful kin, his house empty as Yuan or Yan, he withdrew without companions and lingered without seeking advancement.

sentences.zh: 假班嗣之書，徒聞其語；

translations.literal: Borrowing Ban Si's book, he only heard its words;
translations.idiomatic: Borrowing Ban Si's book, he only heard its words;

sentences.zh: 給王隱之筆，未見其人。

translations.literal: given Wang Yin's brush, he never saw the man.
translations.idiomatic: given Wang Yin's brush, he never saw the man.

sentences.zh: 加以庸瑣涼能，孤陋末學，參職郎署，兼撰《陳史》，致此書延時，未即成續。

translations.literal: Moreover, with mediocre and slight talent, a solitary and shallow late learner, serving in the Secretariat while also compiling the History of Chen, this book was delayed and not soon completed.
translations.idiomatic: With mediocre talent and shallow learning, he served in the Secretariat while also compiling the History of Chen, so the work was long delayed.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，以台郎入聘，屬本邑淪覆，他鄉播遷，行人失時，將命不復。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming he entered as a mission attendant; his native district fell, he was driven to wander abroad, envoys lost their season, and he could not return with his charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year two he went as a mission attendant; his home fell, he wandered abroad, and could not return with his charge.

sentences.zh: 望都亭而長慟，遷別館而懸壺。

translations.literal: He gazed at the capital pavilion and wept long; moving to another lodge he hung up his practice.
translations.idiomatic: He gazed at the capital pavilion and wept long; at another lodge he hung up his practice.

sentences.zh: 家史舊書，在後蕩盡。

translations.literal: The family's old histories were afterward swept away.
translations.idiomatic: The family's old histories were afterward swept away.

sentences.zh: 今止有六卷獲存，又並缺落失次。

translations.literal: Now only six juan survived, and these too were defective and out of order.
translations.idiomatic: Only six juan survived, and even these were defective and out of order.

sentences.zh: 自入京邑以求，隨見補葺，略成七十卷：四《帝紀》八卷，《后妃》一卷，三《太子錄》一卷，為一帙十卷；

translations.literal: Since entering the capital he patched as he could, roughly completing seventy juan: four Imperial Annals in eight juan, Consorts one juan, three Crown Prince Records one juan—one fascicle of ten juan;
translations.idiomatic: Since entering the capital he patched as he could to roughly seventy juan: four Imperial Annals in eight juan, Consorts one juan, three Crown Prince Records one juan—one fascicle of ten juan;

sentences.zh: 《宗室王侯列傳》一帙十卷；

translations.literal: Noble Clans and Marquis Biographies one fascicle of ten juan;
translations.idiomatic: Noble Clans and Marquis Biographies one fascicle of ten juan;

sentences.zh: 《具臣列傳》二帙二十卷；

translations.literal: Full Ministers Biographies two fascicles of twenty juan;
translations.idiomatic: Full Ministers Biographies two fascicles of twenty juan;

sentences.zh: 《外戚傳》一卷，《孝德傳》一卷，《誠臣傳》一卷，《文苑傳》二卷，《儒林傳》二卷，《逸人傳》一卷，《數術傳》一卷，《籓臣傳》一卷，合一帙十卷；

translations.literal: External Kin one juan, Filial Virtue one juan, Loyal Ministers one juan, Literary Grove two juan, Confucian Scholars two juan, Recluses one juan, Number and Arts one juan, Feudatory Ministers one juan—together one fascicle of ten juan;
translations.idiomatic: External Kin one juan, Filial Virtue one juan, Loyal Ministers one juan, Literary Grove two juan, Confucian Scholars two juan, Recluses one juan, Number and Arts one juan, Feudatory Ministers one juan—one fascicle of ten juan;

sentences.zh: 《止足傳》一卷，《列女傳》一卷，《權幸傳》一卷，《羯賊傳》二卷，《逆臣傳》二卷，《叛臣傳》二卷，《敘傳論述》一卷，合一帙十卷。

translations.literal: Knowing When to Stop one juan, Notable Women one juan, Favorites one juan, Jie Bandits two juan, Rebellious Ministers two juan, Defecting Ministers two juan, Autobiographical Discourse one juan—together one fascicle of ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing When to Stop one juan, Notable Women one juan, Favorites one juan, Jie Bandits two juan, Rebellious Ministers two juan, Defecting Ministers two juan, Autobiographical Discourse one juan—one fascicle of ten juan.

sentences.zh: 凡稱史臣者皆先君所言，下稱名案者皆善心補闕。

translations.literal: Where it says "Historian" it is all the late father's words; where it says "named case" it is Shanxin's supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: Passages marked "Historian" are the late father's words; those marked "named case" are Shanxin's supplements.

sentences.zh: 別為《敘論》一篇，托於《敘傳》之末。

translations.literal: He separately composed one Discourse, placed at the end of the Autobiographical Account.
translations.idiomatic: He separately composed one Discourse, placed at the end of the Autobiographical Account.

sentences.zh: 十年，又從至懷遠鎮，加授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he again followed to Huaiyuan garrison and was given additional title Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he again followed to Huaiyuan garrison and was given additional title Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍雁門，攝左親侍武賁郎將，領江南兵宿衛殿省。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen he acted as Left Guard Attendant and General of the Martial Tiger Guard, leading Jiangnan troops to guard the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen he acted as Left Guard Attendant and General of the Martial Tiger Guard, leading Jiangnan troops to guard the palace.

sentences.zh: 駕幸江都，追敘前勳，授通議大夫，詔還本品，行給事郎。

translations.literal: When the carriage went to Jiangdu, former merit was recalled and he was made Grand Master for Discussion; an edict restored his former rank and he served as Acting Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the carriage went to Jiangdu, former merit was recalled and he was made Grand Master for Discussion; an edict restored his former rank and he served as Acting Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，化及弑逆之日，隋官盡詣朝堂謁賀，善心獨不至。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, on the day Huaji murdered the emperor, all Sui officials went to the court hall to offer congratulations; only Shanxin did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen, on the day Huaji murdered the emperor, all Sui officials went to congratulate; only Shanxin stayed away.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁馳告曰：「天子已崩，宇文將軍攝政，合朝文武，莫不咸集。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren hurried to tell him, "The Son of Heaven is dead; General Yuwen holds the regency; all court civil and military have assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hongren hurried to tell him, "The Son of Heaven is dead; General Yuwen holds the regency; all court civil and military have assembled.

sentences.zh: 天道人事，自有代終，何預叔而低徊若此？」

translations.literal: Heaven's way and human affairs have their turn of ending—what has it to do with you that you linger thus?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way and human affairs turn and end—why do you linger so?

sentences.zh: 善心怒之，不肯隨去。

translations.literal: Shanxin was angry and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin was angry and would not go.

sentences.zh: 弘仁返走上馬，泣而言曰：「將軍于叔全無惡意，忽自求死，豈不痛哉！」

translations.literal: Hongren turned back, mounted his horse, and wept, saying, "The general meant your uncle no harm; to seek death suddenly—how is it not painful!
translations.idiomatic: Hongren turned back, mounted, and wept, "The general meant your uncle no harm; to seek death so suddenly—how painful!

sentences.zh: 還告唐奉議，以狀白化及，遣人就宅執至朝堂。

translations.literal: He returned and told Tang Fengyi, who reported to Huaji, who sent men to seize him at his house and bring him to the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: He told Tang Fengyi, who reported to Huaji, who sent men to seize him at home and bring him to court.

sentences.zh: 化及令釋之，善心不舞蹈而出。

translations.literal: Huaji ordered him released; Shanxin went out without the ritual dance of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji ordered him released; Shanxin left without the ritual dance of thanks.

sentences.zh: 化及目送之，曰：「此大負氣。」

translations.literal: Huaji watched him go and said, "This man has great upright spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji watched him go and said, "This man has great spirit.

sentences.zh: 命捉來，罵云：「我好欲放你，敢如此不遜！」

translations.literal: He ordered him seized again and cursed, "I was about to release you—how dare you be so insolent!
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him seized again and cursed, "I meant to release you—how dare you be so insolent!

sentences.zh: 其黨輒牽曳，遂害之。

translations.literal: His followers dragged him off and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His followers dragged him off and killed him.

sentences.zh: 及越王稱制，贈左光祿大夫，封高陽縣公，諡曰文節。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yue assumed power, Shanxin was posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Palace and Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yue assumed power, Shanxin was posthumously made Left Grand Master of the Palace and Duke of Gaoyang, posthumous name Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 善心母范氏，梁太子中舍人孝才之女也。

translations.literal: Shanxin's mother Lady Fan was daughter of Liang's Crown Prince Attendant Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxin's mother Lady Fan was daughter of Liang's Crown Prince Attendant Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 少寡，養孤，博學有高節。

translations.literal: Widowed young, she raised the orphan; broadly learned and of high integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed young, she raised him; learned and of high integrity.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝知之，敕尚食每獻時新，常遣分賜。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui knew her and ordered the Imperial Kitchen to present seasonal delicacies and often send shares to her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen knew her and ordered seasonal delicacies sent from the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 嘗詔範入內，侍皇后講讀。

translations.literal: She was once summoned within to attend the empress in reading and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: She was once summoned to attend the empress in reading and discussion.

sentences.zh: 封永樂郡君。

translations.literal: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongle commandery.
translations.idiomatic: She was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongle commandery.

sentences.zh: 及善心遇禍，范氏九十有二，臨喪不哭，撫柩曰：「能死國難，我有兒矣。」

translations.literal: When Shanxin met disaster, Lady Fan was ninety-two; facing the coffin she did not weep but stroked it and said, "To die for the state's calamity—I have a son.
translations.idiomatic: When Shanxin met disaster, Lady Fan was ninety-two; she did not weep but stroked the coffin and said, "To die for the state—I have a son.

sentences.zh: 因臥不食，後十餘日亦終。

translations.literal: She thereupon lay down and ate nothing, and after more than ten days also died.
translations.idiomatic: She lay down and ate nothing, and after ten days also died.

sentences.zh: 李文博，博陵人。

translations.literal: Li Wenbo was a man of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenbo was a man of Boling.

sentences.zh: 性貞介鯁直，好學不倦。

translations.literal: By nature upright, firm, and straight; he loved learning without tiring.
translations.idiomatic: By nature upright, firm, and straight; he loved learning without tiring.

sentences.zh: 至於教義名理，特所留心。

translations.literal: As for doctrine, meaning, and principle, he paid special attention.
translations.idiomatic: As for doctrine, meaning, and principle, he paid special attention.

sentences.zh: 每讀書至安危得失，忠臣烈士，未嘗不反覆吟玩。

translations.literal: Whenever in reading he reached safety and peril, gain and loss, loyal ministers and martyrs, he never failed to ponder and recite repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he read of safety and peril, loyal ministers and martyrs, he pondered and recited repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為羽騎尉。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang he served as Captain of Feathered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang he served as Captain of Feathered Riders.

sentences.zh: 特為吏部侍郎薛道衡所知，恆令在査事帷中，披檢書史，並察己行事。

translations.literal: He was especially known to Vice Minister of Personnel Xue Daoheng, who always had him in the investigation curtain, examining books and histories and also observing his own conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daoheng especially valued him, keeping him in the investigation curtain to examine books and observe his conduct.

sentences.zh: 若遇政教善事，即抄撰記錄，如選用疏謬，即委之臧否。

translations.literal: When he encountered good matters in government and teaching he copied and recorded them; when appointments were careless he entrusted criticism of praise and blame.
translations.idiomatic: Good policies he recorded; careless appointments he criticized.

sentences.zh: 道衡每得其語，莫不忻然從之。

translations.literal: Whenever Daoheng received his words he gladly followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng gladly followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 後直秘書內省，典校群籍。

translations.literal: Later he served in the inner Secretariat, collating the mass of books.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served in the inner Secretariat, collating books.

sentences.zh: 守道居貧，晏如也。

translations.literal: He kept the Way and lived in poverty, at ease therein.
translations.idiomatic: He kept the Way and lived in poverty, at ease.

sentences.zh: 雖衣食乏絕。

translations.literal: Though food and clothing were exhausted,
translations.idiomatic: Though food and clothing failed,

sentences.zh: 而清操愈厲，不妄通賓客，恆以禮法自處，儕輩莫不敬焉。

translations.literal: his pure conduct grew sterner; he did not casually receive guests and always regulated himself by ritual—his peers all respected him.
translations.idiomatic: his integrity grew sterner; he received no casual guests and lived by ritual—his peers respected him.

sentences.zh: 道衡知其貧，每延於家，給以資費。

translations.literal: Daoheng knew his poverty and often invited him home, supplying expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Daoheng knew his poverty and often fed and supplied him at home.

sentences.zh: 文博商略古今政教得失，如指諸掌。

translations.literal: Wenbo discussed the gains and losses of government and teaching ancient and modern as if pointing to his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo discussed government ancient and modern as if on his palm.

sentences.zh: 然無吏幹。

translations.literal: Yet he had no administrative skill.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had no administrative skill.

sentences.zh: 稍遷校書郎，出為縣丞，遂得下考，數歲不調。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Collator, went out as county assistant, received a low assessment, and for several years received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Collator, then county assistant with a low assessment; for years no new post.

sentences.zh: 道衡為司隸大夫，遇之東都尚書省，甚嗟湣之，奏為從事。

translations.literal: When Daoheng became Censor-in-Chief he met him at the Eastern Capital Secretariat and pitied him greatly, memorializing to make him an aide.
translations.idiomatic: As Censor-in-Chief Daoheng met him at the Eastern Capital and pitied him, memorializing to make him an aide.

sentences.zh: 因謂齊王司馬李綱曰：「今日遂遇文博，得奏用之。」

translations.literal: He therefore said to the Prince of Qi's Major Li Gang, "Today I have met Wenbo and can memorialize to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He told Li Gang, "Today I have met Wenbo and can employ him.

sentences.zh: 以為歡笑。

translations.literal: He took it as a jest.
translations.idiomatic: He said it laughing.

sentences.zh: 其見賞知音如此。

translations.literal: Such was the regard in which he was prized and known.
translations.idiomatic: Such was how he was prized.

sentences.zh: 在洛下，曾詣房玄齡，相送出衢路。

translations.literal: In Luoyang he once visited Fang Xuanling and saw him off to the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he once visited Fang Xuanling and saw him off to the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 玄齡謂曰：「公生平志尚，唯在正直。

translations.literal: Xuanling said to him, "Your lifelong aim lies only in uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling said, "Your lifelong aim is uprightness alone.

sentences.zh: 今既得為從事，故應有會素心。

translations.literal: Now that you have become an aide, you ought to realize your former intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now as an aide you ought to realize that intent.

sentences.zh: 比來激濁揚清，所為多少？」

translations.literal: Recently, in stirring the muddy and raising the clear, how much have you done?
translations.idiomatic: Recently, stirring the muddy and raising the clear—how much have you done?

sentences.zh: 文博遂奮臂厲聲曰：「夫清其流者必潔其源，正其末者須端其本。

translations.literal: Wenbo then flung his arm and said sharply, "To clear the stream one must cleanse the source; to straighten the branch one must square the root.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo flung his arm and said sharply, "Clear the stream at the source; square the root before the branch.

sentences.zh: 今政源混亂，雖日免十貪郡守，亦何所益！」

translations.literal: Now the source of government is confused; though you daily dismiss ten greedy commandery administrators, what good is it!
translations.idiomatic: The source of government is confused; dismissing ten greedy prefects a day does no good!

sentences.zh: 其率直疾惡，不知忌諱，皆如此類。

translations.literal: His bluntness and hatred of evil without regard for taboo were all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt hatred of evil without taboo was all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 時朝政浸壞，人多贓賄，唯文博不改其操。

translations.literal: At the time court government was gradually ruined and many took bribes; only Wenbo did not change his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Court government rotted and many took bribes; only Wenbo held his course.

sentences.zh: 論者以此貴之。

translations.literal: Critics therefore honored him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Critics honored him for this.

sentences.zh: 遭亂播遷，不知所終。

translations.literal: Caught in disorder and driven about, his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Caught in disorder, his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 初，文博在內省校書，虞世基子亦在其內，盛飾容服而未有所知。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wenbo was collating books in the inner province, Yu Shiji's son was also within, richly adorned yet knowing nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenbo collated in the inner province, Yu Shiji's son was there, richly adorned yet knowing nothing.

sentences.zh: 文博因從容問之年紀，答云十八。

translations.literal: Wenbo casually asked his age; he answered eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo asked his age; he answered eighteen.

sentences.zh: 文博乃謂曰：「昔賈誼當此之年，議論何事？

translations.literal: Wenbo then said to him, "When Jia Yi was this age, what did he discuss?
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo said, "At this age Jia Yi discussed state affairs—

sentences.zh: 君今徒事儀容，欲何為者？」

translations.literal: You now attend only to appearance—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: you attend only to appearance—what do you intend?

sentences.zh: 又秦孝王妃生男，文帝大喜，頒賜群官各有差。

translations.literal: Also when the consort of Prince Xiao of Qin bore a son, Emperor Wen was greatly pleased and bestowed gifts on the officials each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiao of Qin's consort bore a son, Wen bestowed gifts on officials by rank.

sentences.zh: 文博家道屢空，人謂其悅賞。

translations.literal: Wenbo's household was repeatedly empty; people thought he rejoiced at the reward.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbo's house was empty; people thought he rejoiced at the reward.

sentences.zh: 乃云：「賞罰之設，功過所歸。

translations.literal: He said, "Rewards and punishments exist for merit and fault.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Rewards and punishments follow merit and fault.

sentences.zh: 今王妃生男，于群官何事，乃妄受賞也！」

translations.literal: The consort bore a son—what have the officials to do with it, that they should rashly receive reward!
translations.idiomatic: A consort bore a son—what is that to the officials, that they rashly take reward!

sentences.zh: 其循名責實，錄過計功，必使賞罰不濫，功過無隱皆爾。
