translations.literal: His insisting on names and demanding substance, recording faults and reckoning merit so that reward and punishment were not excessive and merit and fault not hidden—all were like this.
translations.idiomatic: His holding names to deeds and keeping rewards just—all were like this.

sentences.zh: 文博本為經學，後讀史書，于諸子及論，尤所該洽。

translations.literal: Wenbo was originally trained in the Classics; later he read histories and was especially versed in the masters and discourses.
translations.idiomatic: Originally trained in Classics, he later read histories and mastered the masters.

sentences.zh: 性長議論，亦善屬文。

translations.literal: He excelled in discussion and also wrote well.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in debate and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 著《政道集》十卷，大行於世。

translations.literal: He authored the Collection on the Way of Government in ten juan, which circulated widely.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Collection on the Way of Government in ten juan, widely circulated.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，又有魏郡侯白，字君素，好學有捷才，性滑稽，尤辯俊。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang there was also Hou Bai of Wei commandery, courtesy name Junsu, who loved learning and had quick talent; by nature comical, especially clever in debate.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang there was also Hou Bai of Wei commandery, Junsu, learned and quick, comical and sharp in debate.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，為儒林郎。

translations.literal: Recommended as xiucai, he became Gentleman of the Forest of Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as xiucai, he became Gentleman of the Forest of Learning.

sentences.zh: 通侻不持威儀，好為俳諧雜說。

translations.literal: Easygoing, he kept no dignified bearing and loved jesting tales.
translations.idiomatic: Easygoing, without dignified bearing, he loved jesting tales.

sentences.zh: 人多愛狎之，所在處，觀者如市。

translations.literal: Many loved to be familiar with him; wherever he went onlookers crowded like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Many flocked to him; wherever he went crowds gathered.

sentences.zh: 楊素甚狎之。

translations.literal: Yang Su was very familiar with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was very familiar with him.

sentences.zh: 素嘗與牛弘退朝，白謂素曰：「日之夕矣。」

translations.literal: Su once left court with Niu Hong; Bai said to Su, "The sun is setting.
translations.idiomatic: Su once left court with Niu Hong; Bai said, "The sun is setting.

sentences.zh: 素大笑曰：「以我為'牛羊下來'邪！」

translations.literal: Su laughed loudly and said, "Do you take me for 'cattle and sheep come down'!"
translations.idiomatic: Su laughed, "Do you take me for 'the cattle and sheep come down'!"

sentences.zh: 文帝聞其名，召與語，悅之，令于秘書修國史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard his name, summoned and conversed with him, was pleased, and had him compile the national history in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wen heard his name, summoned him, was pleased, and had him compile history in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 每將擢用，輒曰「白不勝官'而止。

translations.literal: Whenever about to promote him he would say "Bai is not equal to office" and stop.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever about to promote him he would say "Bai cannot bear office" and stop.

sentences.zh: 後給五品食，月餘而死。

translations.literal: Later he was given fifth-rank provisions; after a month more he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later given fifth-rank provisions; after a month he died.

sentences.zh: 時人傷其薄命。

translations.literal: People of the time mourned his short fate.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries mourned his short life.

sentences.zh: 著《旌異記》十五卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He authored the Record of Auspicious Wonders in fifteen juan, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Record of Auspicious Wonders in fifteen juan.

sentences.zh: 明克讓，字弘道，平原鬲人也。

translations.literal: Ming Kerang, courtesy name Hongdao, was a man of Ge in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Kerang, courtesy name Hongdao, was a man of Ge in Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 世仕江左。

translations.literal: For generations the family served in Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family served in Jiangzuo.

sentences.zh: 祖僧紹、父山賓，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengshao and father Shanbin both have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengshao and father Shanbin both have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 克讓少儒雅，善談論，博涉書史，所覽將萬卷，《三禮》、《論語》，尤所研精，龜策曆象，咸得其要。

translations.literal: Kerang in youth was refined and elegant, skilled in discussion, read widely in books and histories—nearly ten thousand juan; the Three Rites and Analects he especially mastered, and in tortoise, milfoil, calendar, and astronomy he grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: In youth refined and eloquent, he read ten thousand juan; mastered the Three Rites and Analects and the arts of calendar and divination.

sentences.zh: 年十四，釋褐湘東王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: At fourteen he donned the clerk's robe as Legal Officer to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he became Legal Officer to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 時舍人硃異在儀賢堂講《老子》，克讓預焉。

translations.literal: When Attendant Zhu Yi lectured on the Laozi in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy, Kerang was present.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Yi lectured on the Laozi in the Hall for Honoring the Worthy, Kerang was present.

sentences.zh: 堂邊有修竹，異令克讓詠之。

translations.literal: Beside the hall were tall bamboos; Yi had Kerang compose a poem on them.
translations.idiomatic: Tall bamboos stood beside the hall; Yi had Kerang compose on them.

sentences.zh: 克讓攬筆輒成，卒章曰：「非君多愛賞，誰貴此貞心？」

translations.literal: Kerang took the brush and finished at once; the closing line said, "If not for your many loves and rewards, who would prize this steadfast heart?
translations.idiomatic: He finished at once; the closing line said, "If not for your love and reward, who would prize this steadfast heart?

sentences.zh: 異甚奇之。

translations.literal: Yi greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi greatly marveled.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He served Liang, reaching Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang, reaching Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 梁滅，歸長安，引為麟趾殿學士。

translations.literal: When Liang perished he returned to Chang'an and was brought in as a Unicorn Toe Hall scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang fell he returned to Chang'an as a Unicorn Toe Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 周武帝即位，為露門學士，令與太史官屬正定新曆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou succeeded he became a Dew Gate scholar and was ordered with astronomical officials to fix the new calendar.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Wu succeeded he became a Dew Gate scholar and fixed the new calendar with astronomers.

sentences.zh: 累遷司調大夫，賜爵曆城縣伯。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Master of the Directorate of Tuning and enfeoffed as Baron of Licheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Grand Master of the Directorate of Tuning and made Baron of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，位率更令，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate he became Director of the Directorate of Regulated Measures and advanced to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui took the mandate he became Director of Regulated Measures and advanced to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 太子以師道處之，恩禮甚厚，每有四方珍味，輒以賜之。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince treated him as teacher; favor was very deep, and whenever there were rare delicacies from the four quarters they were given to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince treated him as teacher; rare delicacies from the four quarters were given him.

sentences.zh: 時東宮盛征天下才學士。

translations.literal: At the time the Eastern Palace lavishly recruited talented scholars from the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace lavishly recruited scholars from the realm.

sentences.zh: 至於博物洽聞，皆出其下。

translations.literal: In breadth of learning and comprehensive knowledge, all were below him.
translations.idiomatic: In learning and comprehensive knowledge all were below him.

sentences.zh: 詔與太常牛弘等修禮議樂。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him with Grand Master of Ceremonies Niu Hong and others to revise rites and music.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered with Niu Hong and others to revise rites and music.

sentences.zh: 當朝典故，多所裁正。

translations.literal: Court precedents he often corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He often corrected court precedents.

sentences.zh: 以疾去官，加通直散騎常侍，卒。

translations.literal: He left office on account of illness, was given additional title Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he left office, was given Regular Attendant of the Direct and Unimpeded Cavalry, and died.

sentences.zh: 上甚惜之，二宮贈賻甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly regretted it; the two palaces gave funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted it deeply; both palaces gave generous funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 所著《孝經義疏》一部，《古今帝代記》一卷，《文類》四卷，《續名僧記》一卷，集二十卷。

translations.literal: His works included one juan of Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety, one juan of Record of Emperors Ancient and Modern, four juan of Literary Categories, one juan of Continued Record of Eminent Monks, and collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Works: Exegesis of the Filial Piety Classic, Record of Emperors, Literary Categories, Continued Record of Eminent Monks, and twenty juan of collected works.

sentences.zh: 子余慶，位司門郎。

translations.literal: His son Yuqing held the post of Director of the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuqing was Director of the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 越王侗稱制，為國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yue Tong assumed power, he became Libationer of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yue Tong assumed power, he became National University Libationer.

sentences.zh: 克讓叔少遐，博涉群書，有詞藻。

translations.literal: Kerang's uncle Shaoxia read widely and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang's uncle Shaoxia read widely and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，位都官尚書。

translations.literal: He served Liang as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served Liang as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 入齊，甚為名流王元景、陽休之等所禮。

translations.literal: Entering Qi he was greatly honored by leading figures Wang Yuanjing, Yang Xiuzhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi he was honored by Wang Yuanjing, Yang Xiuzhi, and others.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，拜中庶子。

translations.literal: During Huangjian he was appointed Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: During Huangjian he was appointed Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈中書令、揚州司馬。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Secretariat Director and Yangzhou Major.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously Secretariat Director and Yangzhou Major.

sentences.zh: 劉臻，字宣摯，沛國相人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Xuanzhi, was a man of Xiang in Pei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, courtesy name Xuanzhi, was a man of Xiang in Pei.

sentences.zh: 父顯，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Xian has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 臻年十八，舉秀才，為邵陵王東閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At eighteen Zhen was recommended as xiucai and became Eastern Pavilion Libationer to the Prince of Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was recommended as xiucai and became Eastern Pavilion Libationer to the Prince of Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yuan he became Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 江陵平，歸魏為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Jiangling was pacified he returned to Wei as Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he went to Wei as Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 周塚宰宇文護辟為中外府記室，軍書羽檄，多成其手。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yuwen Hu of Zhou recruited him as recorder of the inner and outer headquarters; military documents and proclamations were mostly in his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Hu recruited him as headquarters recorder; military documents were mostly his.

sentences.zh: 後為露門學士，授大都督，封饒陽縣子。

translations.literal: Later he was a Dew Gate scholar, granted the title Grand Commander, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Raoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Dew Gate scholar, Grand Commander, Viscount of Raoyang.

sentences.zh: 曆藍田令、畿伯下大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Magistrate of Lantian and Junior Grand Master of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: He was Magistrate of Lantian and Junior Grand Master of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進位儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the mandate he advanced to Honored Standing of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui took the mandate he advanced to Honored Standing of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 左僕射高熲之伐陳也，以臻隨軍主文翰，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: When Left Vice Director Gao Jiong campaigned against Chen, Zhen followed the army and directed documents, advancing to Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong campaigned against Chen, Zhen directed documents and advanced to Duke.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇引為學士，甚親狎之。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong brought him in as scholar and was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong brought him in as scholar and was very close to him.

sentences.zh: 臻無吏幹，又性惚怳，耽經覃思。

translations.literal: Zhen had no administrative skill and was by nature absent-minded, absorbed in the Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He had no administrative skill and was absent-minded, absorbed in the Classics.

sentences.zh: 至於世事，多所遺忘。

translations.literal: As for worldly affairs he forgot much.
translations.idiomatic: He forgot much of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 有劉訥者，亦任儀同，俱為太子學士，情好甚密。

translations.literal: There was a Liu Ne who also held Honored Standing; both were Crown Prince scholars and were very close.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ne also held Honored Standing; both were Crown Prince scholars and close friends.

sentences.zh: 臻住城南，訥住城東。

translations.literal: Zhen lived in the south of the city; Ne lived in the east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen lived south of the city; Ne lived east.

sentences.zh: 臻嘗欲尋訥，謂從者曰：「汝知劉儀同家乎？」

translations.literal: Zhen once wished to visit Ne and said to his attendants, "Do you know Liu Honored Standing's house?
translations.idiomatic: Zhen wished to visit Ne and asked attendants, "Do you know Liu Honored Standing's house?

sentences.zh: 從者不知尋訥，謂臻還家，因答曰：「知。」

translations.literal: The attendants, not knowing he sought Ne, thought Zhen was returning home and answered, "We know."
translations.idiomatic: Attendants thought he was going home and said, "We know."

sentences.zh: 於是引之而去。

translations.literal: They therefore led him away.
translations.idiomatic: They led him away.

sentences.zh: 既扣門，臻尚未悟，謂至訥家，乃據鞍大呼曰：「劉儀同可出矣。」

translations.literal: Having knocked at the gate, Zhen had not yet realized and, thinking he had reached Ne's house, leaned on the saddle and shouted, "Liu Honored Standing, come out!
translations.idiomatic: At the gate he thought it was Ne's house and shouted, "Liu Honored Standing, come out!

sentences.zh: 其子迎門，臻驚曰：「汝亦來邪？」

translations.literal: His son met him at the door; Zhen was startled and said, "Have you come too?"
translations.idiomatic: His son met him; Zhen said, "Have you come too?"

sentences.zh: 其子答曰：「此是大人家。」

translations.literal: His son answered, "This is our great house."
translations.idiomatic: His son said, "This is our house."

sentences.zh: 於是顧眄久之，乃悟，叱從者：「汝大無意，吾欲造劉訥耳！」

translations.literal: He then looked about a long time before understanding, and scolded the attendants: "You are utterly thoughtless—I wished to visit Liu Ne!"
translations.idiomatic: He looked about, understood, and scolded the attendants: "I meant to visit Liu Ne!"

sentences.zh: 性好啖蜆，以音同父諱，呼為扁螺，其疏放多此類也。

translations.literal: By nature he loved to eat clams; because the sound matched his father's taboo name he called them "flat snails"; his heedlessness was often of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He loved clams; because the sound matched his father's taboo he called them "flat snails"—such was his heedlessness.

sentences.zh: 精於兩《漢書》，時人稱為《漢》聖。

translations.literal: He was expert in both Books of Han and people of the time called him "Sage of the Han."
translations.idiomatic: Expert in both Books of Han, he was called "Sage of the Han."

sentences.zh: 開皇十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Kaihuang he died.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year eighteen he died.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in ten juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in ten juan circulated.

sentences.zh: 諸葛潁，字漢，丹楊建康人也。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ying, courtesy name Han, was a man of Jianye in Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ying, courtesy name Han, was a man of Jianye in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 祖銓，梁零陵太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was Administrator of Lingling in Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan was Liang's Administrator of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 父規，義陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Gui was Administrator of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was Administrator of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 潁年十八能屬文，起家邵陵王參軍事，轉記室。

translations.literal: At eighteen Ying could compose prose; he began as staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling and was transferred to recorder.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he could write; he served the Prince of Shaoling and became recorder.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，奔齊，曆學士、太子舍人。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Qi and successively served as scholar and Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Qi as scholar and Crown Prince Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周氏平齊，不得調，杜門不出者十餘年。

translations.literal: When Zhou pacified Qi he received no appointment and shut his door for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou pacified Qi he received no post and shut his door ten years.

sentences.zh: 習《易》、《圖緯》、《蒼》《雅》、《莊》《老》頗得其要，清辯有俊才。

translations.literal: He studied the Changes, charts and apocrypha, Cangjie glossary, Zhuangzi and Laozi, and grasped their essentials; clear in debate and with outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Changes, apocrypha, glossaries, Zhuangzi and Laozi; clear in debate and talented.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣素聞其名，引為參軍事，轉記室。

translations.literal: Prince Jin Guang had long heard his name and brought him in as staff officer, then recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang had heard of him and made him staff officer and recorder.

sentences.zh: 及王為太子，除藥藏郎。

translations.literal: When the prince became Crown Prince he was made Keeper of the Medicine Store.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became Crown Prince he was Keeper of the Medicine Store.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遷著作郎，甚見親幸，出入臥內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he was transferred to Drafting Historian, greatly favored, entering and leaving the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang succeeded he was Drafting Historian, favored in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 帝每賜之曲宴，輒與皇后嬪御連席共榻。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor gave him private banquets he shared couch and mat with the empress and consorts.
translations.idiomatic: At private banquets he shared couch and mat with empress and consorts.

sentences.zh: 潁因間隙，多所譖毀，是以時人謂之「冶葛」。

translations.literal: Ying used openings to slander many; therefore people of the time called him "refining poison."
translations.idiomatic: He used openings to slander many; people called him "refining poison."

sentences.zh: 後錄恩舊，授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Later, recording old favor, he was made Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for old favor, he was made Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜潁詩，其卒章曰：「參翰長洲苑，侍講肅成門，名理窮研核，英華恣討論。

translations.literal: The emperor once gave Ying a poem; its closing lines said, "Joining drafts at Changqiu garden, lecturing at the Suicheng gate, exhausting principle in research, letting brilliance roam in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him a poem ending: "Joining drafts at Changqiu, lecturing at Suicheng, exhausting principle, letting brilliance roam.

sentences.zh: 實錄資平允，傳芳導後昆。」

translations.literal: True records rely on fairness; transmitting fragrance guides later generations.
translations.idiomatic: True records rely on fairness; transmitting fragrance guides posterity.

sentences.zh: 其待遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was his treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his treatment.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，加正議大夫。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Tuyuhun he was given additional title Grand Master for Correct Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he was made Grand Master for Correct Discussion.

sentences.zh: 從駕北巡，卒於道。

translations.literal: Following the northern tour he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: On the northern tour he died on the road.

sentences.zh: 潁性褊急，與柳{巧言}每相忿鬩。

translations.literal: Ying was impatient by nature and constantly quarreled with Liu Guyan.
translations.idiomatic: Impatient by nature, he constantly quarreled with Liu Guyan.

sentences.zh: 帝屢責怒之，而猶不止。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly rebuked and raged at him, yet he still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly rebuked him, yet he did not stop.

sentences.zh: 于後帝亦薄之。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor also thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the emperor also cooled toward him.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷，撰《鑾駕北巡記》三卷，《幸江都道里記》一卷，《洛陽古今記》一卷，《馬名錄》二卷，並行於世。

translations.literal: He left collected works in twenty juan and compiled the Record of the Imperial Carriage's Northern Tour in three juan, Record of the Road to Jiangdu in one juan, Record of Luoyang Ancient and Modern in one juan, and Register of Horse Names in two juan—all circulated.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty juan of works plus records of the northern tour, the Jiangdu road, Luoyang, and horse names—all circulated.

sentences.zh: 有子嘉會。

translations.literal: He had a son Jiahui.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son Jiahui.

sentences.zh: 虞綽，字士裕，會稽餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chuo, courtesy name Shiyu, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chuo, courtesy name Shiyu, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 父孝曾，陳始興王諮議。

translations.literal: His father Xiaoceng was adviser to the Prince of Shixing of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiaoceng was adviser to Chen's Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 綽身長八尺，姿儀甚偉，博學有俊才，尤工草隸。

translations.literal: Chuo stood eight chi, with very fine bearing; broadly learned with outstanding talent, especially skilled in cursive and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo stood eight chi, fine in bearing; learned and talented, skilled in cursive and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 陳左衛將軍傅縡，有盛名於世，見綽詞賦，歎美之。

translations.literal: Fu Zai, General of the Left Guard of Chen, was famed in the world; seeing Chuo's rhapsodies and fu he sighed in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai of Chen was famed; seeing Chuo's fu he praised him.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，為太學博士，遷永陽王記室。

translations.literal: He served Chen as Doctor of the National University and was transferred to recorder to the Prince of Yongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served Chen as National University Doctor and recorder to the Prince of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，晉王廣引為學士。

translations.literal: When Chen perished Prince Jin Guang brought him in as scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell Prince Guang brought him in as scholar.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉為秘書學士，奉詔與秘書郎虞世南，著作佐郎庾自直等撰《長洲玉鏡》等書十餘部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he became Secretariat Scholar and was ordered with Secretariat Gentleman Yu Shinan, Drafting Historian Yu Zizhi, and others to compile more than ten works such as the Jade Mirror of Changqiu.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's start he became Secretariat Scholar and compiled works such as the Jade Mirror of Changqiu with Yu Shinan and Yu Zizhi.

sentences.zh: 綽所筆削，帝未嘗不稱善，而官竟不遷。

translations.literal: Whatever Chuo edited the emperor never failed to praise, yet his office was never promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever Chuo edited the emperor praised, yet he was never promoted.

sentences.zh: 初為校書郎，以籓邸左右，授宣惠尉，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At first he was Collator; as a companion in the prince's mansion he was made Captain for Promoting Grace and transferred to Drafting Historian.
translations.idiomatic: First Collator, then Captain for Promoting Grace, then Drafting Historian in the prince's household.

sentences.zh: 與虞世南、庾自直、蔡允恭等四人常直禁中，以文翰待詔，恩眄隆洽。

translations.literal: With Yu Shinan, Yu Zizhi, and Cai Yungong—four men—he constantly attended within the forbidden precincts as literary awaiting-edict; favor was thick.
translations.idiomatic: With Yu Shinan, Yu Zizhi, and Cai Yungong he constantly awaited edicts within the palace; favor was thick.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，帝舍臨海，頻見大鳥，異之，詔綽為銘。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign the emperor halted at Linhai; great birds were repeatedly seen and he was amazed; he ordered Chuo to compose an inscription.
translations.idiomatic: At Linhai on the Liaodong campaign great birds appeared; the emperor ordered Chuo to compose an inscription.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而善之，命有司勒於海上。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved; he ordered the relevant office to carve it on the seashore.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and ordered it carved on the seashore.

sentences.zh: 以度遼功，授建節尉。

translations.literal: For merit in crossing Liao he was made Captain for Establishing the Command.
translations.idiomatic: For merit crossing Liao he was made Captain for Establishing the Command.

sentences.zh: 綽恃才任氣，無所降下。

translations.literal: Chuo relied on talent and temperament and bowed to no one.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo relied on talent and bowed to no one.

sentences.zh: 著作郎諸葛潁以學業幸於帝，綽每輕侮之，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Drafting Historian Zhuge Ying was favored by the emperor for learning; Chuo often slighted and insulted him, and therefore there was enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ying was favored for learning; Chuo slighted him and they became enemies.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問綽於潁，潁曰：「虞綽粗疏人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Ying about Chuo; Ying said, "Yu Chuo is a coarse and careless man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Ying about Chuo; Ying said, "Yu Chuo is coarse and careless.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 時禮部尚書楊玄感稱其貴踞，虛己禮之，與結布衣之友。

translations.literal: At the time Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan praised his lofty manner and with empty courtesy treated him, becoming friends as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan treated him with empty courtesy and became his friend.

sentences.zh: 綽數從之遊。

translations.literal: Chuo often went about with him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo often visited him.

sentences.zh: 其族人虞世南誡之曰：「上性猜忌，而君過厚玄感。

translations.literal: His clansman Yu Shinan admonished him, saying, "The emperor is suspicious by nature, yet you are too close to Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan admonished him: "The emperor is suspicious, yet you are too close to Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 若與絕交者，帝知君改悔，可以無咎。

translations.literal: If you break with him the emperor will know you have repented and you may escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Break with him and the emperor may spare you.

sentences.zh: 不然終當見禍。」

translations.literal: Otherwise you will surely meet disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise disaster will come.

sentences.zh: 綽不從。

translations.literal: Chuo did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo did not listen.

sentences.zh: 尋有告綽以禁內兵書借玄感，帝甚銜之。

translations.literal: Soon someone reported that Chuo had lent forbidden military books within the palace to Xuanzhi; the emperor deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone reported Chuo lent forbidden military books to Xuanzhi; the emperor resented it.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，其妓妾併入宮，帝因問之曰：「玄感平常時與何人交往？」

translations.literal: When Xuanzhi failed, his singing girls and concubines all entered the palace; the emperor therefore asked them, "With whom did Xuanzhi usually associate?
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzhi failed his concubines entered the palace; the emperor asked whom he associated with.

sentences.zh: 其妾以虞綽對。

translations.literal: A concubine named Yu Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: A concubine named Yu Chuo.

sentences.zh: 帝令大理卿鄭善果窮理其事。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo to investigate fully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Zheng Shanguo of the Ministry of Justice to investigate.

sentences.zh: 綽曰：「羈旅薄游，與玄感文酒談款，實無他謀。」

translations.literal: Chuo said, "A traveler in a thin land, with Xuanzhi I shared literary wine and friendly talk—truly no other plot.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo said, "A sojourner; with Xuanzhi I shared wine and talk—no other plot.

sentences.zh: 帝怒不解，徙綽于邊。

translations.literal: The emperor's anger was not appeased; Chuo was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was not appeased; Chuo was banished.

sentences.zh: 綽至長安而亡。

translations.literal: Chuo reached Chang'an and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo reached Chang'an and fled.

sentences.zh: 吏逮之急，於是潛度江，變姓名，自稱吳卓。

translations.literal: Officers pursued urgently; he thereupon secretly crossed the river, changed his name, and called himself Wu Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Pursued hotly, he crossed the river, changed his name to Wu Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 游東陽，抵信安令天水辛大德舍。

translations.literal: Wandering in Dongyang he came to the house of Xin Dade, Magistrate of Xin'an in Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In Dongyang he came to Magistrate Xin Dade of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，綽與人爭田相訟，因有識綽者而告之，竟為吏所執，坐斬江都。

translations.literal: After more than a year Chuo disputed fields in a lawsuit with someone; because someone recognized Chuo he was reported, was seized by officers, and was executed at Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: After a year Chuo disputed land in court; recognized, seized, and executed at Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 所有詞賦，並行於世。

translations.literal: All his rhapsodies and fu circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: All his rhapsodies and fu circulated.

sentences.zh: 大德為令，誅翦群盜，甚得人和。

translations.literal: Dade as magistrate executed and cut down bandits and was very harmonious with the people.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate Dade suppressed bandits and won the people.

sentences.zh: 與綽俱為使者所執，其妻泣曰：「每諫君無匿學士。

translations.literal: Seized together with Chuo, his wife wept and said, "I always admonished you not to harbor scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Seized with Chuo, his wife wept, "I always told you not to harbor scholars.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，豈不哀哉！」

translations.literal: Today's affair—is it not pitiful!
translations.idiomatic: Today—is it not pitiful!

sentences.zh: 大德笑曰：「我本圖脫長者，乃為人告之，吾罪也，當死以謝綽。」

translations.literal: Dade laughed and said, "I originally meant to free the elder; being reported is my fault—I should die to answer for Chuo."
translations.idiomatic: Dade laughed, "I meant to free him; being reported is my fault—I should die for Chuo."

sentences.zh: 會有詔，死罪得以擊賊自效。

translations.literal: There happened to be an edict that death sentences might be redeemed by striking bandits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed death sentences to be redeemed by fighting bandits.

sentences.zh: 信安吏人詣使者叩頭曰：「辛君人命所懸，不然亦無信安矣。」

translations.literal: The clerks and people of Xin'an kowtowed to the envoy and said, "Magistrate Xin's life hangs in the balance; otherwise there will be no Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an people kowtowed to the envoy: "Magistrate Xin's life is our life.

sentences.zh: 使者留之以討賊。

translations.literal: The envoy kept him to attack bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy kept him to fight bandits.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，斬使者。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and executed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor executed the envoy in anger.

sentences.zh: 大德獲全。

translations.literal: Dade was completely spared.
translations.idiomatic: Dade was spared.

sentences.zh: 王胄，字承基，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhou, courtesy name Chengji, was a man of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhou, courtesy name Chengji, was a man of Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 祖筠、父祥，並《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Jun and father Xiang both have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Jun and father Xiang both have biographies in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 胄少有逸才，仕陳，曆太子舍人、東陽王文學。

translations.literal: Zhou in youth had outstanding talent; he served Chen, successively as Crown Prince Attendant and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In youth talented; in Chen he was Crown Prince Attendant and Literary Scholar to the Prince of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，晉王廣引為博士。

translations.literal: When Chen perished Prince Jin Guang brought him in as Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell Prince Guang made him Doctor.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，從劉方擊林邑，以功授帥都督。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou he followed Liu Fang against Lin Yi and for merit was made Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou's end he followed Liu Fang against Lin Yi and became Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為著作佐郎，以文詞為煬帝所重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was Drafting Historian; his literary style was greatly valued by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's start he was Drafting Historian, valued by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗自東都還京師，賜天下大酺四日。

translations.literal: The emperor once returned from the Eastern Capital to the capital and granted a great feast to the realm for four days.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned from the Eastern Capital and granted a four-day feast to the realm.

sentences.zh: 為五言詩，詔群官詩成者奏之。

translations.literal: He composed pentasyllabic verse and ordered officials whose poems were finished to present them.
translations.idiomatic: He composed pentasyllabic verse and ordered finished poems presented.

sentences.zh: 帝覽胄詩而善之，因謂侍臣曰：「氣高致遠，歸之於胄；

translations.literal: The emperor read Zhou's poem and approved; he therefore said to attendants, "Lofty spirit and far-reaching tone belong to Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Reading Zhou's poem, he told attendants, "Lofty spirit belongs to Zhou;

sentences.zh: 詞清體潤，其在世基；

translations.literal: clear diction and polished style belong to Shiji;
translations.idiomatic: clear style to Shiji;

sentences.zh: 意密理新，惟庾自直。

translations.literal: dense thought and fresh principle belong to Yu Zizhi alone.
translations.idiomatic: dense thought and fresh principle to Yu Zizhi alone.

sentences.zh: 過此者未可以言詩也。」

translations.literal: Beyond these one cannot speak of poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond these one cannot speak of poetry.

sentences.zh: 帝所有篇什，多令繼和。

translations.literal: Whatever the emperor composed he often ordered Zhou to harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the emperor wrote he often had Zhou harmonize.

sentences.zh: 與虞綽齊名，同志友善，于時後進之士，咸以二人為准的。

translations.literal: He was famed equal to Yu Chuo, like-minded and friendly; younger writers of the time all took the two as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: Equal in fame to Yu Chuo; younger writers took both as standard.

sentences.zh: 從征遼東，進授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master for Dispersed Affairs.

sentences.zh: 胄性疏率不倫，自恃才伐，鬱鬱於官。

translations.literal: Zhou was by nature careless and unrestrained, relying on talent and arrogant, depressed in office.
translations.idiomatic: Careless and unrestrained, arrogant in talent, depressed in office.

sentences.zh: 每負氣陵傲，忽略時人。

translations.literal: He often bore his spirit high and overlooked people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He often looked down on contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 為諸葛潁所嫉，屢譖之於帝，帝愛其才而不罪。

translations.literal: Zhuge Ying envied him and repeatedly slandered him to the emperor; the emperor loved his talent and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ying envied and slandered him; the emperor loved his talent and spared him.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書楊玄感虛襟與交，數遊其第。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Yang Xuangan with open mind befriended him and often visited his house.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan befriended him and often visited.

sentences.zh: 及玄感敗，與虞綽徙邊。

translations.literal: When Xuanzhi failed he was banished with Yu Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzhi failed he was banished with Yu Chuo.

sentences.zh: 胄遂亡匿，潛還江左。

translations.literal: Zhou then fled into hiding and secretly returned to Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou fled and secretly returned to Jiangzuo.

sentences.zh: 為吏所捕，坐誅。

translations.literal: He was seized by officers and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Officers seized him and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 所著詞賦，多行於世。

translations.literal: His rhapsodies and fu mostly circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His rhapsodies and fu mostly circulated.

sentences.zh: 庾自直，潁川人。

translations.literal: Yu Zizhi was a man of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zizhi was a man of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 父持，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Chi has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chi has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 少好學，沈靜寡欲。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; quiet and with few desires.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning; quiet and with few desires.

sentences.zh: 仕陳，曆豫章王府外兵參軍、記室。

translations.literal: He served Chen, successively as External Military Attendant and recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen he was External Military Attendant and recorder to the Prince of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入關，不得調。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered the pass and received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell he entered the pass and received no post.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣聞之，引為學士。

translations.literal: Prince Jin Guang heard of him and brought him in as scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Guang brought him in as scholar.

sentences.zh: 大業初，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was appointed Drafting Historian.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye's start he was Drafting Historian.

sentences.zh: 自直解屬文，于五言詩尤善。

translations.literal: Zizhi could compose prose and was especially skilled in pentasyllabic poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi wrote prose and excelled at pentasyllabic poetry.

sentences.zh: 性恭慎，不妄交遊。

translations.literal: By nature respectful and cautious, he did not casually associate.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and cautious, he did not casually associate.

sentences.zh: 特為帝所愛，有篇章必先示自直，令其詆訶。

translations.literal: He was especially loved by the emperor; whenever there was a piece it was first shown to Zizhi for him to criticize.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor especially loved him; new pieces went first to Zizhi for criticism.

sentences.zh: 自直所難，帝輒改之。

translations.literal: What Zizhi found difficult the emperor would revise.
translations.idiomatic: What Zizhi criticized the emperor revised.

sentences.zh: 或至於再三，俟其稱善，然後方出。

translations.literal: Sometimes two or three times—only when he praised it would it then be released.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes two or three revisions—only when Zizhi praised it was it released.

sentences.zh: 其見親禮如此。

translations.literal: Such was the intimate treatment he received.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his treatment.

sentences.zh: 後以本官知起居舍人事。

translations.literal: Later in his former office he also managed the duties of Diarist of the Imperial Progress.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also managed the Diarist of the Imperial Progress.

sentences.zh: 化及作逆，與之北上，自載露車中，感激發病卒。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled he went north with him; he loaded himself in an open cart, was moved and fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji rebelled he went north in an open cart, fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He left collected works in ten juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Collected works in ten juan circulated.

sentences.zh: 潘徽，字伯彥，吳郡人也。

translations.literal: Pan Hui, courtesy name Boyan, was a man of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Hui, courtesy name Boyan, was a man of Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 性聰敏，少受《禮》于鄭灼，受《毛詩》于施公，受《書》于張沖，講《莊》、《老》于張譏，並通大義。

translations.literal: Intelligent by nature; in youth he received the Rites from Zheng Zhuo, the Mao Odes from Master Shi, the Documents from Zhang Chong, and lectured on Zhuangzi and Laozi with Zhang Ji—all grasping the great meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent; studied Rites, Mao Odes, Documents, Zhuangzi and Laozi with masters.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三史》。

translations.literal: He was especially expert in the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: Especially expert in the Three Histories.

sentences.zh: 善屬文，能持論。

translations.literal: Skilled at composing prose and able to sustain debate.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at prose and debate.

sentences.zh: 中書令江總引致文儒之士，徽一詣總，甚敬之。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Jiang Zong introduced literary scholars; Hui visited Zong once and was greatly respected.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong introduced scholars; Hui visited once and was greatly respected.

sentences.zh: 釋褐新蔡王國侍郎，選為客館令。

translations.literal: He first served as Gentleman of the Principality of Xincai and was selected as Director of the Guest Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: First Gentleman of Xincai, then Director of the Guest Lodge.

sentences.zh: 隋遣魏澹聘于陳，陳人使徽接對之。

translations.literal: Sui sent Wei Dan on embassy to Chen; Chen had Hui receive and reply to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui sent Wei Dan to Chen; Chen had Hui receive him.

sentences.zh: 澹將反命，為啟于陳主曰：「敬奉弘慈，曲垂餞送。」

translations.literal: When Dan was about to return with his mission he composed a note to the Chen ruler saying, "Respectfully receiving great kindness, graciously granted a send-off.
translations.idiomatic: Dan's note to the Chen ruler said, "Respectfully receiving kindness, graciously granted send-off.

sentences.zh: 徽以餞送為重，敬奉為輕，卻其啟而不奏。

translations.literal: Hui held send-off as weighty and respectful reception as light; he returned the note and did not memorialize it.
translations.idiomatic: Hui held send-off weighty and respectful reception light; he returned the note unread.

sentences.zh: 澹曰：「《曲禮》云：主敬客。

translations.literal: Dan said, "The Record of Rites says: the host respects the guest.
translations.idiomatic: Dan cited the Record of Rites: the host respects the guest.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：'維桑與梓，必恭敬止'。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'Mulberry and catalpa—reverence must stop.'
translations.idiomatic: The Odes: mulberry and catalpa—reverence must stop.

sentences.zh: 《孝經》：'宗廟致敬。

translations.literal: The Classic of Filial Piety: 'In the ancestral temple show reverence.'
translations.idiomatic: Filial Piety: in the ancestral temple show reverence.

sentences.zh: '又云：'不敬其親，謂之悖禮。

translations.literal: It also says: 'Not revering one's kin is called contrary ritual.'
translations.idiomatic: Also: not revering kin is contrary ritual.

sentences.zh: '孔子敬天之怒，成湯聖敬日躋。

translations.literal: Confucius revered heaven's anger; Cheng Tang's sage reverence daily ascended.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius revered heaven's anger; Cheng Tang's reverence daily ascended.

sentences.zh: 宗廟極重，上天極高，父極尊，君極貴，四者咸同一敬，《五經》未有異文。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple is supremely weighty, heaven supremely high, father supremely honored, ruler supremely noble—the four alike share one reverence; the Five Classics have no differing text.
translations.idiomatic: Temple, heaven, father, ruler—all one reverence; the Five Classics agree.

sentences.zh: 不知以敬為輕，竟何所據？」

translations.literal: I do not know on what basis reverence is taken as light—what is your evidence?
translations.idiomatic: On what basis is reverence light—what is your evidence?

sentences.zh: 徽難之曰：「向所論敬字，本不全以為輕，但施用處殊，義成通別。

translations.literal: Hui rebutted him, saying, "In the discussion just now on the word reverence, it was not entirely held to be light, but application differs and meaning becomes generally distinct.
translations.idiomatic: Hui rebutted: reverence is not wholly light, but usage differs.

sentences.zh: 禮主於敬，此是通言。

translations.literal: Rites chiefly rest on reverence—this is the general saying.
translations.idiomatic: Rites chiefly rest on reverence—the general saying.

sentences.zh: 猶如男子冠而字之，注云：'成人，敬其名也。

translations.literal: It is like when a man is capped and given a style; the commentary says: 'As an adult, reverence for his name.'
translations.idiomatic: As when a man is capped: as an adult, reverence for his name.

sentences.zh: '《春秋》有冀缺，夫妻亦云相敬。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals has Ji Que; husband and wife also say mutual reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn has Ji Que; husband and wife speak mutual reverence.

sentences.zh: 於子則有敬名之義，在夫亦有敬妻之說，此可復並謂極高極尊乎？

translations.literal: For a son there is the meaning of revering the name; for a husband there is also the saying of revering the wife—can these again all be called supremely high and supremely noble?
translations.idiomatic: Sons revere names; husbands revere wives—are these all supremely noble?

sentences.zh: 至若敬謝諸公，固非尊地；

translations.literal: As for reverent thanks to the lords, that is certainly not a place of honor;
translations.idiomatic: Reverent thanks to lords is not a place of honor;

sentences.zh: 公子敬愛，止施賓友；

translations.literal: a prince's reverent love extends only to guests and friends;
translations.idiomatic: a prince's reverent love is for guests and friends;

sentences.zh: 敬問敬報，彌見雷同；

translations.literal: reverent inquiry and reverent reply appear ever more identical;
translations.idiomatic: reverent inquiry and reply appear identical;

sentences.zh: 敬聽敬酬，何關貴隔。

translations.literal: reverent listening and reverent response—what has it to do with noble rank?
translations.idiomatic: reverent listening and response—what has it to do with rank?

sentences.zh: 當知敬之為義，雖是不輕，但敬之於語，則有時混漫。

translations.literal: One should know that the meaning of reverence, though not light, in language is sometimes diffuse.
translations.idiomatic: Reverence is not light, but in language sometimes diffuse.

sentences.zh: 今雲敬奉，所以成疑。

translations.literal: Now to say 'respectfully receiving' is therefore what raises doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Now 'respectfully receiving' raises doubt.

sentences.zh: 聊舉一隅，未為深據。」

translations.literal: I have offered one corner—it is not deep evidence.
translations.idiomatic: One corner offered—not deep evidence.

sentences.zh: 澹不能對，遂從而改焉。

translations.literal: Dan could not reply and thereupon changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Dan could not reply and changed it.

sentences.zh: 隋時有常得志、尹式、劉善經、祖君彥、孔德紹、劉斌，並有才名，事多遺逸。

translations.literal: In Sui there were Chang Dezhi, Yin Shi, Liu Shanjing, Zu Junyan, Kong Deshao, and Liu Bin—all had literary fame; their affairs are mostly lost.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui were Chang Dezhi, Yin Shi, Liu Shanjing, Zu Junyan, Kong Deshao, and Liu Bin—famed writers mostly lost to record.

sentences.zh: 尹式，河間人。

translations.literal: Yin Shi was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Shi was a man of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，官至漢王記室。

translations.literal: During Renshou he reached the post of Recorder to the Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou he was Recorder to the Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 漢王阻兵，式自殺。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Han obstructed the army Shi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Han rebelled Shi killed himself.

sentences.zh: 其族人正卿、彥卿亦俱有俊才，名顯於世。

translations.literal: His clansmen Zhengqing and Yanqing also both had outstanding talent and names displayed in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen Zhengqing and Yanqing also had outstanding talent.

sentences.zh: 劉善經，河間人。

translations.literal: Liu Shanjing was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shanjing was a man of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 曆著作佐郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: He successively served as Drafting Historian and Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Drafting Historian and Crown Prince Attendant.

sentences.zh: 著《酬德傳》三十卷，《諸劉譜》三十卷，《四聲指歸》一卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He authored thirty juan of the Record of Repaying Virtue, thirty juan of the Genealogy of the Liu Clan, and one juan of Guide to the Four Tones—all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He authored Record of Repaying Virtue, Genealogy of the Liu Clan, and Guide to the Four Tones.

sentences.zh: 祖君彥，見其父珽傳。

translations.literal: Zu Junyan—see his father Ting's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Junyan—see his father Ting's biography.

sentences.zh: 孔德紹，會稽人。

translations.literal: Kong Deshao was a man of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Deshao was a man of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 有清才，官至京城縣丞。

translations.literal: He had pure talent and reached the post of Assistant Magistrate of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Pure talent; Assistant Magistrate of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 竇建德署為中書令，專典書檄。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande appointed him Secretariat Director, in sole charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande made him Secretariat Director in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，伏誅。

translations.literal: When Jiande failed he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande failed he was executed.

sentences.zh: 劉斌，南陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Bin was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bin was a man of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖之遴，《南史》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhitui has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhitui has a biography in the History of the Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 斌頗有詞藻，官至信都司功書佐。

translations.literal: Bin had considerable literary talent and reached the post of Secretary in the Merit Office of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had literary talent and was Secretary in the Merit Office of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 竇建德署為中書舍人。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande appointed him Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande appointed him Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，復為劉黑闥中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When Jiande failed he again became Drafting Attendant to Liu Heitong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande failed he served Liu Heitong as Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與黑闥亡歸突厥，不知所終。

translations.literal: Fleeing with Heitong he returned to the Turks; his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing with Heitong to the Turks, his end is unknown.

sentences.zh: 論曰：古人之所貴名不朽者，蓋重言之尚存。

translations.literal: The discourse says: What the ancients prized in an undying name was chiefly that words remain.
translations.idiomatic: The discourse says: ancients prized undying name because words remain.

sentences.zh: 王褒、庾信、顏之推、虞世基、柳{巧言}、許善心、明克讓、劉臻、王貞、虞綽、王胄等，並極南土譽望，又加之以才名，其為貴顯，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Wang Bao, Yu Xin, Yan Zhitui, Yu Shiji, Liu Guyan, Xu Shanxin, Ming Kerang, Liu Zhen, Wang Zhen, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, and the rest all had the highest southern reputation, and with literary fame added, their being honored and eminent was surely fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao, Yu Xin, Yan Zhitui, Yu Shiji, Liu Guyan, Xu Shanxin, Ming Kerang, Liu Zhen, Wang Zhen, Yu Chuo, Wang Zhou, and the rest had the highest southern fame; with talent added, eminence was fitting.

sentences.zh: 自餘或位下人微，居常亦何能自達。

translations.literal: As for the rest, some were low in rank and slight in person; in ordinary life how could they make themselves known?
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest, some were low in rank and obscure; in ordinary life how could they make themselves known?

sentences.zh: 及其靈蛇可握，天綱俱頓，並編緗素，咸貫辭林。

translations.literal: But when the numinous serpent could be grasped and the celestial net was altogether cast down, all were compiled on silk and plain, all penetrating the forest of letters.
translations.idiomatic: But when their moment came and fortune turned, all were written into books and entered the canon of letters.

sentences.zh: 雖其位可下，其身可殺，千載之外，貴賤一焉。

translations.literal: Though their rank could be lowered and their persons could be killed, beyond a thousand years noble and base are one.
translations.idiomatic: Though rank could be stripped and life taken, a thousand years hence noble and base are alike.

sentences.zh: 非此道也，孰云能致？

translations.literal: Without this Way, who could say it can be attained?
translations.idiomatic: Without this path, who could attain it?

sentences.zh: 凡百士子，可不務乎！

translations.literal: All gentlemen—should they not pursue it!
translations.idiomatic: Should not every scholar pursue it!
